findings.claim: The Content Posting API has two posting modes with separate scopes: Direct Post (publishes straight to the profile) uses scope video.publish; Upload (sends a draft to the creator's TikTok inbox) uses scope video.upload.
findings.evidence: Scopes Reference: video.publish is "Directly post content to a user's TikTok profile"; video.upload is for sending content to a user's account as a draft. Direct Post init endpoint: POST /v2/post/publish/video/init/ (scope video.publish). Upload init endpoint: POST /v2/post/publish/inbox/video/init/ (scope video.upload); after upload "users then get an inbox notification and finish the post in TikTok's editing flow" and "Users must click the inbox notification to continue the editing flow and complete the post."

findings.claim: Direct Post requires the app to be approved for video.publish AND each user to have authorized that scope; the Direct Post configuration must be enabled on the Content Posting API product in the app.
findings.evidence: Get Started - Direct Post: "Your app must be approved for the video.publish scope. The target TikTok user must have authorized your app for the video.publish scope." and "To enable the direct posting of content on authorized users' profiles, you need to enable the Direct Post configuration for the Content Posting API in your app."

findings.claim: Unaudited API clients can only post privately: content is forced to private/SELF_ONLY, the posting account must itself be private at posting time, and at most 5 users may post per 24 hours. Only passing TikTok's audit lifts this.
findings.evidence: Content Sharing Guidelines: "Unaudited API Clients can allow up to 5 users to post in a 24 hour window." / "All user accounts using the API client to post must be set to private at the time of posting." / "Unaudited API Clients can only post contents in SELF_ONLY viewership. To make the contents publicly viewable later on, the account owner must first change their account visibility to public, and then change the privacy settings of each content to 'Everyone.'" Get Started: "All content posted by unaudited clients will be restricted to private viewing mode. Once you have successfully tested your integration, to lift the restrictions on content visibility, your API client must undergo an audit to verify compliance with our Terms of Service." Direct Post reference lists 403 unaudited_client_can_only_post_to_private_accounts (publish attempt blocked at /publish/video/init/).

findings.claim: TikTok's Content Sharing Guidelines explicitly state that an app built only to upload to accounts the developer or their own team manages is NOT an acceptable use case for the audit; apps must be intended for a wide audience, not internal/private use.
findings.evidence: Content Sharing Guidelines (as surfaced by search): apps "should not be limited to test applications and should be intended for a wide audience, not limited to internal groups/private use"; listed as not acceptable: "A utility tool to help upload contents to the account(s) you or your team manages." This directly describes Studio Assistant's private single-business use case.

findings.claim: Daily posting ceilings: Direct Post is capped per creator at roughly 15 posts/day shared across all API clients; Upload mode allows at most 5 pending (unfinished) inbox shares per 24 hours; init endpoints are limited to 6 requests/minute per user access token; creator_info query is 20 requests/minute.
findings.evidence: Content Sharing Guidelines: "The upper limit may vary among creators (typically around 15 posts per day/ creator account) and is shared across all API Clients using Direct Post." Upload reference: TikTok limits API-uploaded videos not yet approved and posted by the creator, "at most 5 pending shares in any 24-hour period"; "Each user access token is limited to 6 requests per minute." Query Creator Info: "each user access token is limited to 20 requests per minute"; error codes spam_risk_too_many_posts and spam_risk_user_banned_from_posting exist.

findings.claim: Direct Post UX is tightly prescribed: fetch fresh creator info when rendering the post page, show the creator nickname, privacy must be chosen manually from the creator's returned options with no default, interaction toggles unchecked/greyed when disabled, commercial-content toggles, Music Usage Confirmation declaration, duration check, and explicit consent before any bytes are sent.
findings.evidence: Guidelines/creator-info docs: "API clients must fetch the latest creator info when rendering the Post to TikTok page"; must display the creator's nickname "so users are aware of which TikTok account the content will be uploaded to"; "Users must manually select the privacy status from a dropdown with no default value"; "Disabled interactions must be greyed out ... none checked by default"; privacy_level must "match one of the privacy_level_options returned in the /creator_info/query/ API" else 403 privacy_level_option_mismatch; "API clients must check that the duration of the to-be-posted video follows the max_video_post_duration_sec returned in the creator_info API"; "API Clients must only start sending content materials to TikTok after the user has expressly consent to the upload"; brand_content_toggle = "paid partnership to promote a third-party business", brand_organic_toggle = "promoting the creator's own business"; branded content cannot be private ("either the 'Branded Content' option should be disabled ... or the visibility setting should be automatically switched to public"); declaration must reference "TikTok's Branded Content Policy and Music Usage Confirmation" when branded content is on.

findings.claim: Query Creator Info returns the allowed privacy levels, which differ for public vs private accounts, plus interaction flags and max duration.
findings.evidence: POST /v2/post/publish/creator_info/query/ (scope video.publish). Public accounts: PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE, MUTUAL_FOLLOW_FRIENDS, SELF_ONLY. Private accounts: FOLLOWER_OF_CREATOR, MUTUAL_FOLLOW_FRIENDS, SELF_ONLY. Also comment_disabled, duet_disabled, stitch_disabled (true for private accounts or 'No one' settings) and max_video_post_duration_sec (300 in the doc example).

findings.claim: Direct Post request fields: post_info.title (caption, max 2200 UTF-16 runes, hashtags/@mentions inline), privacy_level, disable_duet/disable_comment/disable_stitch, video_cover_timestamp_ms, brand_content_toggle, brand_organic_toggle, is_aigc; source_info.source is PULL_FROM_URL (video_url) or FILE_UPLOAD (video_size, chunk_size, total_chunk_count; response returns upload_url).
findings.evidence: Direct Post reference: title is "The video caption" with "maximum length of 2200 in UTF-16 runes. If not specified, the post will not have any captions"; example title "this will be a funny #cat video on your @tiktok #fyp"; is_aigc marks AI-generated videos and adds a "Creator labeled as AI-generated" tag; video_cover_timestamp_ms selects the cover frame in ms; for PULL_FROM_URL video_url is "a public-accessible URL from which the TikTok server will pull to retrieve the video resource"; for FILE_UPLOAD the request needs video_size, chunk_size, total_chunk_count and the response returns an upload_url.

findings.claim: PULL_FROM_URL requires the app to have verified ownership of the hosting domain (DNS signature) or exact https URL prefix (signature file) via the app's URL properties; unverified URLs fail with 403 url_ownership_unverified. The URL must be https, must not redirect (3xx), and must stay reachable for the download, which times out one hour after initiation.
findings.evidence: Media Transfer Guide / error table: "To use PULL_FROM_URL as the video transfer method, the developer must verify the ownership of the URL prefix or domain." Domain verification: "adding a signature string to the domain's DNS records"; once verified "all paths under that domain or its subdomains" are owned, but verifying static.example.com does not cover example.com. URL prefix = https scheme + host + path; "URLs that return an HTTP 3xx redirect are considered invalid"; portal flow: enter full URL, download the signature file, upload it to your URL. Verification is done via the "URL properties" button on the app page (under Connect your app), in Production mode; for Sandbox, URL verification is only required for Content Posting API. PULL_FROM_URL is for content "already on server-side file storage services"; FILE_UPLOAD is for video "on the users' devices".

findings.claim: FILE_UPLOAD chunking rules: chunks 5 MB to 64 MB (final chunk may be up to 128 MB), files under 5 MB uploaded as a single whole chunk, 1 to 1000 chunks, uploaded sequentially via PUT to upload_url with Content-Range headers; total_chunk_count = floor(video_size / chunk_size).
findings.evidence: Media Transfer Guide: "each chunk must be at least 5 MB but no greater than 64 MB, except for the final chunk, which can be greater than chunk_size (up to 128 MB) to accommodate any trailing bytes"; "Videos with a total size less than 5 MB must be uploaded as a whole"; "There must be a minimum of 1 chunk and a maximum of 1000 chunks"; chunks "must be uploaded sequentially"; total_chunk_count is video_size divided by chunk_size "rounded down to the nearest integer"; worked example: 50,000,123-byte file with 10,000,000-byte chunk_size gives total_chunk_count 5 and the trailing 123 bytes merge into the last chunk. Content-Range header form: bytes first-last/total. Accepted Content-Type: video/mp4, video/quicktime, video/webm.

findings.claim: Official media limits: MP4 (recommended), WebM, MOV; codecs H.264 (recommended), H.265, VP8, VP9; 23-60 FPS; 360-4096 px for both height and width; max file size 4 GB; longest video sendable via the init endpoint is 10 minutes.
findings.evidence: Media Transfer Guide: "MP4 (recommended) WebM MOV"; "H.264 (recommended) H.265 VP8 VP9"; "Framerate restrictions · Minimum of 23 FPS Maximum of 60 FPS"; "Picture size restrictions · Minimum of 360 pixels for both height and width Maximum of 4096 pixels for both height and width"; "Size restrictions · Maximum of 4GB"; "The longest video a developer can send via the initialize Upload Video endpoint is 10 minutes" (users can trim in-app).

findings.claim: Status polling: POST /v2/post/publish/status/fetch/ with publish_id (either scope). Statuses: PROCESSING_UPLOAD (FILE_UPLOAD path), PROCESSING_DOWNLOAD (PULL_FROM_URL path), SEND_TO_USER_INBOX (Upload mode: draft notification sent), PUBLISH_COMPLETE, FAILED (with fail_reason). post_id appears only for public, moderation-approved posts.
findings.evidence: Get Post Status: endpoint "POST /v2/post/publish/status/fetch/, with the scope video.upload or video.publish"; SEND_TO_USER_INBOX "means a notification has been sent to creator's inbox to complete the draft post using TikTok's editing flow"; PUBLISH_COMPLETE for Direct Post "indicates that the content has been posted"; "post_id is returned only if the post is published for public viewership and has been approved by the TikTok moderation process". Third-party integrators report processing typically 30 s to 2 min and FAILED arriving minutes later (e.g. unsupported encoding).

findings.claim: Sandbox mode: up to 5 sandboxes per app and up to 10 target user accounts (added with their login credentials); sandbox does NOT provide Content Posting API access for public videos; first-time apps must demonstrate the integration in a sandbox for review.
findings.evidence: Add a Sandbox: "You can create up to 5 sandboxes"; up to 10 accounts can be added as target users and "you must provide its login credentials"; "Sandbox mode does not offer access to Content Posting API for public videos or Data Portability API." App Review FAQ: "If your app has not been approved before, you are required to use a sandbox environment on the Developer Portal to demonstrate the integration."

findings.claim: App review is mandatory before any production integration (including Login Kit beyond user.info.basic). For apps created after Sept 9, 2024 the Terms of Service URL, Privacy Policy URL and Web/Desktop URL must be verified before submission; the website must be a fully developed public site (not a landing/login page) with visible Privacy Policy and ToS links; 1-5 demo videos (<=50 MB each) showing the end-to-end flow are required and the demo domain must match the website URL; TikTok gives no timeline or approval guarantee.
findings.evidence: App Review Guidelines/FAQ: "Before you integrate with our developer products, you must submit your app for review"; "you must verify URL properties for all URLs in your app configuration" (apps created after September 9, 2024); website must be "an externally facing, fully developed site, not a landing or login page" with Privacy Policy and Terms of Service links "visible on the website without opening a menu"; "At least one demo video that shows the complete end-to-end flow of the up-to-date integrations is required" (max 5, up to 50 MB each); "If you integrate with a web app, the domain shown in the demo video must match the website URL you provide"; "The user.info.basic scope is added by default ... Anything beyond that requires pre-approval"; app name must not reference social media companies; "We do not provide an official review timeline or any guarantees for approval."

findings.claim: Individual (non-company) developers CAN register and create apps on developers.tiktok.com, but TikTok says individual-account apps are 'not recommended for real app integrations'; organizations are 'highly recommended but not required'. Organization verification needs a business certificate, photo ID and proof of representation. (By contrast, the separate TikTok for Business/Marketing API portal does not onboard individuals at all.)
findings.evidence: Register Your App: "You can register an app under your individual developer account, but it is not recommended for real app integrations"; creating or joining an organization is "highly recommended but not required". Working with Organizations: "employees of a company should register apps under the ownership of the organization and not under their individual accounts." Verify Your Business: documents include "Business certificate; Photo ID of your primary or legal representative; Proof of representation"; "Only registered organization admins can view the Business page and complete verification." business-api.tiktok.com Register as a developer: "currently, we are unable to onboard personal accounts or individual developers"; email must be a verified company-domain address.

findings.claim: The Direct Post audit is applied for from the app's Content Posting API product page; the application asks for product description, user base, content source and expected daily creators, and reviewers check the posting UI against the Content Sharing Guidelines via the demo. Post-audit user caps are set from the usage estimate; no official turnaround is published (third-party reports: several days to two weeks, often with a resubmission).
findings.evidence: Third-party audit guides (Outstand, Mixpost): "On the TikTok Developer Portal go to Products → Content Posting API → Direct Post → Apply"; application covers "your product, your users, where content comes from, and how many creators you expect to publish per day"; post-audit cap is "based on the usage estimates provided in the audit application form"; a documented rejection reason was "UI does not comply with TikTok Content Sharing UX Guidelines" (missing Music Usage Confirmation link before publish). TikTok docs: "TikTok does not state a review duration in the Content Posting API documentation."

findings.claim: Login Kit for Web: authorize at https://www.tiktok.com/v2/auth/authorize/ with client_key, response_type=code, scope, redirect_uri, state; exchange at https://open.tiktokapis.com/v2/oauth/token/ with the client secret. Redirect URIs: max 10, <512 chars, absolute https, no query parameters/fragments; PKCE is specified for desktop/iOS/Android, not required for web.
findings.evidence: Login Kit for Web: "client_key=<client_key>&response_type=code&scope=<scope>&redirect_uri=<redirect_uri>&state=<state>"; "A maximum of 10 URIs is supported. The length of each URI must be less than 512 characters. URIs must be absolute and begin with https. Parameters will be denied."; Login Kit Overview says PKCE applies to desktop, iOS and Android but not web; legacy OAuth v1 tokens are deprecated.

findings.claim: The API cannot attach sounds from TikTok's music library to a video. auto_add_music exists only for photo posts in DIRECT_POST mode. To use TikTok-library/Commercial Sounds on a video, the creator must finish the post in the TikTok app (Upload/inbox mode) or the audio must already be mixed into the uploaded file (with rights cleared).
findings.evidence: Photo reference: auto_add_music "only applies to DIRECT_POST mode"; when true TikTok adds recommended music and "users can later choose to change the post's music". No equivalent field exists on the video Direct Post reference. Upload (MEDIA_UPLOAD) is described as uploading content so "users can complete the post using TikTok's editing flow". Third-party integrators (Buffer: "due to API limitations, we do not have access to TikTok's audio/music library or polls") confirm library sounds are unavailable via API.

findings.claim: TikTok music rules for a business: Business Accounts only see Commercial Sounds (the Commercial Music Library) in the in-app editor; General Music Library songs are not cleared for any brand/business content; Commercial Sounds are the only TikTok-provided sounds licensed for commercial use; externally licensed or original audio in an uploaded file requires agreeing to the Music Usage Confirmation (no copyrighted music, or all licences obtained).
findings.evidence: TikTok for Business Help: "If you use a Business Account, when you start a new video and click on Add Sound, you will only see sounds from the Commercial Music Library ('Commercial Sounds')." About CML: General Music Library songs "are not pre-cleared for commercial content, defined as any content posted by a brand, and are not available for use by any brand or business". CML User Terms: "Commercial Sounds are the only sounds made available on TikTok for Commercial Uses" and business users are responsible for "unauthorized, unlicensed use of sounds contained in the non-commercial 'General Music Library'". Music Usage Confirmation: by agreeing you confirm either that the post has no copyright-protected music, or that you obtained and paid for all necessary licences; "do not accept if you cannot confirm one of them". Business Terms: business use must use the in-app Commercial Sounds page / web CML or pre-clear all music rights. Third-party claims about automatic muting from July 25, 2025 could not be confirmed on an official page.

findings.claim: Recommended 9:16 output for Studio Assistant: 1080x1920 MP4, H.264 + AAC, 23-60 fps (30 typical), well under 4 GB and under 10 minutes; the API itself only enforces 360-4096 px per side, so 1080x1920 is a quality target rather than a hard API rule.
findings.evidence: API hard limits from Media Transfer Guide (360-4096 px, 23-60 FPS, 4 GB, 10 min). TikTok guidance pages: "The ideal format for TikTok videos is a 9:16 vertical aspect ratio. For the best quality, the recommended resolution is 1080 by 1920 pixels"; TikTok Ads materials: "The overwhelming majority of top-performing TikTok videos have a video resolution of 720p or higher"; in-feed ad spec: "Vertical (recommended): 9:16, >=540*960px ... File Size: <=500 MB. Bitrate: >=2,500kbps" (ads spec, not organic).

findings.claim: A separate official route exists for business accounts: TikTok API for Business 'Publish a public video post to an owned TikTok account' (POST /open_api/v1.3/business/video/publish/). It posts PUBLIC videos, requires a TikTok for Business developer registration with a company-domain email and public company website (individuals not onboarded), a verified video URL, and from March 20, 2026 an Accounts API Access Application Form for the 'TikTok Accounts' scope.
findings.evidence: business-api docs: endpoint POST /open_api/v1.3/business/video/publish/; video URL must be publicly reachable, .mp4/.mov/.webm, 1 GB max, 3-600 s, >=360 px, 23-60 FPS; "Since November 16, 2023, unverified video URLs can no longer be used for publishing"; limits 6 posts/minute and 15/day per account; business_id = open_id from OAuth. Register as a developer: "The communication email must be a verified company domain email"; website must be publicly accessible and match the email domain; "Individual developers and personal accounts are currently not onboarded." Accounts API: "Starting March 20, 2026 at 00:00 (GMT+0), developers must complete the Accounts API Access Application Form before submitting a new developer app or requesting a scope increase that includes the 'TikTok Accounts' permission scope."

findings.claim: TikTok's only official endorsement of third-party publishing tools is the TikTok Marketing Partners program (Content Marketing specialty, e.g. Later, Hootsuite, Sprout Social); Ayrshare, Zernio/Late and Buffer were not found in TikTok's partner announcements. Any third-party publisher is simply an audited Content Posting API / Accounts API client; TikTok does not publish a list of audited apps.
findings.evidence: TikTok for Business blog: Content Marketing partners focus on "managing, scheduling, and publishing content on TikTok" and "use TikTok's Accounts API to schedule, publish, and manage posts"; Later announced it was one of the inaugural Content Marketing badge partners (May 2022); Hootsuite and Sprout Social named in a later cohort. No TikTok source lists Ayrshare, Zernio or Buffer as badged partners; Ayrshare's own marketing says "YouTube and TikTok cleared" and "approved connections to the Pinterest and TikTok APIs".

findings.claim: Ayrshare offers pre-audited TikTok direct publishing via its API (video, photo, privacy/visibility, isBrandedContent, isAIGenerated, autoAddMusic), but pricing starts around US$149/month for a single profile, which is disproportionate for one barber account.
findings.evidence: Ayrshare docs: TikTok limit "6 videos per minute and 15 per day"; visibility values public/private/followers/friends; autoAddMusic boolean (default false) adds recommended music that users can change in-app; media guidelines: MP4/MOV/WebM, 3-600 s, 9:16 or 16:9, min 360 px, 10 GB Ayrshare-side max (raised from 1 GB March 2026). Third-party pricing summaries: Premium ~$149/mo (1 profile), Launch ~$299/mo (10 profiles), Business ~$499-599/mo (30 profiles); "API access is included on all Ayrshare plans".

findings.claim: Late (getlate.dev) has rebranded to Zernio; its TikTok posting requires media, explicit consent flags, and a privacy level from the creator's allowed list. It exposes two connection types: accounts connected via TikTok's Business app can only direct-post PUBLIC videos (non-public goes via inbox drafts), while developer-app accounts share an app-wide direct-posting cap. Pricing reportedly usage/per-account based with the first two connected accounts free.
findings.evidence: docs.zernio.com TikTok: posts to POST /v1/posts with platform "tiktok"; "TikTok requires media on every post"; requires content_preview_confirmed: true and express_consent_given: true; privacy level must be one TikTok reports for that creator; Business-app accounts: a video direct post "must be public, and any other level gets rejected", use draft: true to pick audience in TikTok drafts; developer-app accounts "share an app-wide direct posting cap" ("direct posting is at capacity" error). Third-party reviews (Sept 2026 snapshot): first two connected accounts free, then $6/month each for accounts 3-10; getlate.dev redirects to zernio.com; existing API routes/keys unchanged.

findings.claim: Buffer's rebuilt GraphQL API (api.buffer.com) is publicly available to every Buffer customer via personal API keys (one key on Free, more on paid), supports TikTok as a channel, and can create posts with schedulingType automatic or notification; Buffer supports business and personal TikTok accounts but cannot access TikTok's music library or polls, and enforces TikTok's 2200-character caption limit and a 25 posts/24h cap. The legacy REST API shuts down February 1, 2027.
findings.evidence: buffer.com/api: "Buffer's API is publicly available to every Buffer customer"; "API keys are personal and tied to your user account, not your organization. Currently, only the organization owner can create API keys"; requests use the key as a Bearer token against the GraphQL endpoint and "should be made from your server"; third-party apps acting for other users "use OAuth 2.0 (Authorization Code with PKCE)"; "Buffer's Legacy REST API is being fully retired on February 1, 2027". Using TikTok with Buffer: "Buffer supports both business and personal TikTok accounts"; "due to API limitations, we do not have access to TikTok's audio/music library or polls"; notification publishing used when music/polls are added or video exceeds 10 min; limits "25 posts per 24 hours" and "2200 characters per post". API reference: schedulingType 'notification' vs 'automatic'; CreatePostInput marked experimental.

findings.claim: Zapier has no native TikTok publishing action: its native TikTok apps are TikTok Lead Generation (trigger: New Lead) and TikTok Conversions (action: Send Lead Event). Publishing via Zapier goes through intermediaries such as Buffer or Postpone.
findings.evidence: Zapier Help: TikTok Lead Generation lists a single instant trigger "New Lead", "no searches and no actions"; TikTok Conversions integration pages describe a "Send Lead Event" action. Buffer Help "Using Zapier with Buffer": "with video uploads supported, you can manage TikTok posts" and the Zapier integration passes a video to Buffer where "the URL must be a direct link to the media". Zapier listings show Postpone actions with TikTok account, video URL, caption, date/time and duet toggle fields.

findings.claim: No official 2025-2026 changes to the Content Posting API were found; the official changelog's newest surfaced entry is October 8, 2024 (Login Kit for Android requires HTTPS redirect URI). Related dated changes: URL-property verification required for apps created after Sept 9, 2024; Share Video API end-of-life Sept 10, 2023; photo posting added Nov 2023; TikTok for Business Accounts API application form from March 20, 2026.
findings.evidence: Changelog (search summary): "The newest changelog entry it returned is from October 8, 2024" ("Login Kit for Android now requires the authorization request's redirect URI to follow an HTTPS scheme"); Migration Notice: Share Video API deprecated by September 10, 2023; Content Posting API launched April 2023, Direct Post June 2023, photos November 2023. Developer Guidelines: TikTok "reserves the right to deprecate APIs and SDKs" with notice of backward-incompatible changes.

implementation_decision: Decision: ship the draft/export fallback as the only TikTok path in Stage A/B, and do NOT build a direct Content Posting API integration for Studio Assistant. Reasoning: (1) TikTok's Content Sharing Guidelines explicitly list "a utility tool to help upload contents to the account(s) you or your team manages" as an unacceptable use case and require apps intended for a wide audience, so a private single-barber app is very unlikely to pass the audit; (2) without the audit every API post (Direct Post, and per the guidelines also any unaudited client posting) is forced to SELF_ONLY and requires the TikTok account to be set private at posting time, which is useless for a public business profile; (3) app review itself needs a public, fully developed website with visible Privacy Policy/ToS, verified URL properties, demo videos and a sandbox demonstration, with no approval guarantee; (4) even an audited integration cannot attach TikTok Commercial Sounds to videos, which a Business Account can only add inside the TikTok app. Concretely, Studio Assistant will: render a TikTok-ready export (1080x1920 9:16 MP4, H.264 High profile, AAC 48 kHz, 30 fps, target 8-12 Mbps, under 10 min and well under 4 GB, with caption safe margins), generate a caption up to 2200 characters including hashtags/@mentions, store the caption + export in a "Ready to post" queue with an honest status ("Post in the TikTok app; add a Commercial Sound there"), expose a one-tap download/share and copy-caption flow on the owner's phone, and record "Posted" manually. Music handling: never mix third-party commercial tracks into the TikTok export unless the licence explicitly covers TikTok commercial use (and surface the Music Usage Confirmation wording); default exports to voice/original or licensed library audio, and instruct the owner to pick from Commercial Sounds in-app. Optional Stage C upgrade if the owner wants true auto-publishing: integrate a pre-audited provider behind a feature flag rather than TikTok directly, preferring Buffer (personal API key on the owner's own Buffer account, TikTok channel, schedulingType automatic; low cost) or Zernio (first two connected accounts free, requires content_preview_confirmed and express_consent_given flags, privacy must be from creator's allowed list), with Ayrshare rejected on cost (~US$149/month for one profile) and Zapier rejected because it has no native TikTok publish action. The TikTok for Business "publish a public video post to an owned account" API is the only official self-serve public-posting route for a business, but it requires a company-domain email, a public company website, a Business developer app and (since 20 Mar 2026) an Accounts API access application; park it as a future option only if the owner registers the business as a TikTok for Business developer. Status model for the publishing module must therefore have states: exported, handed-off-to-TikTok-app, posted (manual confirm), and, if the provider flag is on, queued/processing/published/failed with the provider's post id.
account_requirements: Owner must have a TikTok account for the shop; a TikTok Business Account restricts in-app sounds to Commercial Sounds (Commercial Music Library) and TikTok says General Music Library tracks are not cleared for any brand/business content; original/voice audio or externally licensed music requires agreeing to the Music Usage Confirmation.
Fallback path (chosen): no developer account, app review or audit needed; owner posts the exported MP4 from the TikTok app/TikTok Studio and adds Commercial Sounds there.

If direct integration is ever attempted: register at developers.tiktok.com (individual accounts allowed but 'not recommended for real app integrations'; create/join an organization for the business, verification needs business certificate + photo ID + proof of representation); create an app with Login Kit + Content Posting API (Direct Post and/or Upload), verified Terms of Service URL, Privacy Policy URL and Web URL (required for apps created after 9 Sep 2024); a public, fully developed website with visible Privacy Policy and ToS links (not a login page); 1-5 demo videos (<=50 MB each) whose domain matches the website URL; sandbox demonstration for a first-time app; then a separate Content Posting API (Direct Post) audit proving UX compliance with the Content Sharing Guidelines - and TikTok lists single-team upload utilities as not acceptable, so expect rejection.

Until audited (if integrating): only 5 users per 24 h, all posts forced SELF_ONLY, the TikTok account must be set private at posting time; Direct Post ~15 posts/day/creator; Upload mode max 5 pending inbox drafts per 24 h; 6 init requests/min per user token.

PULL_FROM_URL (if used) requires verifying the hosting domain (DNS signature) or exact https URL prefix (signature file) in the app's URL properties; FILE_UPLOAD avoids this but must follow 5-64 MB chunk rules.

Provider option (Stage C, optional): Buffer account owned by the business (organization owner creates the personal API key; Free plan has one key, TikTok channel connected via Buffer's own audited app; no TikTok music library/polls; 25 posts/24 h) or Zernio account (first two connected accounts free per Sept 2026 pricing; TikTok connection via Zernio's audited app; consent flags required). Ayrshare starts ~US$149/month for one profile. Zapier cannot publish to TikTok natively.

TikTok for Business API alternative (future only): TikTok for Business developer registration with a company-domain email and publicly accessible company website matching that domain (individuals not onboarded), a Business developer app, and from 20 Mar 2026 the Accounts API Access Application Form for the 'TikTok Accounts' scope; video URL domain must be verified; 1 GB / 3-600 s / 6 per min / 15 per day.
uncertainties: Every source was read via web-search summaries, not full pages: developers.tiktok.com, ayrshare.com, getlate.dev, buffer.com and zapier.com all failed DNS resolution in this sandbox (hosts must be allowed in the session's network settings to fetch them directly). Quoted wording is as surfaced by the search tool and should be re-checked on the live pages before implementation.

Whether the Upload-to-inbox (video.upload) mode is also subject to the unaudited 'account must be private / SELF_ONLY' rule is not fully settled: the Content Sharing Guidelines wording and the unaudited_client_can_only_post_to_private_accounts error are documented on the Direct Post pages; some third-party integrators claim inbox drafts are exempt. Treat Upload mode as audit-gated unless verified in a sandbox.

Official TikTok pages show no visible 'last updated' dates; the search index copies were ~97 days old. One search summary referred to the docs as 'last updated August 2026' but that could not be confirmed. No 2025-2026 Content Posting API changelog entries were found, so changes may exist that the index missed.
Audit turnaround (third-party reports: several days to two weeks) and the exact post-audit caps are unofficial; TikTok publishes no timeline and says approval is not guaranteed.

The exact rendering of the audit application form (Products > Content Posting API > Direct Post > Apply) and whether organization/business verification is mandatory for the audit come from third-party guides, not official docs.

TikTok's own docs are internally inconsistent on some limits: spam_risk_too_many_posts is listed as HTTP 200 on the creator_info page but 403 on Direct Post; status-fetch rate limit (30/min) and the 15-25 posts/day figures are partly from third parties.

Claims about automatic muting of non-Commercial-Music-Library audio on Business Accounts since July 25, 2025 come from music-vendor blogs; no official TikTok page confirming the date or mechanism was found.

Ayrshare, Zernio and Buffer pricing figures are from third-party review/competitor sites (2026 snapshots) and may be outdated; none of these vendors was confirmed as a TikTok Marketing Partner. Buffer's statement that OAuth app clients are available conflicts with a third-party claim that third-party OAuth on the new API is not yet enabled (irrelevant if the owner uses a personal API key).
Whether Buffer's API createPost (marked experimental) supports TikTok automatic publishing with video media end-to-end was not verified.

No Australia-specific restrictions on TikTok developer registration were found, but regional availability of the Developer Portal and of the Commercial Music Library catalogue was not explicitly checked.

topic: Spotify integration feasibility for Studio Assistant (private single-barber-business web app, Ivanhoe VIC, Australia) — Developer Policy/Terms restrictions (AI/ML, previews, third-party transfer, video/sync), Web API changes Nov 2024–Nov 2026 (deprecations, Development Mode, Extended Quota), and whether any permitted private use exists.

findings.claim: The current Spotify Developer Terms are Version 10, effective 15 May 2025, and the Developer Policy is likewise 'Effective as of 15 May, 2025'; no later revision was found as of 2026-11-09.
findings.evidence: Search snippets of the Terms page: 'Version 10, effective as of 15 May, 2025'. Policy page header: 'Effective as of 15 May, 2025'. The April 2025 blog: 'updated Developer Terms, which also take effect May 15, 2025'. Terms Section IX: 'Spotify may revise these Developer Terms from time to time and the most current version will always be posted on our website.' Caveat: search index copies are ~543 days old, so a post-May-2025 revision cannot be fully excluded.

findings.claim: AI/ML: both the Policy and the Terms flatly prohibit training on, or otherwise ingesting, Spotify Content into an ML/AI model; there is no published exception.
findings.evidence: Policy (under 'Respect Content and Creators'): 'Do not use the Spotify Platform or any Spotify Content to train a machine learning or AI model or otherwise ingest Spotify Content into a machine learning or AI model.' Terms Section IV repeats it. April 2025 blog rationale: 'using Spotify data or information to train models is outside the scope of what the platform is built for.' The 2026 'Building with AI' tutorial's suggested prompt: 'do not cache Spotify content beyond what is needed for immediate use, always attribute content to Spotify, and do not use the API to train machine learning models on Spotify data.' Community thread asking for exceptions got 'There isn't an exception' (non-staff). Whether passing API results into an LLM prompt counts as 'ingest' has no official ruling; community reading is that it does.

findings.claim: 30-second previews: 'Audio Preview Clips' are a defined, non-Streaming category that must link back to Spotify and may not be a standalone product — but in practice preview URLs have been null/deprecated for new (Development Mode) apps since 27 Nov 2024.
findings.evidence: Terms definitions: '"Audio Preview Clips" means 30-second preview clips accessible using the Spotify Platform' and 'Widgets or (ii) Audio Preview Clips, are not included in the definition of Streaming'. Policy: 'Metadata, cover art and Audio Preview Clips must be accompanied by a link back to the applicable album, content or playlist on the Spotify Service' and 'Audio Preview Clips may not be offered as a standalone service or product.' Nov 2024 blog removed '30-second preview URLs, in multi-get responses' for new use cases; community threads (2024–2025) report preview_url null for single-track GET, Search and Client Credentials too; the Search reference marks preview_url 'deprecated'. A Feb 2026 community post says preview URLs and audio features 'were already removed'.

findings.claim: Streaming/playback outside Spotify: full streaming is Premium-only, the Spotify app is the default playback mechanism, and the Web Playback SDK is barred from commercial projects without written approval.
findings.evidence: Policy: full streaming 'shall only be made available to subscribers to the Premium Spotify Service'; 'Widgets and (ii) Audio Preview Clips may be made available to Spotify users who do not subscribe to the Premium service'. Design guidelines: 'The Spotify app is the default playback mechanism.' Web Playback SDK page: 'must not be used in commercial projects without Spotify's prior written approval.'

findings.claim: Transfer to third parties is prohibited (even with user consent), including derivative/aggregate data; only data processors such as hosting providers are permitted.
findings.evidence: Terms: 'do not transfer Spotify Content to third parties, including directly or indirectly transferring any data (including aggregate, anonymous or derivative data) received from Spotify to, or use such data in connection with, any advertising or monetization service, ad network, data broker…' and this applies 'even if a user consents to such transfer or use.' Exception: sharing with 'third-party data processors, such as hosting providers' subject to your privacy policy, with you 'responsible for those processors' acts or omissions.' Compliance Tips also rule out repackaging API data and selling it.

findings.claim: Spotify content in videos/exports: synchronising any Spotify sound recording with visual media (video, slideshow, advertising) and mixing/overlapping Spotify audio with other audio are expressly prohibited — so Spotify audio (streams or previews) can never be part of a Studio Assistant render or export.
findings.evidence: Policy: 'Do not synchronize any sound recordings with any visual media, including any advertising, film, television program, slideshow, video, or similar content.' and 'Do not permit any device or system to segue, mix, re-mix, or overlap any Spotify Content with any other audio content (including other Spotify Content).' Compliance Tips 'Synchronization' use-case to avoid: 'Syncing sound recordings accessed via the Spotify Platform with other recordings, lyrics, or video.' Web Playback SDK reference repeats: 'You may not synchronize any sound recordings with any visual media…'

findings.claim: Storage/caching: Spotify Content may only be stored as strictly necessary to run the app, never indefinitely; local caching is limited to temporary metadata and cover art.
findings.evidence: Terms: 'you may not store, aggregate or create compilations or databases of Spotify Content, other than as strictly necessary to operate your SDA. Do not store Spotify Content indefinitely.' and 'Do not locally cache any Spotify Content, except as strictly necessary to enhance the performance of your SDA and its functionality, and limited to the temporary caching of metadata and cover art; or Conditional Downloads of sound recordings.' 'Spotify Content' includes 'cover art… metadata, playlists, and user data'. Compliance Tips: avoid storing data you can fetch on the fly. Policy: make reasonable efforts to show the most current data and delete older data.

findings.claim: Attribution and branding are mandatory whenever Spotify metadata/cover art is displayed.
findings.evidence: Policy: 'If you display any Spotify Content you must clearly attribute the content as being supplied and made available by Spotify, by using the Spotify Marks.' Design guidelines: 'The Spotify logo should never be smaller than 70px in digital… The Spotify icon should never be smaller than 21px in digital'; metadata 'must link back to the Spotify Service'; 'Don't incorporate Spotify's trademarks, in whole or in part, in the name of your company, product, application, service, or website.'

findings.claim: Commercial use: the Policy bars commercial uses of SDAs except limited ones for Non-Streaming SDAs, and Spotify frames Development Mode as for 'learning and non-commercial personal projects' that 'should not be relied on as a foundation for building or scaling a business on Spotify'.
findings.evidence: Policy Section IV ('Streaming and Commercial Use'): 'Except for the limited commercial uses for Non-Streaming SDAs (set out below) commercial uses are not permitted for SDAs.' Non-Streaming SDAs may sell advertising/sponsorships and sell the app or access to it. Feb 2026 blog: 'Development Mode provides a sandboxed environment for learning and experimentation. It is intentionally limited and should not be relied on as a foundation for building or scaling a business on Spotify.' April 2025 blog: 'development mode will remain available for experimentation and personal use.'

findings.claim: Nov 27 2024 Web API change: eight capabilities were withdrawn for all new apps and for existing Development Mode apps without a pending extension request; only apps already in Extended Quota Mode kept them.
findings.evidence: Blog list: 'Related Artists, Recommendations, Audio Features, Audio Analysis, Get Featured Playlists, Get Category's Playlists, 30-second preview URLs, in multi-get responses, Algorithmic and Spotify-owned editorial playlists.' Affected: 'existing apps that are still in development mode without a pending extension request, and new apps registered on or after that date.' Apps with extended mode access using these endpoints 'are not affected'.

findings.claim: Since 15 May 2025 Extended Quota Mode is effectively closed to individuals and small businesses: organizations only, legally registered business, launched service, ≥250k MAU, key markets, commercial viability.
findings.evidence: April 2025 blog: 'Starting May 15, 2025, extended Web API access will be reserved for apps with established, scalable, and impactful use cases that help drive our platform strategy and promote artist and creator discovery'; 'over 95% of the applications we receive for extended Web API access fall short of basic security, privacy, and licensing standards'; existing compliant extended apps 'remain unaffected'. Quota modes page: 'As of May 15th 2025, Spotify only accepts applications from organizations (not individuals)'; requirements listed as a legally registered business or organisation, an active and launched service, at least 250k monthly active users, availability in key Spotify markets, commercial viability, adherence to terms; applications via a Partner Application form 'through a company email'. Terms: 'Spotify makes no promise or guarantee that such extended access request will be approved.'

findings.claim: Feb 2026 Development Mode overhaul: owner must hold Spotify Premium, max 5 authorized users per Client ID, 1 Client ID per developer (raised to 25 in July 2026), and a reduced endpoint set; stated reason is automation/AI risk.
findings.evidence: Feb 6 2026 blog: 'advances in automation and AI have fundamentally altered the usage patterns and risk profile of developer access'; 'Development Mode use will require a Spotify Premium account'; 'developers will be limited to one Development Mode Client ID'; 'each Client ID will be limited to up to five authorized users'; 'API access will be limited to a smaller set of supported endpoints'; 'Starting Wednesday, 11 February, all newly created Development Mode Client IDs will be created under the updated Development Mode rules'; from 9 March the Premium requirement, user cap and one-Client-ID limit 'will take effect as planned for existing Development Mode integrations' while 'we have decided to postpone endpoint access changes for existing integrations.' Migration guide: 'If the owner's Premium subscription lapses, the app will stop working.' Users are added in the Dashboard's Users Management tab (name + Spotify email); non-allowlisted users get 403. rspotify issue quotes the 403 body: 'Your application is blocked from accessing the Web API since you do not have a Spotify Premium subscription.'

findings.claim: Under the Feb 2026 Dev Mode rules, Search (GET /search, limit max 10, default 5) and single-item lookups such as Get Track (GET /tracks/{id}) remain available, while batch GETs, browse endpoints, other users' profiles/playlists, markets, artist top tracks and many fields (popularity, label, album_group, available_markets, followers, linked_from, PrivateUser country/email/product) were removed; external_ids was reinstated in March 2026.
findings.evidence: Changelog lists 'Get Track (GET /tracks/{id}) – Retrieves metadata for a single track.' and 'Search for Item (GET /search)' among endpoints still available; 'The limit parameter maximum value has been reduced from 50 to 10, and the default value has been changed from 20 to 5.' Migration guide: batch fetches 'GET /tracks, /albums, /artists, /episodes, /shows, /audiobooks, /chapters' removed with single-item replacements; 'GET /users/{id}', 'GET /markets', new releases, categories, artist top tracks removed; save/follow calls consolidated into '/me/library'; playlist '/tracks' routes moved to '/items'. rspotify issue #550 (read in full) lists the removed fields. March 2026 changelog: 'external_ids… will continue to be available.' 'Apps in extended quota mode are not affected by any of the changes described in this guide.'

findings.claim: June 2026: user refresh tokens now expire 6 months after the original authorization (not extended by refreshing); new apps immediately, existing apps from 20 Jul 2026; Client Credentials unaffected.
findings.evidence: Blog: 'Refresh tokens issued to apps registered on Spotify for Developers will now require reauthentication after 6 months'; 'Refreshing an access token does not reset or extend the refresh token's 6-month lifetime, which is measured from the moment of the user's original authorization'; expired token → '400 Bad Request… invalid_grant' and the app should send the user through sign-in again; applies to Authorization Code and PKCE flows only.

findings.claim: July 2026: Dev Mode quota is now pooled per developer account (not per Client ID), the Client ID limit rose from 1 to 25, and quota exhaustion returns 429 with a 'reason' of QUOTA_EXCEEDED; no Aug–Nov 2026 changes to Dev Mode rules were found.
findings.evidence: July 23 2026 blog/changelog: 'Client ID limit increased from 1 to 25 per developer account'; 'Going forward, the quota is counted per developer account. If you have multiple apps in Development Mode, the quota for all of those apps is shared under a single budget'; 429 body 'reason' field 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED'. Quota modes page: specific quota groupings and limits 'subject to change' (no published numbers). May 2026 changelog only added 'account_id' to the User object. Searches for Aug–Nov 2026 changelogs returned nothing new.

findings.claim: Privacy obligations apply even to a private app: show a privacy policy before sign-in, offer an easy disconnect, and delete Spotify Personal Data on disconnect/termination.
findings.evidence: Terms: 'You must display a privacy policy to end users before they install or signup to your SDA.' Policy: 'You must provide a privacy policy which clearly describes how you intend to access, use, process and disclose user data'; apps must offer an easy way to disconnect and, on disconnect, 'delete that user's personal data and stop requesting or processing it'; upon termination 'delete Spotify Content, including Spotify Personal Data'. Terms Section V.4: data beyond preselected categories needs explicit consent for any use beyond showing it back to that user.

findings.claim: A no-API alternative exists: the official Spotify Embed (iframe / oEmbed at open.spotify.com/oembed) plays ~30-second previews for logged-out viewers and full tracks for logged-in (Premium) users, needs no developer app, but is governed by the Widget Terms (no local caching, no games, Play Button 'may not be used for commercial purposes').
findings.evidence: Embeds docs list three methods: copy HTML from the Spotify client, the iFrame API, the oEmbed API; 'Creating an Embed' involves only the Share menu, no developer-account step. oEmbed reference: endpoint 'https://open.spotify.com/oembed', response includes html, title, thumbnail. Troubleshooting: 'in some situations the Embed will only stream a preview clip of less than 30 seconds'; removing allow="encrypted-media" means 'the Embed will only allow users to listen to previews'. 2018 dev post: full playback requires the user be 'logged into spotify.com in their web browser'; 'in the cases where full track playback is not supported, we will play 30 second preview clips.' Widget Terms (v2.0, 27 May 2014): 'the Spotify Play Button may not be used for commercial purposes' (embedding on sites with ads is allowed), no game/trivia use without written approval, 'may not use a Widget to locally cache any Spotify Content'.

findings.claim: Playing Spotify in the barber shop itself is outside Spotify's consumer licence; Spotify points businesses to its partner Soundtrack.
findings.evidence: Spotify support: under its Terms and Conditions Spotify 'is only for personal, non-commercial use'; examples of disallowed settings include 'bars, restaurants, schools, stores, salons, dance studios, radio stations'; for a 'commercial environment' it names Soundtrack. (Consumer terms, not developer terms; included because Studio Assistant must not imply in-shop playback is covered.)

implementation_decision:
Decision: Studio Assistant CAN offer Spotify only as an optional, narrowly-scoped "mood/genre reference" feature — never as a music source, never as an input to AI, and never in rendered video. Implement it in two tiers and make the limits explicit in the UI.

Tier 0 (default, ship first; no Spotify developer account, no Premium): the owner pastes a Spotify track/album/playlist link. Studio Assistant stores only the Spotify URL/URI plus the owner's own typed labels (e.g., "upbeat afrobeats for Saturday reels"). On display it renders the official Spotify Embed (iframe built from the link, or oEmbed for title/thumbnail fetched at view time, not persisted) with Spotify attribution and the link back to open.spotify.com. The embed plays Spotify's own ~30s preview or the full track for a logged-in Premium viewer — Studio Assistant never touches audio. Nothing from the embed/oEmbed (title, thumbnail, artist) is stored long-term, fed to the planner/LLM, exported, or sent to any third-party service (TikTok/Instagram/Square/email modules must be firewalled from Spotify data; hosting provider only).

Tier 1 (optional, behind a settings toggle with an acknowledgement screen): in-app track search via the Web API in Development Mode, Authorization Code with PKCE (no Implicit Grant, no Client Credentials), GET /search (limit ≤10, paginate with offset) and GET /tracks/{id}. Save only the Spotify URI + owner notes; show name/artist/cover art by re-fetching at view time (temporary cache only), with Spotify logo/icon ≥70px/21px and link-back on every displayed item. Handle 401/invalid_grant (6-month refresh-token expiry → re-sign-in), 403 (owner's Premium lapsed or user not allowlisted → show plain explanation), 429 (rate limit vs reason=QUOTA_EXCEEDED → back off). Provide a Disconnect button that deletes all Spotify-derived data for that user; publish a privacy policy page and show it before the Spotify sign-in. Treat this tier as revocable: the UI must say Spotify describes Development Mode as for learning and non-commercial personal projects and may withdraw access.

Explicitly NOT supported (show as disabled states with honest copy): in-app 30-second previews via the API (preview_url is null/deprecated for new apps), Audio Features/Analysis, Recommendations, Related Artists, editorial/algorithmic playlists; any AI/LLM analysis, mood classification, or planning that ingests Spotify metadata (Policy/Terms "ingest into a machine learning or AI model" ban); any use of Spotify audio in previews, renders or exports (sync and mixing bans); transferring Spotify data to publishing/analytics/third parties; Extended Quota Mode (organizations with ≥250k MAU only — do not plan for it); and in-shop playback (Spotify consumer licence is personal, non-commercial; a commercial background-music service is needed). Music for the videos themselves must come from Studio Assistant's separate licensed-music model, not Spotify.

If the owner declines the Premium/Dev-Mode requirements, Tier 0 still works; if Spotify later tightens embeds or Dev Mode, degrade to link-only (URL + owner notes) rather than breaking.
account_requirements: Tier 0 (embed/link-only): no Spotify developer account, Client ID or Premium needed; comply with the Widget Terms of Use (no local caching of Spotify Content, no game/trivia use, Play Button not for commercial purposes, no circumventing privacy features) and show Spotify attribution/link-back.
Tier 1 (Web API, Development Mode): a Spotify account for the owner with an ACTIVE Spotify Premium subscription — the app stops working (403) if Premium lapses.

Tier 1: a Spotify for Developers account linked to that Spotify account, accepting the Developer Terms (v10, eff. 15 May 2025) and Developer Policy (eff. 15 May 2025); create a Development Mode app (Client ID) in the Dashboard — up to 25 Client IDs per account since July 2026, quota pooled across them.

Tier 1: register the app's HTTPS redirect URI(s) and use Authorization Code with PKCE (Implicit Grant is deprecated); plan for refresh tokens expiring 6 months after each user's original authorization (re-sign-in flow).

Tier 1: add every user (owner + staff) by name and Spotify email in the app's Users Management tab; hard cap of 5 authorized users per Client ID (unverified whether the owner counts toward the five) — staff without allowlisting get 403.
Tier 1: publish an end-user privacy policy and display it before Spotify sign-in; provide an in-app Disconnect that deletes Spotify Personal Data; delete all Spotify Content on termination.

Tier 1: display Spotify Marks for any Spotify content (logo ≥70px or icon ≥21px, link back to the item on Spotify); do not use 'Spotify' or its marks in the product name; do not modify/crop cover art.

Tier 1: store only Spotify URIs/links plus owner-authored notes; cache metadata/cover art only temporarily; never feed Spotify data to AI/LLM features; never sync/mix Spotify audio with video or other audio; never transfer Spotify data to third parties other than the hosting provider.

No app review exists or is needed for Development Mode; Extended Quota Mode is NOT attainable (organizations only, company email, legally registered business, launched service, ≥250k MAU, key markets, commercial viability) and should not be planned for.

Operational: expect Dev Mode quota/rate limits (429 with reason=QUOTA_EXCEEDED vs ordinary rate limiting); Spotify states Development Mode is for learning and non-commercial personal projects and 'should not be relied on as a foundation for building or scaling a business' — the owner must accept that Spotify may revoke or narrow access at any time.

In-shop music: the owner's Spotify consumer account does not licence playback in a salon/shop; a commercial background-music service (Spotify names its partner Soundtrack) is required — out of scope for Studio Assistant but must not be implied as covered.
uncertainties: No official Spotify page could be read in full: developer.spotify.com, community.spotify.com, open.spotify.com, support.spotify.com (fetch) and most news hosts (techcrunch.com, techzine.eu, vorplabs.com, brizm.dev, musically.com, itechguides.com, ubos.tech, checkleaked.cc, activepieces.com) are blocked in this sandbox (ENOTFOUND); all quoted official wording comes from search-engine summaries, some from index copies ~543 days old (≈ the May 2025 versions). A Terms/Policy revision after 15 May 2025 cannot be fully excluded, though none surfaced.
Section numbering of the AI/ML clause (community 'Clause 14', a GitHub note 'III.14') is unverified; the Terms-side reference to 'Section IV' also comes from a summary.

Whether passing Spotify metadata (track names, artists) into an LLM prompt counts as 'otherwise ingest Spotify Content into a machine learning or AI model' has no official clarification; community readings say yes. The decision treats it as prohibited.

Whether an internal tool used by a business (not sold, no ads, no streaming) is a prohibited 'commercial use' under Policy Section IV, and whether it fits Spotify's 'non-commercial personal projects' framing of Development Mode, is not addressed by any published Spotify guidance; revocation risk exists.

preview_url status: official 2026 changelogs could not be confirmed to list it as removed; the Search reference marks it 'deprecated' and community reports say it has returned null for new/Dev Mode apps since late 2024. Treat previews via the API as unavailable.

Whether the 5-user cap counts the app owner; whether the Feb 2026 endpoint restrictions have since been applied to pre-11-Feb-2026 existing apps (Spotify said postponed, 'details on updated timelines' to follow; none found) — irrelevant for a new Studio Assistant app, which gets the new rules from day one.
Date conflicts on Spotify's community index (lists the 6 Feb 2026 post under 18 Jun 2026 and the 23 Jul 2026 post under 13 Aug 2026) were not resolved; possibly later edits to those posts.

oEmbed endpoint: docs show a plain GET on open.spotify.com/oembed with no credentials, but it could not be tested from the sandbox. Current embed behaviour (30s preview logged-out; full track for logged-in Premium with allow="encrypted-media") is corroborated only by a 2018 Spotify post, WordPress docs and community threads.

Widget Terms wording ('may not be used for commercial purposes') is from the 2014 v2.0 text surfaced by search; the current version was not read, and its application to an internal business tool is unclear.

rspotify issue #550 quoted Spotify as 'moving away from the Client Credentials flow for metadata endpoints', but current Spotify docs still describe Client Credentials for public data; the recommendation to use user OAuth (PKCE) sidesteps this.

Exact Development Mode request quota numbers are not published ('subject to change'); the 250k MAU Extended Quota threshold comes from the undated quota-modes page (consistent with third-party reports).

Australia-specific points were not verified: availability of Spotify for Developers to Australian accounts (assumed), and public-performance/background-music licensing for the salon (not researched here beyond Spotify's own statement).
