findings.claim: Meta now documents three ways to connect an Instagram professional account: 'Instagram API with Instagram Login' (host graph.instagram.com, no Facebook Page), 'Instagram API with Facebook Login for Business' (host graph.facebook.com, Facebook Page required) and, since 2026, 'Instagram API with Unified Login', which Meta calls the recommended setup for new integrations.
findings.evidence: Instagram Platform page (last updated Sep 16, 2026): 'The Instagram API with Unified Login lets your business clients connect their Instagram professional account to your app by logging in with either Instagram or Facebook, without a Facebook Page. Through one login flow, your app can send and receive messages, publish content, moderate comments, and manage ads for those accounts. The Instagram API with Unified Login is the recommended setup for new integrations.' Overview comparison table: Facebook Page 'Required' for Facebook Login, not applicable for Instagram Login; 'Your app can either use Facebook Login or Instagram Login but not both.'

findings.claim: Instagram API with Instagram Login requires only an Instagram professional account (Business or Creator); no Facebook Page; it cannot do ads, hashtag search or product tagging; all endpoints are on graph.instagram.com.
findings.evidence: Overview: 'This API setup does not require a Facebook Page to be linked to the Instagram professional account'; 'this API setup cannot access ads or tagging'; hashtag search and product tagging unchecked for Instagram Login and checked for Facebook Login ('all endpoints are accessed via the graph.facebook.com host' for Facebook Login).

findings.claim: Instagram API with Facebook Login requires the Instagram professional account to be connected to a Facebook Page and cannot access consumer accounts.
findings.evidence: 'If your app implements Facebook Login for Business, your app users' Instagram professional accounts must be connected to a Facebook Page.' 'The Instagram API with Facebook Login cannot access Instagram consumer accounts (i.e., non-Business or non-Creator Instagram accounts).'

findings.claim: Permission names differ by login type. Instagram Login: instagram_business_basic + instagram_business_content_publish (unprefixed scopes such as business_basic were deprecated Jan 27, 2025). Facebook Login: instagram_basic + instagram_content_publish + pages_read_engagement (+ ads_management / ads_read if the user has a Business Manager role on the Page). Meta's App Review page spells the Instagram-Login permission 'instagram_business_content_publishing', an inconsistency across Meta pages.
findings.evidence: Instagram Login overview: 'The new scope values are: instagram_business_basic, instagram_business_content_publish, instagram_business_manage_messages, instagram_business_manage_comments' and 'The old scope values will be deprecated on January 27, 2025.' Content publishing guide lists 'instagram_basic instagram_content_publish pages_read_engagement' for Facebook Login and adds 'ads_management ads_read' if the app user has a Business Manager role on the Page. content_publishing_limit reference: Instagram Login needs instagram_business_basic and instagram_business_content_publish. App Review page: 'New permissions for this API: instagram_business_basic, instagram_business_content_publishing, instagram_business_manage_comments, instagram_business_manage_messages'.

findings.claim: Standard Access is the default and is enough, with no App Review and no Business Verification, when the app serves only Instagram professional accounts the developer owns or manages and the app users hold a role on the app; Advanced Access (App Review + Business Verification) is needed only to serve accounts you don't own/manage.
findings.evidence: Overview: 'Standard Access is the default access level for all apps and limits the data your app can get. It is intended for apps that will only be used by people who have roles on them, during app development, or for testing your app. Advanced Access is the access level required if your app serves Instagram professional accounts that you don't own or manage.' Access Levels: 'Permissions with Standard Access can only be requested from app users who have a role on the requesting app.' App Review page table: 'My app is only for a business I own or manage. No login or Instagram Login, Standard Access, Not required' vs 'I am a Tech Provider and my app serves multiple businesses ... Advanced Access, Required'. 'You must complete Business Verification if your app requires Advanced Access; if your app will be used by app users who do not have a Role on the app itself, or a Role in a Business that has claimed the app.'

findings.claim: For an app that only manages your own Instagram accounts, Meta says you do not even need to build a login flow: configure the business login settings in the App Dashboard and generate long-lived tokens there ('Generate access tokens' > 'Add account' logs the Instagram account in via a popup).
findings.evidence: Business Login doc: 'if your app serves only your Instagram professional accounts, or accounts you manage, you do not need to implement a login flow. However, you will need to configure the business login settings in the App Dashboard to obtain an Instagram app ID and an Instagram app secret, as well as obtain long-lived access tokens to use in your API calls.' Create an App doc: 'In the Generate access tokens section click Add account. Click Continue and log in to your Instagram account in the popup window.'

findings.claim: As of late October 2026 Meta no longer offers 'API setup with Instagram login' to newly created apps; the App Dashboard routes new apps using the 'Manage messaging & content on Instagram' use case to 'API setup with Unified login'. Apps created earlier reportedly keep the old setup.
findings.evidence: Dashboard message quoted in Postiz issue #2350 (reported Oct 29-31, 2026): 'API setup with Instagram login is not available for newer apps. Your app uses API setup with Unified login instead.' instaContentHelper PR #29 (merged Nov 3, 2026): 'Meta no longer offers Instagram Login to new apps, and the replacement is API setup with Unified login.' Also: 'The classic Facebook dialog with explicit scopes is refused (Invalid Scopes) for new apps'. Community-reported; no official announcement located.

findings.claim: Unified Login is built on a Facebook Login for Business configuration: the dialog is facebook.com/dialog/oauth with client_id + config_id (config_id replaces scope), response_type=code and override_default_response_type=true; the code is exchanged at graph.facebook.com/vNN/oauth/access_token; with a 'System-user access token' configuration the app receives a Business Integration System User token (requires the user to log in via a business portfolio) which defaults to never expiring; API calls run on graph.facebook.com and the token is rejected by graph.instagram.com.
findings.evidence: Facebook Login for Business doc: 'If you select System-user access token, your app receives a business integration system user access token and your app users are required to log in using a business portfolio. This is only required if this configuration needs continuous access to business assets, such as Facebook Pages, ad accounts or Instagram accounts.' 'config_id has replaced scope (which should not be used), the response_type has been set to code ... override_default_response_type must be set to true.' 'business integration tokens default to never expire for the common offline server-to-server communication.' System-user token guide: two options, non-expiring and expiring (valid for 60 days), 'all integrations should adopt expiring tokens'. Community tests (OpenReply #104, Oct 31-Nov 1, 2026, Graph v26.0): 'The code exchange produces a SYSTEM_USER token with no expiration timestamp'; 'Operational calls use graph.facebook.com'; 'The same token was rejected by graph.instagram.com/me'. roadie #49 quotes the Unified Login overview: returns a 'Business Integration System User' access token that 'keeps working if the person who connected leaves.'

findings.claim: Under Unified Login the connected Instagram account is discovered with GET /me/assigned_instagram_accounts (fallback /me/accounts?fields=instagram_business_account for Page-linked accounts); the publishing endpoints are unchanged (POST /{ig-id}/media -> poll status_code -> POST /{ig-id}/media_publish). Granted permissions use the Facebook-style names (instagram_basic, instagram_content_publish, ...). A reported gotcha: without business_management the assigned-accounts list came back empty and calls failed with code 100 / subcode 33; under Standard Access business_management was silently dropped from the token unless public_profile had Advanced Access.
findings.evidence: WP Scheduled Posts PR #133 (Nov 4, 2026): primary '/me/assigned_instagram_accounts', fallback '/me/accounts?fields=instagram_business_account'; publishing 'POST ... /{ig-id}/media create a container ... polls it until status_code is FINISHED, then calls /media_publish' on graph.facebook.com/v26.0; permissions 'instagram_basic and instagram_content_publish, set in the Login for Business configuration'. OpenReply #104: initial permissions 'instagram_basic, instagram_manage_comments, instagram_content_publish, instagram_manage_messages, public_profile'; 'Before business_management was added, /me/assigned_instagram_accounts returned {"data": []}, and calls on the Instagram account ID failed with 100/33'; 'business_management persisted only when public_profile had Advanced Access. With Standard access, the consent screen listed it but the token dropped it silently.' Postiz #2350: configuration 'Login variation: General ... System-user access token (SUAT), expiration Never ... Business assets: Instagram account (required)'; 'A business portfolio is mandatory'.

findings.claim: In Development mode, people with a role on the app (admin/developer/tester, or an Instagram Tester who accepted the invite) can use the permissions without App Review, which is how a single-business app publishes to the owner's own account; serving other accounts needs Advanced Access.
findings.evidence: Access Levels: Standard Access permissions 'can only be requested from app users who have a role on the requesting app.' roadie #49 (Oct 30, 2026): 'In development mode, people with a role on the app get every permission without App Review.' OpenReply #104: a comment from an account without an app role produced no webhook while one from an Instagram Tester did. Vendor/community guides: add the account under Roles > 'Instagram Testers', then accept in the Instagram app (Settings > Website permissions / 'Apps and Websites' > 'Tester Invites').

findings.claim: Instagram Login tokens: authorization code valid 1 hour and single-use; short-lived Instagram User token valid 1 hour; exchange at GET https://graph.instagram.com/access_token?grant_type=ig_exchange_token for a 60-day long-lived token; refresh at GET https://graph.instagram.com/refresh_access_token?grant_type=ig_refresh_token (token must be at least 24 hours old and unexpired; each refresh gives another 60 days); long-lived exchange must be server-side because it includes the app secret. An expired token cannot be refreshed (one implementer's Instagram Login token expired 2026-10-29).
findings.evidence: Business Login doc: 'Your app can exchanged this short-lived access token for a long-lived Instagram user access token that is valid for 60 days'; 'Requests for long-lived tokens must be made in server-side code. These requesting include your app secret'. Overview: refresh requires the token to be at least 24 hours old, still valid, and basic permission granted. PrenSJ2 gist: authorize https://www.instagram.com/oauth/authorize (api.instagram.com/oauth/authorize also accepted), exchange POST https://api.instagram.com/oauth/access_token grant_type=authorization_code, then ig_exchange_token / ig_refresh_token. shipblu PR #455: the Instagram Login token 'an Instagram User token, sixty days ... expired on 2026-10-29'.

findings.claim: Reels publishing flow: (1) POST /{ig-user-id}/media with media_type=REELS and video_url (a publicly reachable HTTPS URL; no direct file upload), optional caption, cover_url, thumb_offset (ms), share_to_feed (bool), audio_name, location_id, user_tags, collaborators; (2) poll GET /{container-id}?fields=status_code,status until FINISHED; (3) POST /{ig-user-id}/media_publish?creation_id={container-id}; (4) read back GET /{media-id}?fields=permalink,media_product_type. A published reel does not read back as media_type REELS.
findings.evidence: Official guide: a reel container is built 'from the video path passed through the video_url parameter, with media_type=REELS included'; 'To determine if a published video has been designated as a reel, request its media_product_type field instead.' April 2026 gist (citing Meta): container parameters 'media_type=REELS, video_url (required), caption, alt_text, location_id, user_tags, collaborators, cover_url, thumb_offset (ms), share_to_feed (boolean), audio_name'; 'Must be a publicly accessible HTTPS URL. Direct file upload is not supported.' Official media reference: 'Music tagging is only available for original audio'; audio_name applies to Reels only and 'you can rename the audio only once.'

findings.claim: Container status_code values are EXPIRED, ERROR, FINISHED, IN_PROGRESS and PUBLISHED; when status_code is ERROR the status field holds an error subcode; receiving a container id does not mean the video uploaded; unpublished containers expire after 24 hours.
findings.evidence: IG Container reference: 'EXPIRED - The container was not published within 24 hours and has expired.' 'ERROR - The container failed to complete the publishing process.' 'FINISHED - The container and its media object are ready to be published.' 'IN_PROGRESS - The container is still in the publishing process.' 'PUBLISHED - The container's media object has been published.' 'If status_code is ERROR, this value will be an error subcode.' Guide: 'video uploads are asynchronous, so receiving a container ID does not guarantee that the upload was successful. To verify that a video has been uploaded, request the status_code field on the IG Container. If its value is FINISHED, the video was uploaded successfully.'

findings.claim: Meta's recommended polling cadence is once per minute for no more than 5 minutes; publishing before FINISHED returns error code 9007 / subcode 2207027 ('Media is not ready for publishing'), which should be handled by continuing to poll rather than recreating the container.
findings.evidence: Third-party relays of the guide: 'poll once per minute, for no more than 5 minutes' (adaptlypost, postzen). Error mapping (postzen, bundle.social): '9007 / 2207027 | Media is not ready for publishing'; 're-creating the container on a 9007 will queue a second upload for a post that was going to succeed'. Exact official wording not read directly.

findings.claim: Publishing limit: Meta's guide says 100 API-published posts per rolling 24 hours (carousels count as one, enforced on media_publish), but the media_publish reference (updated Jan 21, 2025) and the content_publishing_limit reference say 50; apps should read the live quota from GET /{ig-user-id}/content_publishing_limit?fields=quota_usage,config rather than hardcode it.
findings.evidence: Guide: 'Instagram accounts are limited to 100 API-published posts within a 24-hour moving period. Carousels count as a single post.' 'This limit is enforced on the POST /<IG_ID>/media_publish endpoint when attempting to publish a media container.' media_publish reference: 'An Instagram professional account can only publish 50 posts within a 24 hour moving period.' content_publishing_limit reference: quota_usage = number of IG Containers published since `since` (Unix timestamp no older than 24 hours) or in the last 24 hours; config holds quota_total (50) and quota_duration (86400). Permissions: Instagram Login instagram_business_basic + instagram_business_content_publish; Facebook Login instagram_basic + instagram_content_publish + pages_read_engagement.

findings.claim: General API rate limit: Instagram Platform endpoints (except Business Discovery and Hashtag Search) use Business Use Case rate limiting, counted per app + app-user pair over a rolling 24 hours, with an allowance of 4800 x impressions of the account's content in the last 24 hours.
findings.evidence: Overview: 'all endpoints are subject to Instagram Business Use Case rate limiting except for Business Discovery and Hashtag Search endpoints, which are subject to Platform Rate Limiting.' Rate Limits doc: 'An app's call count is unique for each app and app user pair, and is the number of calls the app has made in a rolling 24 hour window'; calls within 24 hours = 4800 x impressions.

findings.claim: Official Reels video specifications (IG User Media reference): container MOV or MP4 (MPEG-4 Part 14), no edit lists, moov atom at the front; audio AAC, max 48 kHz, mono or stereo, 128 kbps; video HEVC or H.264, progressive scan, closed GOP, 4:2:0 chroma subsampling; frame rate 23-60 FPS; picture size max 1920 columns; aspect ratio between 0.01:1 and 10:1 with 9:16 recommended 'to avoid cropping or blank space'; video bitrate VBR 25 Mbps max; duration 3 seconds minimum to 15 minutes maximum; file size 300 MB maximum; cover photo JPEG, 8 MB max, sRGB, 9:16 recommended. Third-party claims of 1 GB / 90 s / H.264-only are outdated or refer to Reels-tab eligibility.
findings.evidence: Search summary of the official reference: 'MOV or MP4 (MPEG-4 Part 14), with no edit lists and the moov atom at the front of the file'; 'AAC audio at up to 48 kHz, mono or stereo, and HEVC or H264 video, progressive scan, closed GOP, 4:2:0 chroma subsampling'; '23-60 FPS'; 'Maximum columns of 1920 horizontal pixels'; 'aspect ratio runs from 0.01:1 to 10:1 ... recommends 9:16'; 'Variable video bitrate up to 25 Mbps, and audio at 128 kbps'; 'Between 3 seconds and 15 minutes long, with a 300 MB maximum file size'; cover 'JPEG, 8 MB maximum, sRGB color space, with a recommended 9:16 aspect ratio'. Also: 'the media_url field is omitted for video media that contains copyrighted or licensed audio.'

findings.claim: Error behaviour (third-party mappings, consistent across sources, official error-code page not retrievable): 9007/2207027 media not ready (keep polling); 352/2207026 unsupported video format (re-encode to MP4/MOV H.264/HEVC + AAC); -2/2207003 media download timeout (host on fast CDN, retry); 24/2207006 media not found (bad URL, or missing permission/expired token); 25/2207050 account restricted (fix in Instagram app); 4/2207051 spam block (stop publishing for that account; not a rate limit); 9/2207042 publishing cap reached. Official examples seen: 2207073 'Media Type Not Supported', 2207025 'Instagram business user access denied', 2207024 'resource does not exist'. In May 2026 developers saw code 100 / subcode 33 'Authorization Error' when polling new containers (Meta-side issue later reported resolved; treat as transient and retry).
findings.evidence: postzen / bundle.social error tables as summarised: '9007 / 2207027 | Media is not ready for publishing'; '352 / 2207026 ... unsupported'; '-2 / 2207003 ... download timeout'; '25 / 2207050 ... account restricted'; '4 / 2207051 ... behavioural block, not a rate limit'; '9 / 2207042 ... publishing cap'; '24 / 2207006 ... possible permission error due to missing permission or expired token'. Meta IG Media doc example: error_subcode 2207073 'Media Type Not Supported'. Meta developer forum thread (publishing fails for all accounts since May 23, 2026): 'GET /{creation_id}?fields=status_code,status returned Authorization Error (code 100, subcode 33) for newly created containers'; developers 'now treat code 100 / subcode 33 during container polling as a potentially transient error and retry.'

findings.claim: Copyright detection: for an unpublished container you can read copyright_check_status (status completed/error/in_progress/not_started plus matches_found true/false); for published media copyright_check_information lists the rights holder's policy with actions BLOCK or MUTE per geo and matched audio/video segments. Early detection applies only to media created via the content publishing API; documented under the Facebook Login section.
findings.evidence: 'Key-values pairs return include matches_found set to true (the video is violating copyright) or false'; actions 'BLOCK, meaning the video is blocked from the audiences listed in the geos array, or MUTE, meaning the video is muted for audiences listed in the geos array'; 'Early copyright detection is supported only for Instagram media created via the content publishing API.'

findings.claim: 2025-2026 content-publishing changes: Mar 24, 2025 alt_text field for image posts; Dec 3, 2025 Content Publishing API gained Trial Reels (both login types; graduation strategy MANUAL or SS_PERFORMANCE) and a delete endpoint for posts/stories/reels (Facebook Login version only) plus collab-invite endpoints; Basic Display API deprecated Dec 4, 2024; Graph API v26.0 is current per third parties (community tests on v26.0/v27.0).
findings.evidence: Guide: 'on March 24, 2025, we introduced the new alt_text field for image posts on the /<INSTAGRAM_PROFESSIONAL_ACCOUNT_ID>/media endpoint.' Dec 3, 2025 blog: Content Publishing API 'now supports creating Trial Reels, with options for both Facebook and Instagram Login'; new endpoint 'for removing posts, stories, and reels from Instagram accounts linked to a Facebook Page, available through the Facebook Login version'; IG Media delete reference: 'this only works with the Facebook Login version of the API'. Third-party: 'the current Graph API version is v26.0, released on July 29, 2026'.

findings.claim: Music rules: Instagram's licensed music library may be unavailable depending on account type and country/region, and business accounts are steered to Meta Sound Collection (royalty-free music and sound effects: 'over 14,000 music tracks ... and over 1,500 sound effects'); licensed tracks can be muted later when rights agreements change; reels with licensed music cannot be boosted; subscriber-only content may only use Sound Collection or music you own/are authorised to use.
findings.evidence: Help Center: 'The Licensed Music Library isn't available for your account type or in your country or region'; audio issues 'typically occur due to licensing agreements, regional restrictions, or account types'; 'If you don't have access to the licensed music library, then you can add audio from our Sound Collection'; Sound Collection is 'an audio library of sound effects and royalty free music that you can download for your videos.' Boost a reel: 'Reels can't use licensed music. Instead, Instagram recommends using royalty-free music, like what's available in our Sound Collection, or original audio.' Subscriptions: 'you can only use music from Meta's Sound Collection or music that you own and are specifically authorized to use.' Third-party guides consistently state the licensed library is cleared for personal, non-commercial use, which is why business accounts lose it; Meta's business-help article on eligibility could not be read.

findings.claim: Meta Sound Collection licence: non-exclusive, royalty-free, covers commercial and non-commercial use but only inside content published on Meta products (Facebook/Instagram); tracks may not be used separately or on other platforms.
findings.evidence: Sound Collection Terms (as summarised): Meta grants a non-exclusive, royalty-free license covering commercial and non-commercial use 'only inside content published on Meta products'; users 'may not perform, distribute, make available, or otherwise use the audio separately from those products'; third parties: 'you can only use these tracks within Meta products (Instagram, Facebook)'.

findings.claim: The API cannot attach Instagram-library or trending audio to a reel: any music must be mixed into the video file before upload; audio_name only renames the reel's original audio (once). Embedded copyrighted music is subject to copyright detection (mute/block).
findings.evidence: Official reference: 'Music tagging is only available for original audio'; audio_name 'applies to Reels only' and 'you can rename the audio only once.' Upload-Post docs: audio_name 'does not let you pick licensed/trending music from Instagram's library via API'; PostProxy 2026: library tracks, trending sounds and catalogue music 'can't be added via the API, so music must be in the file before upload.' Third-party services (Ayrshare, bundle.social) expose library audio only through their own intermediated access.

findings.claim: After a reel is published (by API or in-app) Instagram does not offer a general 'add music' edit; the only audio change is 'Replace audio' when the reel's audio has been muted ('Audio unavailable' > 'Replace audio', one time, with a track from Instagram's library). A broader Edit > 'Replace Audio' option is reported (c. July 2026) for published feed posts/carousels, not confirmed for reels. Practical workaround is delete/archive and re-upload with the music embedded.
findings.evidence: Help Center 'Replace muted audio on your Instagram reel' (relayed): 'Tap Audio unavailable. Tap Replace audio, then tap Replace audio again'; 'Instagram lets you replace a muted track only one time'; replacement 'must come from Instagram's library'. Help Center Reels page: 'After posting a reel, you can share, save, manage or delete your reel.' 2026 guides: Instagram 'does not let you swap, replace, or add music to a feed post, carousel, or reel after it goes live'; one guide: 'Replace Audio launched around July 2026 for swapping the track on published feed posts and carousels.'

implementation_decision:
Build Studio Assistant's Instagram module as a thin adapter over Meta's official container flow, and target the 2026 "API setup with Unified login" for the owner's brand-new Meta app while keeping a legacy "Instagram Login" switch:

1. Auth adapter with two modes behind one interface (`InstagramAuthProvider`):
   - PRIMARY (new apps, Nov 2026): Unified Login = Facebook Login for Business configuration. Login URL https://www.facebook.com/{vNN}/dialog/oauth?client_id=META_APP_ID&config_id=CONFIG_ID&redirect_uri=...&response_type=code&override_default_response_type=true&state=... (no `scope` param). Exchange the code server-side at https://graph.facebook.com/{vNN}/oauth/access_token (client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, code). Expect a Business Integration System User token; verify with /debug_token (type SYSTEM_USER, expires_at 0 if the configuration is set to "Never"; if 60-day, schedule refresh). Discover the account via GET /me/assigned_instagram_accounts?fields=id,username (fallback GET /me/accounts?fields=instagram_business_account{id,username}); if the list is empty, show the owner the "add business_management to the configuration under Facebook Login for Business > Configurations and reconnect" remediation. All API calls on graph.facebook.com (never graph.instagram.com with this token). Pin one Graph version (v26.0 today) in config.
   - FALLBACK (if the owner's app still has "API setup with Instagram login"): https://www.instagram.com/oauth/authorize with scope=instagram_business_basic,instagram_business_content_publish; exchange at api.instagram.com/oauth/access_token; upgrade with graph.instagram.com/access_token?grant_type=ig_exchange_token; refresh weekly via refresh_access_token?grant_type=ig_refresh_token (token must be >24 h old); alert the owner 7 days before expiry; all calls on graph.instagram.com.
   - Keep the Meta app in Development mode with Standard Access: only the owner (app admin / Instagram Tester, business-portfolio admin) connects, so no App Review and no Business Verification. Do not build a public connect flow.

2. Publishing pipeline (idempotent job per reel, states: rendered -> uploaded -> container_created -> processing -> ready -> publishing -> published | failed | expired):
   - Pre-flight: GET /{ig-id}/content_publishing_limit?fields=quota_usage,config and block when quota_usage >= config.quota_total (plan around 50 even though the guide says 100; show remaining quota in the UI).
   - Host the rendered MP4 (and optional JPEG cover) at a publicly reachable HTTPS URL (object storage with a time-limited signed URL valid at least 2 hours; no auth cookies, correct Content-Type, HTTP 200, Range support).
   - POST /{ig-id}/media with media_type=REELS, video_url, caption (<=2,200 chars, <=30 hashtags), share_to_feed=true by default, optional cover_url or thumb_offset (ms), optional audio_name only when the audio is the shop's own original audio; never claim to attach Instagram library music.
   - Poll GET /{container}?fields=status_code,status,copyright_check_status every 60 s for 5 minutes, then back off to every 5 minutes for up to 24 h (container lifetime); treat IN_PROGRESS as waiting; on FINISHED check copyright_check_status.matches_found and warn the owner before publishing; on ERROR map `status` subcode (2207026 unsupported format -> re-encode; 2207003 download timeout -> retry with fresh URL; 2207050/2207051 -> stop and explain) ; on EXPIRED create a new container.
   - POST /{ig-id}/media_publish?creation_id=...; on 9007/2207027 keep polling (do not recreate); on 9/2207042 quota reached -> queue for next window; on code 100 subcode 33 during polling -> retry with backoff. Then GET /{media-id}?fields=id,permalink,media_product_type and store the permalink.
   - Encode with FFmpeg to the official spec before upload: 1080x1920 (9:16), H.264 High profile yuv420p progressive, closed GOP (e.g. -g 60 -keyint_min 60 -sc_threshold 0), 30 fps (23-60 allowed), VBR <= 25 Mbps (target 8-12 Mbps), AAC 48 kHz 128 kbps stereo, MP4 with -movflags +faststart and no edit lists, duration 3 s-15 min (recommend 15-90 s), file <= 300 MB; validate with ffprobe and refuse to upload otherwise.

3. Music policy in the product: only (a) the shop's own/original audio, (b) tracks the owner holds a commercial licence for, or (c) Meta Sound Collection downloads (allowed only for content that stays on Meta products, so do not reuse those renders on TikTok/YouTube) may be mixed into a reel destined for the API. The UI must state plainly that Instagram library/trending audio cannot be added by the API and cannot be added in the Instagram app after publishing (only "Replace audio" if a track gets muted); offer an "Export for manual posting" path (download the MP4 + copy caption) when the owner wants Instagram-library music, since a Business account in Australia may not even see the licensed library.

4. Honest states and observability: surface quota, token health (type/expiry), container status, copyright match warnings, and Meta error codes verbatim (error_user_msg) in the owner's dashboard; log Graph version and request ids; one retry policy for transient errors, none for policy errors.
account_requirements: Instagram professional account for the barber shop (Business or Creator). Business is recommended; Stories publishing via API is Business-only, and the shop's commercial use already disqualifies the personal licensed music library in practice.

A Meta developer account (Facebook login) and a new Meta app of type Business with the use case 'Manage messaging & content on Instagram'. Expect the dashboard to say 'API setup with Instagram login is not available for newer apps. Your app uses API setup with Unified login instead.'

A Meta business portfolio (Business Manager / Meta Business Suite) that owns or has claimed the Instagram account; the app must be connected to that portfolio. The owner must be an admin of the portfolio and must log in through it during the Unified Login flow (System-user access token configurations require business-portfolio login). No Business Verification is needed while the app stays at Standard Access for the owner's own account.

Facebook Login for Business product + one configuration: Login variation General; Access token = System-user access token; Expiration 'Never' (or 60 days with scheduled refresh); Business assets = Instagram account (ad account optional); Permissions at least instagram_basic and instagram_content_publish (add instagram_manage_insights / instagram_manage_comments if those modules are wanted); add business_management via Facebook Login for Business > Configurations if /me/assigned_instagram_accounts returns empty (community-reported gotcha). Record the config_id and a valid HTTPS OAuth redirect URI.

App settings required before login works: Privacy Policy URL, User Data Deletion callback/URL, App Domains, and (for Instagram-Login-style setups) deauthorize and data-deletion callback URLs; keep the app in Development mode.

App roles: the owner (and any staff who will connect) must be an Admin/Developer/Tester on the app and, if the dashboard shows the Instagram Testers section, must be added as an Instagram Tester and accept the invite in the Instagram app (Settings > Website permissions / Apps and websites > Tester invites). Standard Access only covers people with a role on the app.

No Facebook Page is required for Unified Login or Instagram Login. If the Instagram account is already linked to a Facebook Page, the owner must be able to perform admin-equivalent tasks on that Page and must complete Page Publishing Authorization if Meta prompts for it, or publishing is blocked.

App Review / Advanced Access is NOT required while the app publishes only to Instagram accounts the owner owns/manages and connected via role holders. If Studio Assistant is ever offered to other barbers, Meta requires App Review with screen recordings per permission plus Business Verification, and the app must be Live.
Publicly reachable HTTPS hosting for rendered videos and cover images (object storage with signed URLs), since the API fetches video_url itself and does not accept file uploads.

Music: a documented source for every track mixed into API-published reels: the shop's original audio, tracks the owner has a commercial sync licence for, or Meta Sound Collection downloads (Meta-products-only licence). Instagram library/trending audio is unavailable via API and cannot be added after publishing.

Operational: respect the per-account publishing quota (read content_publishing_limit; 50 vs 100 per rolling 24 h is inconsistent in Meta's docs), keep the Graph API version pinned and reviewed quarterly, and monitor token health (SUAT 'Never' vs 60-day expiry; Instagram Login tokens must be refreshed before 60 days).
uncertainties: No official Meta page could be read directly: developers.facebook.com, developers.secure.facebook.com, help.instagram.com, www.facebook.com, web.archive.org and r.jina.ai all failed in this sandbox. Every 'official' quote above comes from search-engine snippets of Meta pages, cross-checked against third-party mirrors; wording and current values should be re-verified against the live docs once those hosts are allowed.

The 2026 'Unified Login' change is documented here mainly from community sources (GitHub issues/PRs dated Oct 29 - Nov 7, 2026) plus Meta's Sep 16, 2026 landing page and the Facebook Login for Business docs. The official 'Instagram API with Unified Login' page (developers.facebook.com/documentation/instagram-platform/instagram-api-with-unified-login/) was not readable; exact permission names offered in its configuration editor, token default expiry, Standard-Access behaviour for role holders, and whether copyright_check_status is exposed under it are unconfirmed.

Whether existing apps created before late Oct 2026 keep 'API setup with Instagram login' indefinitely, and whether Meta has labelled the Facebook Login setup 'legacy', is based on single community reports.

Publishing quota: Meta's guide says 100 API-published posts per rolling 24 h; the media_publish reference (updated Jan 21, 2025) and content_publishing_limit reference say 50. Which value the API enforces for a given account is unknown; the live quota_total should be read at runtime.

Permission spelling: Meta pages show both 'instagram_business_content_publish' (content publishing guide, Business Login doc, limit reference) and 'instagram_business_content_publishing' (App Review page). The former appears to be the real scope value, but the dashboard should be treated as authoritative.

The 'once per minute, for no more than 5 minutes' polling guidance and the 'publicly accessible server' requirement for video_url were only seen via third-party relays of the guide, not in a Meta snippet.

Error-code meanings (2207026, 2207003, 2207006, 2207050, 2207051, 2207042, 9007/2207027) come from consistent third-party tables; Meta's own error-codes reference page could not be retrieved. One third party (Zernio) lists 2207027 as 'Unknown error', so treat mappings as advisory.
Reels video specification values were taken from a search summary of the IG User Media reference indexed around Mar 2025; changes since then (e.g. to the 300 MB cap or duration) would not be visible.

Music: Meta's Business Help article 'Access to the licensed music library on Instagram' (facebook.com/business/help/402084904469945) could not be read, so the precise eligibility rule for Business vs Creator accounts, and its application in Australia, is unverified; the '14,000 tracks / 1,500 effects' Sound Collection counts are from a Jul 2025 Meta page and may have changed.

Post-publish audio editing: the 'Replace audio' behaviour for muted reels is from Help Center snippets relayed by third parties; reports of a broader Edit > 'Replace Audio' option for feed posts/carousels (c. Jul 2026) are unverified and were not confirmed for reels.

Token lifetime for Business Integration System User tokens under Unified Login: Facebook Login for Business docs say such tokens 'default to never expire', while the system-user guide recommends 60-day expiring tokens; the actual default in the Unified Login configuration editor was not read directly.
Current Graph API version (v26.0, released Jul 29, 2026 per third parties; community tests also mention v27.0) was not confirmed from Meta's changelog.
No Australia-specific Instagram API or music-licensing rules were found; regional availability of the licensed music library is acknowledged by Meta but not specified per country.

findings.claim: The Bookings API is available to Australian sellers (Australia was in the GA launch set and the AU pricing page lists the Bookings API as a plan feature), but Square says it is 'limited in international locales' without enumerating AU-specific limits.
findings.evidence: GA blog (12 May 2022): "developers in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, Spain, and Japan can access the API". AU pricing page lists "Bookings API (write access)" under the Plus label: "The app can create, update or cancel every booking of a seller. A seller is granted this permission through a paid subscription plan." Concepts page: "The Bookings API is limited in international locales. For supported international locales, see Square Appointments FAQs." A 2026 forum thread from an Australian barbershop shows the API in active use in AU.

findings.claim: Seller-level create/update/cancel via API requires an active or trial Appointments Plus or Premium subscription; without it those calls return 403. Reads (and buyer-level writes) work on the Free plan.
findings.evidence: Official spec text on CreateBooking, UpdateBooking, CancelBooking (and booking custom-attribute writes): "For calls to this endpoint with seller-level permissions to succeed, the seller must have subscribed to *Appointments Plus* or *Appointments Premium*." Read endpoints (ListBookings, RetrieveBooking, BulkRetrieveBookings, SearchAvailability, profiles) carry no plan requirement. Concepts page: "When a seller doesn't have the Appointments Plus or Premium subscription plan, all the API calls targeted at the seller with buyer-level permissions and those with seller-level readable permissions succeed. However, API calls targeted at the seller with seller-level writeable permissions fail with a 403 response." Onboarding page: "In the production environment, each seller using your application must also have an active or trial Appointments Plus or Appointments Premium subscription to create, update, or cancel seller-level bookings." Overview: "With the free subscription plan, you can call the Bookings API to create, update or cancel buyer-level bookings with the seller."

findings.claim: The app can detect at runtime whether seller-level writes are allowed via BusinessBookingProfile.support_seller_level_writes.
findings.evidence: Spec: BusinessBookingProfile.support_seller_level_writes (boolean): "Indicates whether the seller's subscription to Square Appointments supports creating, updating or canceling an appointment through the API (`true`) or not (`false`) using seller permission." Docs: "call RetrieveBusinessBookingProfile and inspect the response for the support_seller_level_writes attribute. Only when the returned value is true can you proceed successfully to create, update, or cancel seller-level bookings."

findings.claim: Seller-level bookings are created as ACCEPTED; buyer-level bookings start PENDING. Buyer-level apps only see/affect bookings they created.
findings.evidence: Create and Manage Bookings: "A booking created with seller-level permissions is always deemed as accepted. When created, the booking status is automatically set to ACCEPTED. This is different from the booking created with buyer-level permissions, where the booking status is set to PENDING. Only when the seller accepts or declines the pending booking, does the booking status change from PENDING to ACCEPTED or DECLINED, respectively." Overview (buyer-level): "an application must create a booking to get event notifications about changes to a booking". Spec scope text: APPOINTMENTS_ALL_READ "Grants read access to all of a seller's booking information, calendar, and business details."

findings.claim: OAuth scope semantics (exact official descriptions from the spec's securitySchemes).
findings.evidence: APPOINTMENTS_READ: "__HTTP Method__: `GET`, `POST` Grants read access to booking information. For example, to call the RetrieveBooking endpoint." APPOINTMENTS_WRITE: "__HTTP Method__: `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE` Grants write access to booking information. For example, to call the CreateBooking endpoint." APPOINTMENTS_ALL_READ: "Grants read access to all of a seller's booking information, calendar, and business details. This permission must be accompanied by the `APPOINTMENTS_READ` permission." APPOINTMENTS_ALL_WRITE: "Grants write access to all booking details, including double-booking a seller. This permission must be accompanied by the `APPOINTMENTS_WRITE` permission." APPOINTMENTS_BUSINESS_SETTINGS_READ: "Grants read access to booking business settings. For example, to call the ListTeamMemberBookingProfiles endpoint." (search summary adds RetrieveBusinessBookingProfile requires it). CUSTOMERS_READ: "Grants read access to customer information. For example, to call the ListCustomers endpoint." CUSTOMERS_WRITE: "Grants write access to customer information. For example, to create and update customer profiles." Per-endpoint text: reads need APPOINTMENTS_READ (buyer) or APPOINTMENTS_ALL_READ + APPOINTMENTS_READ (seller); writes need APPOINTMENTS_WRITE (buyer) or APPOINTMENTS_ALL_WRITE + APPOINTMENTS_WRITE (seller). Webhook scopes in spec: payment.* → PAYMENTS_READ; customer.* → CUSTOMERS_READ; order.* → ORDERS_READ.

findings.claim: Key Bookings endpoints and constraints (current spec, Square-Version 2026-09-16).
findings.evidence: GET /v2/bookings ListBookings — query params limit, cursor, customer_id, team_member_id, location_id, start_at_min ("If this is not set, the current time is used"), start_at_max ("If this is not set, the time of 31 days after `start_at_min` is used"). POST /v2/bookings CreateBooking — required: "`Booking.location_id` - `Booking.start_at` - `Booking.AppointmentSegment.team_member_id` - `Booking.AppointmentSegment.service_variation_id` - `Booking.AppointmentSegment.service_variation_version`". POST /v2/bookings/availability/search SearchAvailability — "The time range must be at least 24 hours and at most 32 days long"; filter.booking_id "is commonly used to reschedule an appointment" (cannot combine with location_id/segment_filters). POST /v2/bookings/bulk-retrieve. GET /v2/bookings/business-booking-profile RetrieveBusinessBookingProfile. GET /v2/bookings/location-booking-profiles (+/{location_id}). GET /v2/bookings/team-member-booking-profiles (+/{team_member_id}, +/bulk-retrieve). GET/PUT /v2/bookings/{booking_id} Retrieve/UpdateBooking ("Individual attributes explicitly specified here override the corresponding values of the existing booking"). POST /v2/bookings/{booking_id}/cancel CancelBooking (body: idempotency_key, booking_version "The revision number for the booking used for optimistic concurrency"). Booking.location_id: "Once set when the booking is created, its value cannot be changed." Booking custom attributes endpoints also exist (writes plan-gated).

findings.claim: Booking status values and the fact that status is read-only through the API (so NO_SHOW cannot be set by the app).
findings.evidence: Spec BookingStatus: PENDING "An unaccepted booking. It is visible to both sellers and customers."; CANCELLED_BY_CUSTOMER "A customer-cancelled booking. It is visible to both the seller and the customer."; CANCELLED_BY_SELLER "A seller-cancelled booking. It is visible to both the seller and the customer."; DECLINED "A declined booking. It had once been pending, but was then declined by the seller."; ACCEPTED "An accepted booking agreed to or accepted by the seller."; NO_SHOW "A no-show booking. The booking was accepted at one time, but have now been marked as a no-show by the seller because the client either missed the booking or cancelled it without enough notice." Booking.status is readOnly: true in the spec ("The status of the booking, describing where the booking stands with respect to the booking state machine"). Also read-only: id, created_at, updated_at, transition_time_minutes, all_day, creator_details, source. Booking.source enum: FIRST_PARTY_MERCHANT, FIRST_PARTY_BUYER, THIRD_PARTY_BUYER, API — "Access to this field requires seller-level permissions."

findings.claim: Webhook events relevant to Studio Assistant and their scopes; seller-level delivery needs APPOINTMENTS_ALL_READ too; events can be missed so reconcile by polling.
findings.evidence: Spec x-webhook: booking.created scopes [APPOINTMENTS_READ], booking.updated scopes [APPOINTMENTS_READ] (both PUBLIC, since 2020-12-16); payment.created / payment.updated → [PAYMENTS_READ]; customer.created / customer.updated / customer.deleted → [CUSTOMERS_READ]; order.created / order.updated / order.fulfillment.updated → [ORDERS_READ] (marked BETA). Payload: merchant_id ("The ID of the target seller associated with the event"), location_id, type ("The value is `\"booking.created\"`"), event_id ("A unique ID for the event"), created_at, data.type "booking", data.id, data.object.booking. Docs: "To receive this event with seller-level permissions, you must have APPOINTMENTS_ALL_READ and APPOINTMENTS_READ set for the OAuth scope." A forum thread reports "Webhook booking.created events are missing for some appointments"; Square's advice was to hold both scopes to get events for Dashboard/POS-created bookings.

findings.claim: Webhook signature verification: header x-square-hmacsha256-signature = base64(HMAC-SHA256(key, notificationUrl + rawBody)); the SDK helper is WebhooksHelper.verifySignature and it is async.
findings.evidence: SDK source WebhooksHelper.ts: params "requestBody — The JSON body of the request", "signatureHeader — The value for the `x-square-hmacsha256-signature` header", "signatureKey — The signature key from the Square Developer portal for the webhook subscription", "notificationUrl — The notification endpoint URL as defined in the Square Developer portal for the webhook subscription"; implementation: `const payload = notificationUrl + requestBody; const hashBase64 = await createHmacOverride(payload, signatureKey); return hashBase64 === signatureHeader;` declared `static async verifySignature(...): Promise<boolean>`. createHmacOverride.ts: `crypto.createHmac("sha256", key); hmac.update(payload, "utf8"); return hmac.digest("base64");`. README: `import { WebhooksHelper } from "square"; const isValid = WebhooksHelper.verifySignature({ requestBody, signatureHeader: request.headers['x-square-hmacsha256-signature'], signatureKey: "YOUR_SIGNATURE_KEY", notificationUrl: "https://example.com/webhook" });` (README omits `await`; the method returns a Promise). index.ts: `export { WebhooksHelper } from "./wrapper/WebhooksHelper";`

findings.claim: Sandbox supports the Bookings API once the sandbox test account is onboarded to Square Appointments; Plus/Premium can be subscribed in sandbox with a test card at no cost.
findings.evidence: Onboarding page: "To use the Bookings API and test your application built on the API, the Square Appointments services must be activated for targeted Square seller accounts." For sandbox: open the Sandbox Dashboard from the Developer Console's Sandbox Test Accounts section and "Follow steps 2–9 in Onboard a Production account to finish onboarding the Sandbox account." "The following procedure describes how to subscribe your default test account to Appointments Plus or Appointments Premium using a test credit card that is never charged." Official sample README: "The appointments service is free in the Sandbox environment and may incur service charges in the Production environment." and "Note that use of the Sandbox environment is always free of charge." Webhooks docs: sandbox testing uses the Developer Console test-event feature, and creating/updating a booking in the sandbox account triggers real events. Spec/SDK sandbox base URL: https://connect.squareupsandbox.com (SquareEnvironment.Sandbox).

findings.claim: Current Node SDK: npm package `square` v46.0.0 (published 2026-09-15, Node >= 18), Fern-generated `SquareClient` with `token` and `environment`; legacy client available as `square/legacy`.
findings.evidence: npm registry: latest 46.0.0 published 2026-09-15T21:05:48Z; engines node >=18.0.0; 43.0.0 2025-06-18; 44.0.0 2026-01-22. Release note 46.0.0: "This release of the nodejs SDK includes support for Square API version 2026-09-16." README: `import { SquareClient, SquareEnvironment } from "square"; const client = new SquareClient({ token: process.env.SQUARE_ACCESS_TOKEN, environment: SquareEnvironment.Production });` BaseClient options: `environment?`, `baseUrl?`, `version?: "2026-09-16"`, `headers?`; default header `"Square-Version": options?.version ?? "2026-09-16"`. Legacy: "the new SDK also exports the legacy SDK as `square/legacy`" — `import { Client } from "square/legacy"; new Client({ bearerAuthCredentials: { accessToken } })`; migration: "Upgrade the NPM module to `^40.0.0` or later". Bookings methods in SDK: client.bookings.list / create / searchAvailability / bulkRetrieveBookings / getBusinessProfile / retrieveLocationBookingProfile / bulkRetrieveTeamMemberBookingProfiles / get / update / cancel; client.bookings.teamMemberProfiles.list/get; client.bookings.locationProfiles.list; client.bookings.customAttributes.*; client.bookings.customAttributeDefinitions.*.

findings.claim: Catalog model for services: items of product_type APPOINTMENTS_SERVICE with variations carrying service_duration (ms), available_for_booking and team_member_ids; services with a non-zero no-show fee cannot be booked via the API, and the fee is not settable (nor, in the current spec, readable) via API.
findings.evidence: Spec CatalogItemProductType.APPOINTMENTS_SERVICE: "A service that can be booked using the Square Appointments app." and "Connect V2 only allows the creation of `REGULAR` or `APPOINTMENTS_SERVICE` items." CatalogItemVariation.service_duration: "...duration of the service in milliseconds. For example, a 30 minute appointment would have the value `1800000`"; available_for_booking: "a bool representing whether this service is available for booking"; team_member_ids: "Tokens of employees that can perform the service represented by this variation. Only valid for variations of type `APPOINTMENTS_SERVICE`." Docs: "You cannot use the Bookings API to book a service that has a non-zero cancellation fee set on its no_show_fee attribute. The non-zero cancellation fee is set in the Square Dashboard. It cannot be set using the Bookings API." Note: no `no_show_fee` property exists on CatalogItemVariation in the current public spec; BusinessAppointmentSettings.cancellation_fee_money ("The flat-fee amount charged for a no-show booking") is the business-level setting exposed.

findings.claim: There is no API linkage between a booking and its payment/order; 'the appointment happened and was paid' can only be inferred heuristically. Square has no COMPLETED booking status.
findings.evidence: Spec grep: no Order*, Payment*, Tender*, Checkout* or Invoice* schema has any property referencing a booking or appointment. Only indirect signals exist: CustomerCreationSource.APPOINTMENTS ("The customer profile was created automatically when an appointment was scheduled") and ApplicationDetails.square_product enum value APPOINTMENTS ("The Square product, such as Square Point of Sale (POS), Square Invoices..."), Payment.order_id, Payment.customer_id, Payment.team_member_id, Order.customer_id, OrderLineItem.catalog_object_id ("The CatalogItemVariation ID applied to this line item"). Forum (Square staff): "with the APIs there isn't a way to map a booking to the payment or order" and "Nor is it possible to map the payment or order to the booking." Developers "infer the relationship by matching on three signals: customer ID, service variation ID against order line items, and timing"; one found a matcher "only accurate 80% of the time". BookingStatus has no completed/attended value; an ACCEPTED booking remains ACCEPTED after its start time unless the seller marks NO_SHOW or cancels.

findings.claim: Australian plan pricing/features (per Square's AU pricing page via search summary): Free A$0, Plus A$40/mo per location, Premium A$90/mo per location; Bookings API write access and no-show protection sit in Plus; Free has no staff limit.
findings.evidence: AU pricing page: "$0/mo. for a single location" (Free), "$40/mo. per location" (Plus), "$90/mo. per location" (Premium); Free lists unlimited staff accounts ("There is no employee limit"); Plus adds "customer confirmation texts and emails, cancellation policy and fees, class scheduling, waitlist, and appointments reports" and "Bookings API (write access)"; Premium adds "resource management, custom staff commissions"; "free 30-day trial", no contract; AU FAQ: plans are "on a per-location basis". US pages show US$49/US$149 — not AU prices.

findings.claim: 2025–2026 changes: no Bookings API schema/endpoint changes were found; plan names unchanged; the SDK moved to the Fern-generated client (v40+ with square/legacy shim) and now tracks monthly API versions.
findings.evidence: Spec: no booking/appointment/availability-related schema or property carries an x-since >= 2024-06 (coverage of x-since is incomplete). Forum (Aug 2026): "the last Bookings API update in the Square API changelog was September 2024"; Square staff reply: they are "continuing development on the Bookings API"; the thread lists gaps ("customer confirmations, personal events, schedule changes, recurring appointments"). Last concrete Bookings changelog found: 2024-04-17 "UpdateBooking endpoint - Disallows updates of a booking's appointment segments after a deposit is made for the booking."; the release index lists Bookings API under 2024-09-19/2024-10-17 (details not retrieved). SDK: 43.0.0 (2025-06-18) → 44.0.0 (2026-01-22) → 46.0.0 (2026-09-15, API 2026-09-16).

findings.claim: Seller profile/settings available read-only to drive UI: booking policy, cancellation window/fee, lead times, bookable team members, online booking site URL.
findings.evidence: Spec BusinessBookingProfile: booking_enabled; booking_policy ("ACCEPT_ALL" / "REQUIRES_ACCEPTANCE"); allow_user_cancel; business_appointment_settings { min_booking_lead_time_seconds, max_booking_lead_time_seconds, cancellation_window_seconds ("The cut-off time in seconds for allowing clients to cancel or reschedule an appointment"), cancellation_fee_money, cancellation_policy, cancellation_policy_text, any_team_member_booking_enabled, multiple_service_booking_enabled }. TeamMemberBookingProfile.is_bookable: "Indicates whether the team member can be booked through the Bookings API or the seller's online booking channel or site". LocationBookingProfile: booking_site_url ("Url for the online booking site for this location"), online_booking_enabled.

implementation_decision:
Build the Square module in two capability tiers and gate the second at runtime.

TIER 0 — implement now; works on Square Appointments Free (and any plan):
- Auth: single-seller private app. Store the owner's Square production access token (or OAuth token) server-side; use `square@^46.0.0` (Node >= 18): `new SquareClient({ token, environment: SquareEnvironment.Production | Sandbox })`; leave Square-Version at the SDK default (2026-09-16) and pin only if a response shape changes.
- Reads (scopes APPOINTMENTS_READ + APPOINTMENTS_ALL_READ + APPOINTMENTS_BUSINESS_SETTINGS_READ + CUSTOMERS_READ + ITEMS_READ + MERCHANT_PROFILE_READ + PAYMENTS_READ + ORDERS_READ): `bookings.list` in <=31-day windows with cursor pagination (poll every 5–15 min, plus a nightly reconciliation of the past/next 31 days); `bookings.get`/`bulkRetrieveBookings`; `bookings.searchAvailability` (24h–32-day ranges; use `booking_id` filter for reschedule previews); `bookings.getBusinessProfile` (cache `support_seller_level_writes`, `booking_policy`, cancellation settings); `bookings.teamMemberProfiles.list` (filter `is_bookable`); `bookings.locationProfiles.list` (show `booking_site_url`); Catalog search for `product_type = APPOINTMENTS_SERVICE` with `service_duration`, `available_for_booking`, `team_member_ids`; Customers retrieve/search for names; Payments/Orders list for the attendance heuristic.
- Webhooks: one subscription for booking.created, booking.updated, payment.created, payment.updated, customer.created/updated/deleted. Verify with `await WebhooksHelper.verifySignature({ requestBody: rawBodyString, signatureHeader: req.headers['x-square-hmacsha256-signature'], signatureKey, notificationUrl })` using the raw body (no JSON.parse first) and the exact notification URL configured in the Developer Console (watch trailing slashes); dedupe on `event_id`; treat each event as a trigger to re-fetch the booking (authoritative), never as the sole source of truth (missed booking.created events are reported).
- Status model: mirror Square's six statuses verbatim and derive local views: Upcoming (ACCEPTED, start_at in future), Needs action (PENDING), Cancelled (CANCELLED_BY_CUSTOMER / CANCELLED_BY_SELLER / DECLINED), No-show (NO_SHOW), Past (ACCEPTED with start_at + duration in the past). Never present "completed" as a Square fact.
- "Did it happen / was it paid?" heuristic (clearly labelled as inferred): for a Past booking, look for a COMPLETED Payment at the same location within [start_at − 30 min, start_at + duration + ~3 h] whose `customer_id` matches, preferring payments whose `application_details.square_product == 'APPOINTMENTS'` and whose Order line items include `catalog_object_id == appointment_segments[].service_variation_id`; score by matches (customer, service, team_member_id, time). Expose states: Attended & paid (match found), Attended – no payment matched, No-show (NO_SHOW), Cancelled. Let the owner confirm/override locally and persist the owner's override.

TIER 1 — implement behind a runtime gate (requires Appointments Plus or Premium; scopes APPOINTMENTS_WRITE + APPOINTMENTS_ALL_WRITE, plus CUSTOMERS_WRITE if the app creates customers):
- Enable Create/Reschedule/Cancel UI only when `getBusinessProfile().support_seller_level_writes === true`; on a 403 from a write, flip the module to read-only and explain that a paid Appointments plan is required.
- `bookings.create` (seller-level → booking is ACCEPTED immediately; supply idempotency_key, location_id, start_at, customer_id, appointment_segments[{ team_member_id, service_variation_id, service_variation_version, duration_minutes }]); `bookings.update` for reschedule (send `version`; use searchAvailability with `booking_id` first); `bookings.cancel` with `booking_version`.
- Known hard limits to surface in UI: (a) the API cannot mark NO_SHOW or otherwise change `status` — the owner must do that in Square Appointments; (b) services carrying a non-zero no-show fee cannot be booked through the API — if the owner uses Plus no-show protection on a service, API booking for that service will fail, so either keep those bookings in Square's own channels or keep fee-free variations for staff-made bookings; (c) deposits/payments cannot be attached to a booking via API.

DO NOT build buyer-level writes (APPOINTMENTS_WRITE alone) for the staff tool: they create PENDING "customer" bookings and the app only sees its own bookings. (This is the only Free-plan write path and could later back a customer-facing widget.)

Testing: use the sandbox (connect.squareupsandbox.com); onboard the default sandbox test account to Appointments in the Sandbox Dashboard, seed APPOINTMENTS_SERVICE items and bookable team members, optionally subscribe the sandbox account to Appointments Plus with a test card (never charged) to exercise Tier 1, and use Developer Console test events plus real sandbox booking changes for webhooks.
account_requirements: Square seller account in Australia with Square Appointments activated (one-time in Square Dashboard). The Free plan (A$0, unlimited staff per AU pricing page) is enough for Tier 0 reads + webhooks.

For Tier 1 seller-level create/update/cancel via API: an active or trial Square Appointments Plus (A$40/mo per location, AU) or Premium (A$90/mo per location, AU) subscription; confirm with RetrieveBusinessBookingProfile.support_seller_level_writes === true. Without it, seller-level writes return 403.

Square Developer account and an application in the Developer Console; for the owner's own account use the app's production access token (or complete OAuth with scopes: APPOINTMENTS_READ, APPOINTMENTS_ALL_READ, APPOINTMENTS_BUSINESS_SETTINGS_READ, CUSTOMERS_READ, ITEMS_READ, MERCHANT_PROFILE_READ, PAYMENTS_READ, ORDERS_READ; add APPOINTMENTS_WRITE + APPOINTMENTS_ALL_WRITE for Tier 1 and CUSTOMERS_WRITE if creating customers). APPOINTMENTS_ALL_* must be accompanied by APPOINTMENTS_READ/WRITE respectively.

Webhook subscription in the Developer Console pointing to a public HTTPS notification URL of Studio Assistant, subscribed to booking.created, booking.updated, payment.created, payment.updated, customer.created/updated/deleted; store the subscription's signature key as a secret; the notification URL string used for verification must exactly match the one configured.

No Square App Marketplace listing or app review is needed for a private, single-seller integration used only by the owner's own account (standard Square practice; not re-verified this session because the docs host was blocked).

Catalog hygiene in Square: services must be APPOINTMENTS_SERVICE items with variations having service_duration, available_for_booking = true and team_member_ids; team members must exist in Square Team and be bookable (TeamMemberBookingProfile.is_bookable). Services with a non-zero no-show fee cannot be booked via the API.

Sandbox for development: default sandbox test account onboarded to Square Appointments via the Sandbox Dashboard; optional sandbox Appointments Plus/Premium subscription with a test card (sandbox is free of charge).
Runtime: Node.js >= 18 and the `square` npm package v46.x (API version 2026-09-16); raw-body capture on the webhook route for signature verification.
uncertainties: developer.squareup.com, squareup.com and dev.to could not be fetched in this sandbox (DNS not allowed). API mechanics (scopes, plan-gating text, endpoints, statuses, webhook scopes, signature algorithm, SDK) were verified from the official OpenAPI spec (Square-Version 2026-09-16) and SDK 46.0.0 source read in full; docs-page wording and all pricing/plan/sandbox-procedure details come from search summaries of official pages and could be stale.

AU pricing (Free A$0 / Plus A$40 / Premium A$90 per location) is from a search summary of squareup.com/au/en/appointments/pricing whose page metadata the search engine flagged as old; confirm on the live AU pricing page before quoting the owner. US pricing (US$49/US$149) differs.

Whether the 2024-09-19 and 2024-10-17 changelog entries changed Bookings behaviour was not retrieved; the Aug 2026 forum thread says the last Bookings changelog entry was September 2024 and no 2025–2026 Bookings changes were found.

The official step3validate page was not read; the verification algorithm (base64 HMAC-SHA256 over notificationUrl + raw body) is taken from the official SDK implementation. The SDK compares with `===` (not constant-time) and the README example omits `await` although verifySignature is async.

Which status CancelBooking produces at each permission level (CANCELLED_BY_SELLER vs CANCELLED_BY_CUSTOMER) was not verified, and the search summary reported an internal inconsistency on the 'Create and Manage Bookings' page about whether seller-level cancel applies to ACCEPTED only or PENDING-or-ACCEPTED bookings.

The docs reference a `no_show_fee` attribute on services, but the current public spec exposes no such property on CatalogItemVariation, so the app cannot pre-detect fee-bearing services; the exact error code returned by CreateBooking for such services is unknown.

Using the Developer Console production access token (instead of OAuth) for the owner's own account, and the absence of any app-review requirement for a private app, follow standard Square practice but were not re-verified in this session.

'The Bookings API is limited in international locales' — the specific Australian limitations are not enumerated in any source found; the 2026 Australian barbershop forum thread suggests the API works in AU apart from the no-show-fee restriction.
Spec x-since coverage is incomplete (e.g. Booking.status and support_seller_level_writes carry no x-since), so 'no booking schema additions since mid-2024' is weak evidence.
order.* webhooks are marked BETA in the spec; payment.* and booking.* are PUBLIC.
Reports of missing booking.created webhook events are from a community thread; the frequency is unknown, hence the recommendation to reconcile by polling.
