findings.claim: Programmatic access to Business Profile data is gated: a new Cloud project has 0 QPM quota until Google approves an access application; approval shows as 300 QPM.
findings.evidence: Prereqs/FAQ: "If your quota is 0 QPM (Queries Per Minute), your project has not yet been approved. If your quota is set to 300 QPM, your project is approved." and "if your quota limit for the Google Business Profile API is 0, you have not yet been granted access. Don't request a quota increase. Instead, submit the Application For Basic API Access." Approved projects get "a standard default quota for all seven APIs" (300 QPM for most). Access is at Cloud-project level and the authorizing user must still have access to each profile; the APIs are free.

findings.claim: Eligibility and application steps: verified profile active 60+ days, a website for the listed business, a Google Cloud project; submit the GBP API contact form choosing 'Application for Basic API Access' with the project number; reviewed within ~14 days.
findings.evidence: Prereqs page (per summary): applicants must "manage a Google Business Profile that is verified and active for 60+ days" and "have a website representing the business listed on the GBP"; "Select the project in the Cloud Console, find its project number on the dashboard, and submit through the GBP API contact form, choosing the 'Application for Basic API Access' option"; "Access requests are typically reviewed within 14 days"; "If your application is rejected, make sure you have met the requirements stated earlier before re-applying." One summary also reported a Google Account plus "an Organization account" and that "your website domain should match the email domain you submit with" - neither confirmed by a second search (see uncertainties).

findings.claim: Google frames the APIs as intended for large businesses and third parties, which is a real approval risk for a single-location barber.
findings.evidence: Business Profile Help 'How to use the Business Profile APIs' / application workflow intro: the APIs are "designed for developers who represent large, tech-savvy businesses and third parties" and "users must have technical experience and coding knowledge"; the workflow page is about "requesting API access to manage your Business Profiles at scale".

findings.claim: Reviews are read via the legacy-but-active Google My Business API v4: accounts.locations.reviews.list (max page size 50, default newest-updated first, verified locations only); replies via updateReply (PUT .../reviews/{reviewId}/reply, max 4096 bytes).
findings.evidence: reviews.list: "a GET to the location's reviews path and returns a paginated set of reviews for a verified location. The page size tops out at 50. If you omit ordering, results default to most-recently-updated first"; updateReply "is a PUT to the review's /reply path, and it creates a reply if none exists, which you can only do for verified locations... The reply comment has a maximum length of 4096 bytes." Request path uses /v4/accounts/{accountId}/locations/{locationId}/reviews. Requires scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/business.manage (plus.business.manage deprecated).

findings.claim: Known issue: reviews.list pagination can be inconsistent beyond page 1.
findings.evidence: Known issues page: "Pages after the first may not always return a completely consistent set, and some reviews may be missing from page 2 onward."

findings.claim: 2025-2026 changes: the v4 reviews surface gained ReviewReplyState (Apr 1, 2026), ReviewMediaItems (Apr 20, 2026), PolicyViolation on replies (Jul 1, 2026) and review_reply_url (Jul 24, 2026); the Q&A API was discontinued Nov 3, 2025; no deprecation or replacement of the v4 reviews endpoint was found.
findings.evidence: v4 change log: ReviewReplyState "giving visibility into the moderation status of your review replies through the list and batch-get methods"; ReviewMediaItems "thumbnail image and video URLs via the get, list, and batch-get review methods"; PolicyViolation "populated only when the reply state is REJECTED"; "accounts.locations.reviews.get doesn't currently return the reviewReplyState or policyViolation fields, so use list". Deprecation schedule: "The My Business Q&A API was discontinued on November 3, 2025" with no replacement; "Google replaced the accounts.locations.reportInsights method from Google My Business v4.9 with the new Business Profile Performance API." Latest-updates page newest entry Nov 2, 2026 (Business Information v1alpha locations.getExtended edit status).

findings.claim: Account and location IDs for the reviews path come from the Account Management API (GET /v1/accounts) and Business Information API (accounts.locations.list with a mandatory readMask).
findings.evidence: Account Management: "GET /v1/accounts Lists all of the accounts for the authenticated user"; names are "accounts/{account_id}"; "The personal account of the user doing the query will always be the first item". Business Information: accounts.locations.list "sends a GET to v1/{parent=accounts/*}/locations"; "accounts.locations.list and locations.get now requires a readMask"; location name takes the form "locations/{locationId}" (v1 dropped the accounts/{accountId}/ prefix, but the v4 reviews path still needs both IDs).

findings.claim: New/updated review events can be pushed via the My Business Notifications API to a Cloud Pub/Sub topic (NEW_REVIEW, UPDATED_REVIEW) instead of polling.
findings.evidence: "NEW_REVIEW is a new review added to the location, with review_name giving the added review and location_name giving the location's resource name. UPDATED_REVIEW covers a review on the location that has been updated." Method: PATCH https://mybusinessnotifications.googleapis.com/v1/accounts/{accountId}/notificationSetting with updateMask; the service account mybusiness-api-pubsub@system.gserviceaccount.com "must have at least Publish permissions on the Pub/Sub topic"; "Each account has one notification setting and one topic"; requires business.manage. The v4 accounts.updateNotifications method is deprecated.

findings.claim: Search impressions, direction requests, call clicks, website clicks and bookings are available only through the Business Profile Performance API v1 (daily granularity), which needs the same approval and business.manage scope.
findings.evidence: Methods: locations.getDailyMetricsTimeSeries, locations.fetchMultiDailyMetricsTimeSeries ("returns each date's values for the metrics you request... requires the business.manage OAuth scope"), locations.searchkeywords.impressions.monthly.list. DailyMetric values include BUSINESS_IMPRESSIONS_DESKTOP_MAPS, BUSINESS_IMPRESSIONS_DESKTOP_SEARCH, BUSINESS_IMPRESSIONS_MOBILE_MAPS, BUSINESS_IMPRESSIONS_MOBILE_SEARCH, BUSINESS_DIRECTION_REQUESTS ("how many times someone requested directions to the business location"), CALL_CLICKS ("clicks on the profile's call button"), WEBSITE_CLICKS ("The number of times the business profile website was clicked"), BUSINESS_BOOKINGS ("bookings made from the business profile via Reserve with Google"), BUSINESS_FOOD_ORDERS, BUSINESS_FOOD_MENU_CLICKS. "Only daily data is available. Hourly metrics are not supported." Quota 300 QPM.

findings.claim: Performance metric changes in 2025-2026: BUSINESS_CONVERSATIONS was removed on 2026-01-31; MESSAGING_CLICKS was added on Oct 14, 2026.
findings.evidence: Performance change log: BUSINESS_CONVERSATIONS "deprecated as of 2024-07-31, following the Google Business Messages shutdown. Its removal date is 2026-01-31. There is no replacement." Oct 14, 2026: "added a MESSAGING_CLICKS metric to track clicks on the message or chat button, such as WhatsApp or text message."

findings.claim: Google documents how the dashboard metrics are counted and that the searches (keywords) metric lags up to 5 days and is monthly; no general latency figure is published for calls/directions/website clicks.
findings.evidence: Help page: searches "is updated at the start of each month, and new data may take up to 5 days to become available in this report"; views: "A person can only be counted once a day"; directions "counts unique direction requests by accounting for multiple taps, direction cancellations, and spam"; calls: "The number of times a customer clicked on the call button on your Business Profile"; website clicks: "The number of times people clicked on the website link on your Business Profile". The GA4 integration keeps GBP metrics only for "the last 6 months".

findings.claim: The official way to get a review-request link is to copy it from the Business Profile dashboard ('Read Reviews' > 'Get more reviews' share icon); QR codes are desktop-only; customers need a Google Account.
findings.evidence: "Go to your Business Profile. Select Read Reviews and then Get more reviews [Share icon]." Copy the link or save the QR code ("right-click the code and choose Save image as"); "reviews QR codes can only be generated on a computer browser, not on mobile devices"; "Customers must be signed into a Google Account to leave a review"; suggested placements: "thank-you emails... at the end of a chat interaction, or add it to your receipts". Alternate paths: in Google Search select "Ask for reviews"; in Maps "Customers > Reviews > Get more reviews".

findings.claim: The short-link format https://g.page/r/<id>/review and the long form https://search.google.com/local/writereview?placeid=<PLACE_ID> are not documented by Google; only third-party guides describe them.
findings.evidence: Searches restricted to support.google.com returned no page describing the g.page/r format ("none of the results mention the g.page/r format itself"). Third-party guides: "The link Google generates usually looks something like https://g.page/r/YOUR_ID/review" and the long form is "https://search.google.com/local/writereview?placeid=YOUR_PLACE_ID", with the caveat that "Google does not document that URL and behavior varies by device, so test it signed out before printing it". Sources disagree on whether the short link is permanent ("stays active as long as your Google Business Profile exists" vs "works until the profile is re-verified").

findings.claim: The only Google-documented programmatic write-a-review link is Places API (New) Place Details field googleMapsLinks.writeAReviewUri (GA Aug 21, 2025), billed at the Place Details Pro SKU.
findings.evidence: Place Details (New): the write-review URL "sits inside a googleMapsLinks object alongside placeUri, directionsUri, reviewsUri, and photosUri"; docs describe writeAReviewUri as "a link for writing a review of this place on Google Maps"; "The googleMapsLinks field must be in the field mask" (example X-Goog-FieldMask: googleMapsUri,googleMapsLinks); "The googleMapsLinks field triggers the Place Details Pro SKU. Per the release notes, the field became generally available on August 21, 2025."

findings.claim: Public rating, review count and up to five reviews are available without GBP API approval via Places API (New), subject to Maps Platform billing/caching rules.
findings.evidence: Place Details (New): rating is "A rating between 1.0 and 5.0, based on user reviews of this place"; userRatingCount is "the total number of reviews, with or without text"; "Requesting reviews and reviewSummary returns up to five user-submitted Review objects" and "triggers the Place Details Enterprise + Atmosphere SKU". Pricing since March 1, 2025: "Essentials at 10,000 free calls per month per SKU, Pro at 5,000, and Enterprise at 1,000". Caching: "place IDs are exempt from the caching restriction, so they can therefore be stored indefinitely"; lat/long may be cached "up to 30 consecutive days"; other content caching is restricted.

findings.claim: Google policy: businesses may ask all customers for genuine reviews, but may not offer incentives, gate/selectively solicit, discourage negative reviews, or set staff review quotas.
findings.evidence: Maps UGC policy: merchants may not "discourage or prohibit negative reviews, or selectively solicit positive reviews from customers"; may not "request staff solicit a certain number of reviews"; prohibits "offering incentives such as payment, discounts, free goods and/or services in exchange for posting any review or revision or removal of a negative review". Permitted: "Solicit or encourage the posting of content that does represent a genuine experience, without offering incentives to do so or attempting to influence the rating or the contents of the review." Business Profile Help: "Offering incentives, like free or discounted goods or services, in exchange for customers to post reviews, change reviews, or remove negative reviews is considered fake & misleading content and is strictly prohibited." 'Incentivized or Biased Reviews' page: such content "is not allowed and will be removed from Maps"; repeated/serious violations can lead to account restrictions.

findings.claim: Australian law (ACCC guidance) points the same way: incentivised reviews must be offered equally and disclosed, review gating was flagged in the ACCC's Dec 2023 sweep, and suppressing genuine negative reviews can breach the ACL.
findings.evidence: ACCC: "Businesses that offer incentives to those who write positive reviews risk misleading consumers and breaching the CCA"; incentives only if offered equally to "likely critics and fans", reviewers told it applies "whether their review is positive or negative", and "prominently disclosed". The Dec 2023 sweep examined businesses that "direct customers with positive experiences to post a public review, while referring those with negative experiences directly to the business"; businesses "must not suppress or remove genuine negative reviews".

findings.claim: Search Console API: searchanalytics.query gives clicks/impressions/CTR/position by query, page, country, device and date; needs scope webmasters.readonly (or webmasters) and read permission on the exact property; data arrives after ~2-3 days and is kept 16 months.
findings.evidence: "This request requires authorization with at least one of the following scopes" (webmasters.readonly: "View Search Console data for your verified sites"); prerequisites: "searchAnalytics.query ... needs read permissions on that property"; siteUrl must match the property, e.g. "http://www.example.com/" (URL-prefix) or "sc-domain:example.com" (Domain); "data is typically available after 2-3 days"; Search Console "keeps data for the last 16 months"; rowLimit "1-25,000; Default is 1,000" with startRow paging; Performance data "limited to 50K rows of data per day per type ... per property". sites.list (GET https://www.googleapis.com/webmasters/v3/sites) returns permission levels siteOwner / siteFullUser / siteRestrictedUser / siteUnverifiedUser. URL Inspection API: "2000 QPD, 600 QPM" per property.

findings.claim: Search Console verification: a property must have at least one verified owner; methods are HTML file, HTML tag, Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, or DNS record; Domain properties can only be verified via DNS TXT.
findings.evidence: "a property must have at least one verified owner, or no users will have access to the property"; "Users who aren't verified can still get access. If you can't prove ownership, a current owner can grant you access"; "Domain name provider verification is more complex, but it is the only way to verify a Domain property"; DNS TXT "can take up to 48 hours"; a Domain property "covers all subdomains ... and multiple protocols"; URL-prefix "includes only URLs with the specified prefix, including the protocol"; ownership "lasts as long as Search Console can still confirm the token"; HTML tag is checked on the non-logged-in homepage ("google-site-verification").

findings.claim: OAuth consent-screen status matters for a private app: External + 'Testing' expires refresh tokens after 7 days; 'Production' removes that limit but unverified sensitive/restricted scopes show an 'Unverified app' warning and a lifetime 100-user cap; 'Internal' (Workspace/Cloud Identity org) apps are exempt from verification.
findings.evidence: "A Google Cloud Platform project with an OAuth consent screen configured for an external user type and a publishing status of 'Testing' is issued a refresh token expiring in 7 days, unless the only OAuth scopes requested are a subset of name, email address, and user profile"; in production "refresh tokens generally don't expire unless they are revoked or remain unused for a prolonged period (typically six months)"; "The user cap limits the number of users that can grant permission to your app when requesting unapproved sensitive or restricted scopes ... applies over the entire lifetime of the project"; Google shows an "Unverified apps warning message if your project's OAuth clients request authorization of scopes considered sensitive or restricted before your project has completed verification"; internal-use exception: "the app is used only by people in your Google Workspace or Cloud Identity organization. The project must be owned by the organization, and its OAuth consent screen needs to be configured for an Internal user type." Whether business.manage is flagged 'sensitive' was not confirmed; "Sensitive scopes ... have a sensitive indicator on the Google Cloud Console's OAuth consent screen configuration page."

implementation_decision:
Build the Google integration in three independent tiers so the app is useful with zero Google approvals and only lights up extra metrics when an authorised integration exists.

Tier 0 (ships now, no Google API, no approval): link-based review requests. Settings screen asks the owner to paste the review link copied from the Business Profile dashboard (Read Reviews > Get more reviews > share icon, desktop only) and optionally the Place ID. Store the pasted link verbatim; never synthesise g.page/r/... or search.google.com/local/writereview?placeid=... URLs (both undocumented). Requests go out through Studio Assistant's own SMS/email channel after an appointment, to every opted-in client uniformly (no filtering by satisfaction, no pre-screen 'how was it?' question, no incentive copy, no per-staff targets). Wording is neutral: ask for an honest review of their experience. Tracking is first-party only: requests sent, delivered, link clicks via an app-owned redirect (/r/<token> -> 302 to the stored official link; the redirect must not gate or branch on anything), and an optional manual 'review received' tick by the owner. UI guardrails: a short policy notice on the compose screen, no 'send only to happy clients' control, and copy templates that avoid any reward language (Google policy + ACCC).

Tier 1 (optional, Maps Platform key only, no GBP approval): if the owner adds a restricted Google Maps Platform API key and Place ID, call Places API (New) Place Details with field mask googleMapsLinks,rating,userRatingCount once a day (far below the 5,000/month Pro free cap). Use googleMapsLinks.writeAReviewUri as the canonical review link (fall back to the pasted link), show current star rating and review count on the dashboard, cache only the Place ID indefinitely and keep the latest rating/count snapshot with its fetch time (treat as a display cache, not a historical series, until the caching terms are checked). Do not request the reviews field (Enterprise + Atmosphere SKU, 1,000/month cap, caching restrictions) in this tier.

Tier 2 (only when 'Google Business Profile (API)' is connected): requires an approved Cloud project (quota shows 300 QPM, not 0) and the owner's OAuth grant with scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/business.manage. Resolve IDs via Account Management accounts.list and Business Information accounts.locations.list (readMask=name,title), then: list reviews with v4 accounts.locations.reviews.list (pageSize 50, order by updateTime desc, tolerate the documented pagination inconsistency by re-syncing on updateTime watermark), reply from the app via updateReply (enforce 4096 bytes, surface reviewReplyState/policyViolation from the list response), and ingest new reviews either by polling or via Notifications API Pub/Sub (NEW_REVIEW, UPDATED_REVIEW). Performance panel via Business Profile Performance API fetchMultiDailyMetricsTimeSeries: search/maps impressions (desktop+mobile), BUSINESS_DIRECTION_REQUESTS, CALL_CLICKS, WEBSITE_CLICKS, BUSINESS_BOOKINGS, MESSAGING_CLICKS (added Oct 2026), plus searchkeywords.impressions.monthly (monthly, up to 5-day lag). Do not reference BUSINESS_CONVERSATIONS (removed 2026-01-31) or the Q&A API (discontinued 2025-11-03). When not connected, show an honest 'Not connected - metrics available only through an approved Business Profile API integration' state with a link to the GBP dashboard; never show placeholder numbers.

Tier 3 (optional, separate): Search Console integration with scope webmasters.readonly after the owner verifies the shop website (prefer a Domain property with DNS TXT). Show clicks, impressions, CTR, average position by query/page/date with a 2-3 day lag note and 16-month history; sites.list first to confirm the property and permission level.

OAuth app setup: one Cloud project, External consent screen published to Production (not left in Testing, which kills refresh tokens after 7 days and would break background sync), owner is the only user so the 100-user cap is irrelevant; if the console flags business.manage as sensitive, either accept the unverified-app warning for the single owner account or complete sensitive-scope verification; use Internal user type instead if the owner has Google Workspace. Store refresh tokens encrypted, detect invalid_grant and prompt reconnect. Feature-flag each tier and record integration status per tier in the DB so dashboards can state exactly which metrics come from which authorised source.
account_requirements: Business Profile: a verified Google Business Profile for the Ivanhoe location that has been verified and active for 60+ days, with the shop website listed on it; the Google account that will authorise the app must be an owner/manager of that profile.

Review link (Tier 0): owner copies the link/QR from Business Profile on a desktop browser (Read Reviews > Get more reviews > share icon) and pastes it into Studio Assistant; no API or approval needed.

Google Cloud project with APIs enabled: My Business Account Management API, My Business Business Information API, Google My Business API (v4, reviews), Business Profile Performance API, My Business Notifications API (if Pub/Sub is used); OAuth 2.0 client (web) and consent screen requesting https://www.googleapis.com/auth/business.manage.

GBP API access approval (Tier 2): submit the 'Application for Basic API Access' via the GBP API contact form with the Cloud project number; expect review within ~14 days; confirm approval by quota changing from 0 QPM to 300 QPM; do not file a quota-increase request while at 0. Be prepared for rejection since Google describes the APIs as designed for large businesses and third parties; re-apply only after confirming the prerequisites.

OAuth publishing status: set the consent screen to Production (External) or Internal (requires a Google Workspace/Cloud Identity organisation); if business.manage is flagged 'sensitive' in the console, either accept the unverified-app warning for the single owner login (lifetime 100-user cap) or complete Google's sensitive-scope verification (brand/domain verification, privacy policy URL on the owned domain).

Pub/Sub notifications (optional): a Cloud Pub/Sub topic in the same project with Publish permission granted to mybusiness-api-pubsub@system.gserviceaccount.com; one notification setting/topic per account.

Places API (New) (Tier 1): Google Maps Platform billing account with a restricted API key; usage stays within the per-SKU monthly free caps (Place Details Pro 5,000 calls; Enterprise + Atmosphere 1,000 calls if reviews are ever requested); comply with Maps Platform caching/attribution terms (cache Place ID indefinitely, not other content long-term).

Search Console (Tier 3): the owner verifies the shop website in Search Console (DNS TXT record for a Domain property, or HTML tag/file for a URL-prefix property), the authorising Google account has at least read ('restricted') permission on that property, and the Search Console API is enabled in the Cloud project with scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/webmasters.readonly.

Policy compliance (all tiers): ask every client uniformly, no incentives or discounts for reviews, no gating/pre-screening, no discouraging negative reviews, no staff review quotas; keep review-request copy neutral (Google Maps UGC policy and ACCC guidance).
uncertainties: Both developers.google.com and support.google.com were unreachable from the sandbox (ENOTFOUND), so every finding relies on search-engine summaries of the official pages rather than full-page reads; exact wording and page update dates should be re-checked against the live pages before they are quoted to the owner.

Two prerequisite details were reported by one search summary but not confirmed by a second: that applicants need an 'Organization account' and that the applicant's email domain should match the website domain. If true, the owner may need an email address on the shop's own domain rather than a gmail.com address when applying.

Whether Google will approve Basic API access for a single-location barber is unknown; the help centre says the APIs are 'designed for developers who represent large, tech-savvy businesses and third parties'. Community reports suggest small businesses are approved, but no official statement was found.

Whether https://www.googleapis.com/auth/business.manage is classified as a 'sensitive' scope (triggering the unverified-app warning / verification) was not confirmed; check the sensitive indicator on the Cloud Console consent-screen page.

The g.page/r/<id>/review short link and search.google.com/local/writereview?placeid= long link are undocumented by Google; their stability (e.g. after re-verification) is unknown. Only googleMapsLinks.writeAReviewUri from Places API (New) is documented.

Maps Platform caching rules for rating/userRatingCount beyond display were not read directly from the Service Specific Terms; the place-ID exemption and 30-day lat/long rule were confirmed, but whether a historical rating series may be stored should be checked against the live terms.

No official latency figure exists for Performance API daily metrics (only the monthly searches metric's 'up to 5 days'); dashboards should display the last available date rather than assume same-day data.
The reviews.list pagination inconsistency is documented as a known issue without a fix date; a watermark-based re-sync is a mitigation, not a guarantee of completeness.

No announcement of a replacement for the v4 reviews endpoint was found; it remains active with 2026 field additions, but the v4 API as a whole is described as being phased out, so a future migration should be assumed possible.

The Search Console scope description says 'verified sites' while the permissions help page says unverified users can be granted access by an owner; no source states that an unverified property is rejected by searchanalytics.query. For Studio Assistant the owner will verify the site anyway.

Page ages are approximate (reported by the search tool as days-old counts): review-link help page ~Dec 2025/Jan 2026, GBP limits/FAQ ~Aug 2026, Search Console limits page ~Aug 2025; GBP change-log entries are dated to the day (Apr 1, Apr 20, Jul 1, Jul 24, Oct 14 and Nov 2, 2026).

findings.claim: Supabase Storage S3 endpoint format is https://<project_ref>.storage.supabase.co/storage/v1/s3 (the older https://<project_ref>.supabase.co/storage/v1/s3 host also works but is not recommended for large uploads); clients must use path-style addressing and the project's AWS region string.
findings.evidence: S3 Authentication doc code sample: `forcePathStyle: true, region: 'project_region', endpoint: 'https://project_ref.storage.supabase.co/storage/v1/s3'`. Admonition: "For optimal performance when uploading large files you should always use the direct storage hostname... Instead of `https://project-id.supabase.co` use `https://project-id.storage.supabase.co`". Also: "generate a pair of credentials (Access Key ID and Secret Access Key), copy the endpoint and region from the S3 configuration page". Sydney projects are region ap-southeast-2 (regions page lists 'Oceania (Sydney) ap-southeast-2').

findings.claim: Supabase S3 access keys are server-side only and bypass RLS entirely; a per-user alternative (session token = user JWT) exists.
findings.evidence: "S3 access keys provide full access to all S3 operations across all buckets and bypass RLS policies. These are meant to be used only on the server." Session token method: "All S3 operations performed with the Session Token are scoped to the authenticated user. RLS policies on the Storage Schema are respected." (credentials: accessKeyId = project_ref, secretAccessKey = anon key, sessionToken = user access token).

findings.claim: Supabase's S3 implementation supports the full multipart upload set and presigned (SigV4 query-string) URLs, plus GetObject with Range, HeadObject, PutObject, CopyObject, DeleteObject(s), ListObjectsV2; it does not support versioning, bucket CORS/lifecycle/encryption config, SSE-C, ACLs, tagging, object locking or Content-MD5. The S3 connection must be enabled in Storage settings.
findings.evidence: Compatibility doc: "Storage supports presigning a URL using query parameters. Specifically, Supabase Storage expects requests to be made using AWS Signature Version 4. To enable this feature, enable the S3 connection via S3 protocol in the Settings page for Supabase Storage." Implemented rows marked ✅: ListMultipartUploads, CreateMultipartUpload, CompleteMultipartUpload, AbortMultipartUpload, UploadPart, UploadPartCopy, ListParts, GetObject, HeadObject, PutObject, DeleteObject, DeleteObjects, ListObjects, ListObjectsV2, CopyObject, ListBuckets, HeadBucket, CreateBucket, DeleteBucket, GetBucketLocation. ❌: DeleteBucketCors, GetBucketEncryption, GetBucketLifecycleConfiguration, GetBucketCors, PutBucketCors, PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration; per-op ❌ for SSE-C, ACLs, tagging, object locking, Content-MD5. "S3 versioning is not supported... Deleted objects are permanently removed and cannot be restored." "all these protocols are interoperable" (standard, resumable, S3).

findings.claim: Supabase S3 presigned URLs are capped at 7 days (604800 s) by the storage server, matching the SigV4 spec; this is enforced in code rather than documented.
findings.evidence: signature-v4.ts: `const MAX_PRESIGNED_EXPIRY_SECONDS = 604800` and `if (!/^[1-9]\d{0,5}$/.test(expires) || expiresSec > MAX_PRESIGNED_EXPIRY_SECONDS) { throw ERRORS.InvalidSignature('Invalid expiration') }`; expired requests throw `ERRORS.ExpiredSignature()`.

findings.claim: supabase-js createSignedUrl takes expiresIn in seconds with no documented maximum; the server only enforces integer >= 1 and a JWT numeric bound that is effectively unlimited. createSignedUploadUrl tokens are fixed at 2 hours. Individual signed URLs cannot be revoked.
findings.evidence: storage-js JSDoc: "expiresIn The number of seconds until the signed URL expires. For example, `60` for a URL which is valid for one minute." createSignedUploadUrl: URLs "are valid for 2 hours". Server schema (getSignedURL.ts): `expiresIn: { type: 'integer', finite: true, minimum: 1, examples: [60000] }` then `assertValidNumericJWTExpiration(expiresIn)` whose ceiling is `MAX_ABSOLUTE_JWT_EXPIRATION_SECONDS = Math.floor(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER / 1000)` minus now. Downloads doc: "You can't revoke individual signed URLs. To invalidate a specific one, delete, move, or rename the underlying object." / "To revoke all signed URLs, rotate your project's URL signing key, and then revoke the previous key."

findings.claim: Buckets are private by default; private objects are only reachable via an authenticated download (user JWT + RLS) or a time-limited signed URL. Public buckets skip auth for reads and cache better.
findings.evidence: "When a bucket is set to **Private** all operations are subject to access control via RLS policies. This also applies when downloading assets. Buckets are private by default. The only ways to download assets within a private bucket is to: Use the download method by providing an authorization header containing your user's JWT... Create a signed URL with the createSignedUrl method that can be accessed for a limited time." "Public buckets are more performant than private buckets since they are cached differently." Access-control doc: "Service keys entirely bypass RLS policies, granting you unrestricted access to all Storage APIs."

findings.claim: Signed-URL responses are CDN-cached per unique token on Smart CDN (Pro+ only), so freshly generated signed URLs always miss the cache; token expiry and cache TTL are independent.
findings.evidence: Smart CDN doc: "Smart CDN caching is automatically enabled for Pro Plan and above." "With Smart CDN enabled, signed URL responses are cached at the CDN edge... Smart CDN treats each unique token as a separate cache key, meaning the first request with any given signed URL results in a cache miss"; "If you generate a new signed URL on every request, the cache will never be warm and every request hits the origin." "Token expiry (`expiresIn`) and the object's response cache TTL (`cacheControl`) are independent." CDN fundamentals: private-bucket per-user checks mean "it results in a cache miss for both the users".

findings.claim: Per-file size limits: Free is hard-capped at 50 MB; Pro/Team can set the global limit up to 500 GB (raised from 50 GB on 18 Jul 2025); per-bucket limits must be lower than the global limit; the global limit must be raised in Storage Settings.
findings.evidence: File limits doc table: Free 50 MB, Pro 500 GB, Team 500 GB, Enterprise Custom. "Free projects can't go above 50 MB. Pro and higher can go up to 500 GB"; "set it in the _Global file size limit_ field in your Storage Settings"; per-bucket max "must be lower than the global limit". Blog 'Storage: 10x Larger Uploads...' published 18 Jul 2025 (search summary).

findings.claim: Large server-side uploads to Supabase should use S3 multipart (aws-sdk lib-storage Upload); max 500 GB on paid plans; unfinished multipart uploads are auto-aborted after 24 h. TUS resumable uploads require fixed 6 MB chunks and 24 h upload URLs.
findings.evidence: S3 uploads doc: "Use `PutObject` to upload smaller files... The maximum file size on paid plans is 500 GB." "This method is preferable over Resumable Upload for server-side uploads, when you want to maximize upload speed at the cost of resumability. The maximum file size on paid plans is 500 GB." "All multipart uploads are automatically aborted after 24 hours." Resumable doc: chunks must be 6MB ("keep it at 6MB for now"), upload URL "valid for up to 24 hours", endpoint `/storage/v1/upload/resumable` on `<project-id>.storage.supabase.co`, concurrent clients on one upload URL get `409 Conflict`.

findings.claim: Storage pricing (USD): Free 1 GB, Pro/Team 100 GB included, overage $0.0213/GB-month (billed as GB-hours); Egress: Free 5 GB uncached + 5 GB cached, Pro/Team 250 GB + 250 GB, overage $0.09/GB uncached and $0.03/GB cached; one unified egress quota across DB, Storage, Auth, Functions, Realtime.
findings.evidence: pricing_storage_size partial: "$0.00002919 per GB-Hr ($0.0213 per GB per month)... Free 1 | Pro 100 | Team 100". Egress doc: "$0.09 per GB per month for uncached egress, $0.03 per GB per month for cached egress. You are only charged for usage exceeding your subscription plan's quota. | Free | 5 GB / 5 GB | - | Pro | 250 GB / 250 GB | $0.09 per GB / $0.03 per GB". Egress "is network data sent out to a connected client" incl. Storage; measured against "a single Unified Egress Quota shared across all services" (summary).

findings.claim: Plan/compute pricing: Pro is $25/month and includes $10 compute credits that cover one Micro instance (~$10/mo, $0.01344/hr); Nano is free-plan only; Pro disk 8 GB included then $0.125/GB-month; Free has a fixed 2 GB disk and a 500 MB database-size fair-use quota.
findings.evidence: Compute doc: "Paid plans include $10 in Compute Credits, which cover one project running on the Micro/Nano Compute size"; table Nano $0, Micro $0.01344/hr ~$10, Small ~$15; "You cannot launch Nano instances on paid plans, only Micro and above"; billing example line "Pro Plan | - | $25". Disk doc: "$0.125 per GB per month... provisioned with an 8 GB disk. You are only charged for provisioned disk size exceeding these 8 GB." Database-size doc: "Free Plan projects have a fixed disk size of 2 GB. The disk does not autoscale." and "The 500 MB _database size_ quota... is a billing quota".

findings.claim: Free-plan projects are paused after 7 days of low database activity (restorable for 1 year); paid projects are never auto-paused. This makes Free unsuitable for a production barber app that is quiet some weeks.
findings.evidence: "Supabase pauses Free Plan projects that show low activity over a 7-day period to save server resources." "Typically a few user requests to the database each day over the previous week is enough to keep the project from being paused." "You can restore a paused project for up to 1 year after it was paused". "Paid projects cannot be paused and are not subject to pausing for inactivity."

findings.claim: Connection modes: direct db.<ref>.supabase.co:5432 (IPv6 unless IPv4 add-on); shared Supavisor session mode <pooler-host>:5432 (IPv4 on every plan, supports prepared statements, user postgres.<ref>); shared transaction mode :6543 (no prepared statements, no pipelining, session state not kept); dedicated PgBouncer pooler db.<ref>.supabase.co:6543 (Pro+, transaction mode only, prepared statements OK on PgBouncer >= 1.21, IPv6/IPv4-addon). Session mode on 6543 was removed 28 Feb 2025.
findings.evidence: Table: Direct `db.[PROJECT-REF].supabase.co:5432` IPv6/IPv6/IPv4; Session `aws-[INDEX]-[REGION].pooler.supabase.com:5432` IPv4 all plans; Transaction `...:6543` IPv4; Dedicated `db.[PROJECT-REF].supabase.co:6543` -/IPv6/IPv4. "The shared pooler doesn't support prepared statements in transaction mode." "Transaction mode does not support query pipelining." "On the Pro Plan and above, Supabase provisions a dedicated pooler (PgBouncer)... runs in transaction mode only... supports prepared statements on PgBouncer 1.21 and later." "The IPv4 add-on is not dual-stack: enabling it swaps the project's IPv6 (AAAA) DNS record for an IPv4 (A) record". Changelog (search): Session Mode on port 6543 sunset 2025-02-28; "Port 6543 now serves only Transaction Mode, and Session Mode remains on port 5432".

findings.claim: Supabase's own guidance for a persistent Node backend: direct connection if the host has IPv6 (or the IPv4 add-on), otherwise shared-pooler session mode; transaction mode is for serverless; dedicated pooler for high load on Pro+.
findings.evidence: Method table: "A persistent backend on IPv6, or with the IPv4 add-on | Direct connection | No pooler in the path." "A persistent backend on an IPv4-only network | Shared pooler, session mode | The shared pooler is IPv4-only on every plan." "A serverless or edge function | Shared pooler, transaction mode | These environments open many short-lived connections." "A high-load application on the Pro Plan and above | Dedicated pooler". Pooling doc: "Direct connections remain the best choice for long-lived sessions, and shared pooler session mode is the alternative w[hen IPv4 is needed]". Serverless advice: pool size 1, prepared statements off, `ssl: 'require'`.

findings.claim: Connection budgets on the smallest instances are tight: Nano/Micro allow 60 Postgres connections, 200 pooler clients and a default pooler pool size of 15 (per role); Small is 90/400/15. Supabase services (Auth, Storage, PostgREST) consume part of the 60.
findings.evidence: Compute doc table: "Nano (free) | 5 | 5 | 60 | 200 | 15", "Micro | ... | 60 | 200 | 15", "Small | ... | 90 | 400 | 15". Pooling doc: "Direct connections + Shared pooler backend connections + Dedicated pooler backend connections < Postgres max connections for your compute instance"; "Supabase services hold their own connections, including Auth, Storage, PostgREST, and the health checker". Connection-management: pool size "applies per database role"; keep pool size <= 80% of max connections (<= 40% with heavy PostgREST use).

findings.claim: IPv4 add-on costs $4/month ($0.0055/hr), is Pro+ only, is NOT covered by the Spend Cap, and is only needed for direct/dedicated-pooler connections from IPv4-only networks; the shared pooler is always IPv4.
findings.evidence: "$0.0055 per hour ($4 per month)." "IPv4 Hours are **not** covered by the Spend Cap." IPv4 doc: shared pooler (ports 6543 and 5432) "Always uses IPv4, with no add-on needed"; add-on "available on the Pro Plan and above". Cost-control: Spend Cap "available only with the Pro Plan"; when on, "further usage of that item is disallowed until the next billing cycle".

findings.claim: pg-boss (v12.38.x; project has 12.38.1 installed) does NOT need LISTEN/NOTIFY: workers poll by default (pollingIntervalSeconds, default 2 s). LISTEN/NOTIFY is an opt-in optimisation that needs a session-pinned connection and does not work through transaction-mode poolers; when unavailable pg-boss logs `listen_notify_unavailable` and keeps polling.
findings.evidence: Workers doc: "By default, workers fetch new jobs by polling on their `pollingIntervalSeconds`"; "This is an **opt-in optimization on top of polling, not a replacement for it.**" Constructor doc `useListenNotify` (default false): "This option holds one dedicated database connection open for listening. It requires a session-pinned connection: it works with the built-in connection pool and with a `db` adapter that implements `listen`, but **not** through PgBouncer in transaction or statement pooling mode, which disables `LISTEN/NOTIFY`. When a listener cannot be established, pg-boss emits a `warning` event of type `listen_notify_unavailable` and continues with polling only." README: "relies on Postgres's SKIP LOCKED"; Node >= 22.12, Postgres >= 13. The repo's packages/queue/src/index.ts does not set useListenNotify (polling only; `max: 6` worker / `3` producer).

findings.claim: pg-boss's SQL is pooler-friendly even in transaction mode: it issues unnamed parameterised queries (no named prepared statements), uses transaction-scoped advisory locks inside explicit transactions, and only runs per-connection session statements for test clocks.
findings.evidence: db.ts executeSql: `return await client.query(text, values)` (no `name`), pool is `new pg.Pool({...this.config, onConnect...})`, `max` "defaults to 10". plans.ts: `function advisoryLock(...) { return \`SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(...)\` }` wrapped as `transaction(noAdvisoryLocks ? statements : [advisoryLock(schema, key), ...statements])`; stats use `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock`; `noAdvisoryLocks` flag exists. `setSessionStatements` is only called with `plans.enableClockOverride()` for TestClock. Caveat: pg-boss holds its `max` connections open as a long-lived pool and the dedicated LISTEN client is a separate `pg.Client`.

findings.claim: Cloudflare R2 is markedly cheaper for video-heavy private media: $0.015/GB-month standard storage, zero egress via the S3 API, Class A $4.50/M and Class B $0.36/M ops, with a monthly free tier of 10 GB-months, 1M Class A and 10M Class B.
findings.evidence: R2 pricing doc: Storage (Standard) $0.015 per GB-month; Class A $4.50 per million; Class B $0.36 per million; free tier "10 GB-months of storage, 1 million Class A requests, and 10 million Class B requests" (Standard only); egress "Free for all storage classes when data leaves R2 through the Workers API, S3 API, or r2.dev domains". Infrequent Access $0.01/GB-month + $0.01/GB retrieval, 30-day minimum.

findings.claim: R2's S3 API is a drop-in for the project's S3Store: endpoint https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, region `auto`, full multipart set, presigned GET/HEAD/PUT/DELETE valid 1 s to 7 days (S3 API domain only, not custom domains), 5 GiB single PUT, 5 TiB objects, 10,000 parts, and an Oceania location hint `oc` (best-effort) set at bucket creation.
findings.evidence: S3 API doc: endpoint `https://<ACCOUNT_ID>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`; implemented GetObject, HeadObject, PutObject, CopyObject, DeleteObject, DeleteObjects, ListObjectsV2, CreateMultipartUpload, UploadPart, UploadPartCopy, CompleteMultipartUpload, AbortMultipartUpload, ListMultipartUploads, ListParts; region `auto` (`us-east-1` treated as auto). Presigned doc: "Timeout from 1 second to 7 days (604,800 seconds)"; presigned URLs "cannot be used with custom domains"; POST form uploads unsupported. Limits: 5 TiB object, 5 GiB single upload, 10,000 parts, 1 write/sec per key. Data-location: hints table `oc | Oceania`, "Location Hints are a best effort and not a guarantee", set via `LocationConstraint` in `CreateBucketConfiguration` or dashboard.

findings.claim: The repository is already shaped for this: packages/storage S3Store (@aws-sdk/client-s3 3.1164, lib-storage multipart with 8 MB parts, s3-request-presigner GET URLs, private-bucket-only design) and packages/config exposes DATABASE_URL, optional QUEUE_DATABASE_URL, S3_ENDPOINT/S3_REGION/S3_BUCKET/S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID/S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY/S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE; apps/worker creates a pg.Pool with max 8 plus pg-boss max 6.
findings.evidence: /home/user/editor/packages/storage/src/s3.ts: "S3-compatible store. Works with Supabase Storage (S3 protocol), Cloudflare R2 and AWS S3. Buckets must be private; browsers only ever receive presigned, expiring URLs."; `new Upload({... partSize: 8 * 1024 * 1024, queueSize: 3 })`; `getSignedUrl(this.client, cmd, { expiresIn: options.expiresInSeconds })`. /home/user/editor/packages/config/src/index.ts lines 17-33. /home/user/editor/apps/worker/src/main.ts: `createDatabase(env.DATABASE_URL, { max: 8, applicationName: 'studio-worker' })` and `createQueue({ connectionString: env.QUEUE_DATABASE_URL ?? env.DATABASE_URL, role: 'worker' })`.

implementation_decision:
Recommended Studio Assistant configuration (decision):

1. Supabase Pro project in Sydney (ap-southeast-2), Micro compute (covered by the $10/month compute credit), Spend Cap ON. Free is rejected for production: 50 MB per-file hard cap (phone videos exceed it), 7-day inactivity pausing, 1 GB storage / 5 GB egress, fixed 2 GB disk. Expected baseline: USD $25/month (+$4 only if the IPv4 add-on is needed).

2. Database connections (keep the repo's split of DATABASE_URL vs QUEUE_DATABASE_URL):
   - apps/worker (long-lived Node process running FFmpeg + pg-boss): use the DIRECT connection `postgresql://postgres:<pw>@db.<ref>.supabase.co:5432/postgres?sslmode=require` when the worker host has IPv6 egress; otherwise use shared-pooler SESSION mode `postgresql://postgres.<ref>:<pw>@aws-<n>-ap-southeast-2.pooler.supabase.com:5432/postgres` (copy the exact host from the Connect dialog). Do not buy the IPv4 add-on unless both direct and session mode are unworkable. Set QUEUE_DATABASE_URL to the same direct/session string. pg-boss needs no LISTEN (the repo does not enable useListenNotify; polling every 2 s is fine for render jobs); keep it that way, which also keeps the option of transaction mode open, but prefer direct/session so heartbeats, migrations and the long-lived pool are not subject to pooler client limits.
   - Connection budget on Micro: Postgres max 60 (shared with Auth/Storage/PostgREST), pooler default pool size 15 per role. The current worker settings (pg.Pool max 8 + pg-boss max 6 = 14) nearly exhaust the 15-connection session pool; reduce to pg.Pool max 4 and pg-boss max 3 for the worker (and raise the Dashboard Pool Size to ~30 if needed, staying under 80% of 60).
   - apps/web (Next.js): if deployed serverless (Vercel/Sydney), use shared-pooler TRANSACTION mode on port 6543 with pool size 1, `sslmode=require`, and never use named prepared statements (do not call drizzle `.prepare()`; node-postgres unnamed `$1` queries are fine). The web app's pg-boss producer (`supervise: false`, unnamed queries, xact-scoped advisory locks) works through transaction mode. If the web app runs on the same VPS as the worker, just use the same direct/session string. The dedicated PgBouncer pooler (Pro+) is unnecessary at this scale.
   - Use `sslmode=verify-full` with the downloaded project root cert where the driver supports it; enable "Enforce SSL" in Database settings.

3. Media storage: use Cloudflare R2 for all blobs (source footage, analysis frames, previews, exports) via the existing S3Store: STORAGE_DRIVER=s3, S3_ENDPOINT=https://<account_id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, S3_REGION=auto, S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=true, one private bucket created with location hint `oc` (Oceania), API token scoped Object Read & Write to that bucket. Rationale: the worker re-downloads multi-GB source footage from object storage for every render and the owner downloads large exports; on Supabase that is billable uncached egress ($0.09/GB after 250 GB, and private-bucket signed URLs rarely hit the CDN), whereas R2 egress is free and storage is $0.015 vs $0.0213 per GB-month with a 10 GB free tier. Presigned GET URLs stay short-lived (15-60 min; both providers cap at 7 days). Multipart via lib-storage (8 MB parts) is supported on both.
   - Alternative (single-vendor): Supabase Storage via S3 protocol with the same driver: enable the S3 connection in Storage Settings, generate S3 access keys (server-only; they bypass RLS), S3_ENDPOINT=https://<ref>.storage.supabase.co/storage/v1/s3, S3_REGION=ap-southeast-2 (as shown on the S3 settings page), S3_FORCE_PATH_STYLE=true, raise the Global file size limit (Pro) to e.g. 20 GB and set a bucket-level limit/MIME allowlist, keep the bucket private. Acceptable for a small catalogue but budget for egress; do not rely on supabase-js createSignedUrl since the app serves presigned S3 GETs itself (7-day server cap).
   - Keep LocalDiskStore for dev; the S3Store already abstracts both targets so switching is config-only.

4. Operational notes: Supabase Storage auto-aborts multipart uploads after 24 h (R2: set a lifecycle rule for incomplete multipart uploads); deleted objects are unrecoverable on Supabase (no versioning), so keep the planned CLEANUP job conservative; run Drizzle migrations over the direct/session connection, never through 6543.
account_requirements: Supabase account + organization on the Pro plan (USD $25/month; includes $10 compute credits, 100 GB storage, 250 GB uncached + 250 GB cached egress, 8 GB disk). Free plan is only acceptable for development (50 MB file cap, 7-day inactivity pausing, 2 GB fixed disk).
Create the project in the specific region 'Oceania (Sydney) ap-southeast-2'; choose Micro compute (Nano cannot be launched on paid plans).

Set/record the database password; copy the three connection strings from the Dashboard 'Connect' dialog (direct 5432, session pooler 5432 with user postgres.<ref>, transaction pooler 6543); optionally download the SSL root certificate and enable 'Enforce SSL'.
Optionally raise the pooler 'Pool Size' in Database settings (keep below ~80% of the 60-connection Micro limit).

IPv4 add-on (USD $4/month, Pro+, not covered by Spend Cap) only if the worker host is IPv4-only AND a direct connection is required; otherwise use the shared session pooler which is IPv4 on all plans.
Decide the Spend Cap (Pro only): ON blocks overage (storage/egress/disk) at quota; OFF bills $0.0213/GB storage, $0.09/GB uncached egress, $0.125/GB disk.

If using Supabase Storage: in Storage settings enable the S3 protocol connection, generate an S3 Access Key ID/Secret (server-side only, bypasses RLS), raise the Global file size limit (Pro max 500 GB) and create a private bucket with its own size/MIME restrictions.

If using Cloudflare R2 (recommended for media): a Cloudflare account with R2 enabled, a private bucket (location hint 'oc'), the account ID for the S3 endpoint, and an R2 API token scoped to Object Read & Write on that bucket. Free tier 10 GB-month / 1M Class A / 10M Class B; $0.015/GB-month beyond; egress free.
Worker host must provide either IPv6 egress (for the Supabase direct connection) or use the IPv4 shared pooler; Node >= 22.12 for pg-boss 12.x; Postgres >= 13 (Supabase is 15/17).
No app review, developer-program approval or business verification applies to Supabase or Cloudflare R2; both are self-serve with a payment method.
uncertainties: supabase.com, developers.cloudflare.com and pgboss.io are DNS-blocked in this sandbox; all 'full page' reads are the open-source documentation sources on raw.githubusercontent.com (supabase/supabase master, cloudflare/cloudflare-docs production, timgit/pg-boss master), which are the inputs to the published sites but could be slightly ahead of or behind the live pages.

The Supabase pricing page itself was not read; Pro $25/month comes from a docs billing example and search summaries, and the Free plan '2 active projects' limit comes only from search summaries of the pricing page.

The 'Transaction mode limitations' section (SET / listen-notify / temporary tables not persisting) was reported by the fetch tool's summary rather than quoted verbatim; the prepared-statement and pipelining limitations are verbatim.

Supavisor's exact pool_size accounting in session mode (per user/db/mode combination) is described in a KB article (supavisor-faq) that was not retrievable; the docs state pool size 'applies per database role'.

Supabase S3 presigned-URL 7-day cap and the createSignedUrl expiry ceiling are taken from the storage server source on master, not from documentation; the deployed platform version is assumed to match.
Whether Supabase still labels the S3 protocol 'public alpha' (Apr 2024 blog) or 'GA' (feature page/changelog label) could not be confirmed with a dated promotion announcement.
Whether enabling R2 on a Cloudflare account requires adding a payment method even within the free tier was not verified.

pg-boss docs were read at master (package.json 12.38.2) while the repo has 12.38.1 installed; the cited options (useListenNotify, max, supervise, migrate) exist in both, but exact defaults should be re-checked against the installed README if upgraded.
The eventual worker hosting provider (and therefore IPv6 availability) is unknown; this decides direct connection vs session pooler vs the $4 IPv4 add-on.
