findings.claim: TikTok publishes no fixed pixel safe zone; its official guidance is qualitative and template-based, and the zone shrinks with caption length.
findings.evidence: Auction In-Feed Ads help page (search summary): "The safe zone size is determined by the dimension (vertical, horizontal, or square), ad caption length, and any additional formats used"; TopView page: "the longer the caption, the smaller the safe zone will be" and "do not place any text, logos, or key messages on areas where buttons, usernames, and captions may appear in the in-feed section"; the in-feed page offers downloadable safe-zone files (LTR and RTL/Arabic, with and without anchor: "If you use anchors in the video ads, download the safe zone files with the anchor") and says elements outside the zone "might be covered or cropped". Recommended vertical format: 9:16, at least 540x960 px.

findings.claim: TikTok's organic (non-ad) guidance defines the safe zone as the area not covered by UI and tells creators to keep text, subtitles and overlays inside it, avoiding the frame edges.
findings.evidence: Creator Academy (search summary): the safe zone is "the part of the screen not covered by its buttons or the name, caption, and audio"; "Keep your text, subtitles, overlays, and subjects within the safe zone, so nothing is blocking your content"; covers article advises avoiding elements around the edges of the frame. No pixel values given.

findings.claim: Third-party readings of TikTok's official in-feed template (drawn on a 720x1280 frame) give, scaled to 1080x1920: 240 px top, 660 px bottom, 120 px each side, plus a right-hand action-button column ~180 px wide starting ~840 px from the top (i.e. up to ~300 px from the right edge in the lower frame). These are NOT TikTok's own published numbers.
findings.evidence: Socialync: "On a 1080 by 1920 pixel frame ... keep text, faces and logos out of the top 240 pixels, the bottom 660 pixels and 120 pixels on each side. TikTok's profile picture, like, comment, save and share buttons also cover a column 180 pixels wide inside the right margin, starting 840 pixels from the top." AdCheckLab cites the same template and says the right margin grows to 300 px in the lower part; it also claims "TikTok replaced this template in April 2025 ... the template it now ships has no caption variants" (unverified).

findings.claim: Other widely cited community TikTok figures are smaller and mutually inconsistent: 130 px top / 484 px bottom / 140 px right / 44 px left; 150/440/60; 900x1492 central box; or percentages (top 10%, bottom 25%, right 15%).
findings.evidence: ezUGC: "leaving 130px at the top, 484px at the bottom, 140px on the right, and 44px on the left"; other guides: "safe area of roughly 960 x 1330 px (60 px side margins, 150 px top, 440 px bottom)"; Postplanify/Adaptlypost: 900x1492 centred area; Novustools: avoid top 10%, bottom 25%, right 15%.

findings.claim: Meta's official Reels safe-zone guidance is expressed in percentages: leave ~14% of the top, ~35% of the bottom and ~6% of each side free of text/logos. At 1080x1920 that is 269 px top, 672 px bottom, 65 px per side (central area ~950x979 px).
findings.evidence: Meta Ads Guide, Awareness Image Ad Specs on Instagram Reels (search summary): "Consider leaving roughly 14% of the top, 35% of the bottom, and 6% on each side of your asset free from text, logos, or other key creative elements" so the profile icon and call-to-action don't cover them; page lists 9:16 and 1440 x 2560 px for image assets. Note: the figures come from the Reels IMAGE ad spec page; a dedicated Reels VIDEO ad spec page did not surface in any search.

findings.claim: Meta's Stories (not Reels) video ad guidance uses a smaller bottom band and gives explicit pixel values: 14% (250 px) top and 20% (340 px) bottom.
findings.evidence: Meta Ads Guide, Awareness Video ad specs on Instagram Stories (search summary): keep "roughly 14% (250 pixels) of the top and 20% (340 pixels) of the bottom of the video free from text, logos or other key creative elements"; 9:16, 1440 x 2560 recommended. The 250/340 px figures do not map cleanly onto 1080x1920 (14% of 1920 = 269; 20% = 384).

findings.claim: Meta provides an official Reels safe-zone checker template (PPT/PSD/Keynote) and recommends keeping key messages inside the safe zone; its text-overlay help page no longer imposes a 20% text rule and gives no pixel figures.
findings.evidence: Meta Reels ads page: "Reels safe zone checker in PPT, PSD, and Keynote formats"; Meta developer blog (2024-11-07): "Put your key messages within the Reels safe zone to ensure they're landing clearly"; Meta claims Reels ads built as 9:16 video with audio and key elements in the safe zone had "34.5% lower cost per result than image ads". Business Help 980593475366490: text-overlay tool retired, no limit on text in images, shorter text still recommended; no safe-zone pixel values.

findings.claim: Third-party Instagram Reels templates disagree: 220 top / 420 bottom / 35 sides (FileFlippers), 140 top / 500 bottom / 130 right (Brandeal), bottom 400 px (CampaignSwift), and a lower-right block (~21% in from the right, ~40% up from the bottom) said to appear in Meta's diagram (Hopper HQ, camclo3d). The task's '220/420' figures trace to FileFlippers, not Meta.
findings.evidence: Search summary: "The 220 px top / 420 px bottom figures come from one source, FileFlippers, which reserves about 220 px at the top, 420 px at the bottom, and 35 px on each side on a 1080x1920 frame"; "Meta's diagram reportedly also blocks the lower-right corner, about 21% in from the right edge and 40% up from the bottom"; Whymatters states Meta's page gives no pixel figures and that 14%/35% is a common rule of thumb.

findings.claim: Instagram Graph API Reel specifications (official): MOV or MP4 container with moov atom at the front and no edit lists; AAC audio, 48 kHz max, mono/stereo, 128 kbps; HEVC or H.264, progressive scan, closed GOP, 4:2:0 chroma; 23-60 fps; VBR video bitrate 25 Mbps max; max width 1920 px; aspect ratio 0.01:1-10:1 with 9:16 recommended; duration 3 s min / 15 min max; file size 300 MB max.
findings.evidence: IG User Media reference (search summary quoting the page): "Audio codec: AAC, 48khz sample rate maximum, 1 or 2 channels (mono or stereo)"; "Video codec: HEVC or H264, progressive scan, closed GOP, 4:2:0 chroma subsampling"; "Frame rate: 23-60 FPS"; "Video bitrate: VBR, 25Mbps maximum; Audio bitrate: 128kbps"; "15 mins maximum, 3 seconds minimum"; "File size: 300MB maximum"; "Required aspect ratio is between 0.01:1 and 10:1 but we recommend 9:16 to avoid cropping or blank space"; container "MOV or MP4 (MPEG-4 Part 14), no edit lists, moov atom at the front of the file". Video is supplied via public video_url or a resumable upload session.

findings.claim: Meta's Facebook Reels Publishing API (a separate product) gives the closest thing to an encoder recipe: 1080x1920 recommended (min 540x960), 24-60 fps fixed frame rate, progressive, closed GOP 2-5 s, 4:2:0, H.264/H.265 (VP9, AV1 also), AAC Low Complexity 48 kHz stereo 128 kbps+, 3-90 s.
findings.evidence: Reels Publishing API (search summary): "Minimum is 540 x 960 pixels"; "Frame Rate: 24 to 60 frames per second"; "Video Settings: Chroma subsampling 4:2:0, closed GOP (2-5 seconds), compression H.264, H.265 (VP9, AV1 are also supported), fixed frame rate, progressive scan"; audio "48 kHz and 128kbs+ bitrate, stereo, and AAC Low Complexity"; duration 3 to 90 seconds (Facebook, not Instagram).

findings.claim: Meta's own H.264 level guidance (Live Video API) is Level 4.1 for 1080p up to 30 fps and Level 4.2 for 1080p60, with 3,000-6,000 kbps (30 fps) and 4,500-9,000 kbps (60 fps) for live streams.
findings.evidence: Live Video API reference (search summary): "1080p @ 60 FPS at 1920x1080 with a 4,500-9,000 Kbps video bitrate range", 1080p30 "3,000-6,000 kbps"; "H.264 at Level 4.1 for up to 30 FPS and Level 4.2 for 60 FPS". This is a streaming spec, used here only for level selection.

findings.claim: Instagram Help Center (consumer) Reels requirements: aspect ratio between 1.91:1 and 9:16; minimum 30 fps; minimum 720 px resolution; recording/editing up to 20 minutes, but Reels over 3 minutes are not recommended to new audiences; boosting a Reel requires 90 s or less and 9:16.
findings.evidence: Reel size & aspect ratios page: "You can upload a reel with an aspect ratio between 1.91:1 and 9:16" and Reels "should have a minimum frame rate of 30 FPS (frames per second) and minimum resolution of 720 pixels". Record a reel page: "You can record and edit videos up to 20 minutes with Instagram Reels" and "Reels over 3 minutes won't be recommended to new audiences". Boost page: "Reels must be 90 seconds or less and have a full-screen (9:16) vertical format". Creators blog (2025): 3-minute reels became eligible for recommendation (previously only up to 90 s).

findings.claim: Instagram's recommendation eligibility penalises low-resolution, watermarked, bordered, muted or majority-text reels, so exported files should be full-frame 9:16 without letterboxing or third-party watermarks.
findings.evidence: Instagram Creators blog: recommends "high-resolution, 9 x 16 vertical videos with no borders, where text does not cover the majority of the screen"; Instagram avoids recommending "low-resolution or watermarked reels, reels that are muted or contain borders, reels that are majority text".

findings.claim: Instagram/Facebook Reels accept HDR uploads from phones (since July 2023); the IG API spec mentions only 4:2:0 chroma and says nothing about colour primaries, so SDR BT.709 is the only spec-neutral choice.
findings.evidence: Meta Newsroom, July 2023: people can upload HDR videos from their phones to Reels and play them back in full HDR, described as the earliest of Meta's efforts to add HDR support across its apps. IG User Media spec lists "4:2:0 chroma subsampling" with no colour-space requirement.

findings.claim: TikTok Content Posting API restrictions (official): MP4 (recommended), WebM, MOV; H.264 (recommended), H.265, VP8, VP9; 23-60 fps; each dimension 360-4096 px; max 4 GB; developer upload ceiling 10 minutes; the per-creator limit (3, 5 or 10 minutes) must be read from max_video_post_duration_sec; no audio spec is published.
findings.evidence: Media Transfer Guide (search summary quoting): "Supported media formats: MP4 (recommended) WebM MOV; Supported codecs: H.264 (recommended) H.265 VP8 VP9"; "Framerate restrictions: Minimum of 23 FPS Maximum of 60 FPS"; picture size at least 360 px and at most 4096 px for height and width; "Size restrictions: Maximum of 4GB"; "The longest video a developer can send via the initialize Upload Video endpoint is 10 minutes"; "all TikTok creators can post 3-minute videos, while some have access to post 5-minute or 10-minute videos"; Direct Post: "API clients must check if the duration of the to-be-posted video follows the max_video_post_duration_sec returned in the creator_info API"; chunks 5-64 MB (final up to 128 MB), 1-1000 chunks; "Each user access_token is limited to 6 requests per minute"; "at most 5 pending shares within any 24-hour period"; Direct Post Content-Type values video/mp4, video/quicktime, video/webm. Audio codec/sample rate/bitrate not documented.

findings.claim: TikTok Studio (web) manual upload requirements (official): MP4 or WebM, 720x1280 or higher, up to 30 minutes, under 10 GB; web uploads are not trimmed; an 'Upload HD' switch enables 1080p in select countries. MOV is not listed for web upload.
findings.evidence: TikTok Support, Tools for creators: "Uploaded videos must be: In MP4 or WebM file format, 720x1280 resolution or higher, up to 30 minutes in length, less than 10 GB"; Making a post: "When you upload a video on your web browser, your entire video will be uploaded. To change the length of the video, upload your video in the TikTok app"; Newsroom: "Upload HD" switch on the Publishing page under "More options"; "In select countries, people can now choose to upload their videos in 1080p".

findings.claim: TikTok ad (In-Feed) specs, relevant only if the owner later promotes posts: 9:16 at >=540x960; .mp4/.mov/.mpeg/.3gp/.avi; auction non-Spark ads up to 10 minutes; <=500 MB; >=516 kbps; reservation in-feed ads 5-60 s (9-15 s recommended) with >=2,500 kbps.
findings.evidence: Auction In-Feed Ads: "File formats: .mp4, .mov, .mpeg, .3gp .avi. Video duration: up to 10 minutes. File size: Less than or equal to 500 MB. findings.evidence: TechCrunch 2022-02-28: TikTok rolled out uploads of up to 10 minutes after raising the cap from 3 minutes in 2021; TechCrunch 2023-10-23: testing 15-minute uploads with select users; TechCrunch 2024-01-24: testing 30-minute uploads in beta apps. TikTok Support page (above) lists "up to 30 minutes" for TikTok Studio web uploads.

findings.claim: Instagram API publishing volume limit is documented inconsistently (100 vs 50 API-published posts per 24-hour moving period); 2026 changelog entries (Trial Reels, is_ai_generated label) do not change Reels file specs.

implementation_decision:
Studio Assistant renders at exactly 1080x1920 (9:16, square pixels) and uses ONE layout model that is the conservative union of Meta's official percentages (14% top / 35% bottom / 6% sides) and the most conservative widely-cited reading of TikTok's official in-feed template (240 top / 660 bottom / 120 sides / 300 px right in the lower frame). Pixel decisions (origin top-left):

UI EXCLUSION BANDS (never place text, logos, CTAs, subtitles here):
- Top band: y < 270 (IG 14% = 269; TikTok 240).
- Bottom band: y >= 1248 (IG 35% = 672 px from bottom; TikTok 660).
- Side bleed: x < 120 and x > 960 everywhere (TikTok 120; IG 65).
- Right action-button column: x > 780 for y >= 840 (TikTok 180-px icon column inside the 120-px margin from y~840; IG lower-right block ~21%/227 px wide in the bottom 40%).

TEXT-SAFE RECTANGLES exposed to the planner/renderer:
- R_strict (default for everything): x 120-780, y 270-1248 (660 x 978). Any text box the renderer emits must be fully inside R_strict unless it qualifies for R_head.
- R_head (titles/hooks/logos whose box bottom <= 840): x 120-960, y 270-840 (840 x 570). This is clear of both platforms' button columns.
- Subtitles/captions: centred at x = 540, max width 480 (x 300-780), bottom-anchored with box bottom <= 1248 (default baseline band y 1100-1248), minimum font size 56 px, 2-3 words per line, drop-shadow or pill background for legibility. Centring at 540 with 480 width keeps them centred on screen while still inside R_strict.
- Logo/watermark: top-right of R_head, right edge at x 960, top at y 270 (clear of both top bars and the right-hand icons). Never a third-party-style watermark (hurts IG recommendations).
- Subject framing (soft, not enforced): keep faces/the haircut within y 270-1440 and x 0-940; the UI overlays are translucent so partial overlap of the subject is tolerable, text is not.
- Previews: overlay a dimmed-band PNG of the exclusion bands (two toggles: 'TikTok' and 'Reels') on the five preview renders so the owner can see what the apps cover; the exported file never contains the overlay.

EXPORT PRESET (single universal file for both platforms; FFmpeg):
- Scale/crop every source to 1080x1920 (crop, never letterbox; setsar=1). Do not export 4K (IG max width 1920 would reject a 2160-wide file).
- Video: libx264, -profile:v high, -level 4.1 at <=30 fps or 4.2 at 60 fps, -pix_fmt yuv420p, progressive, constant frame rate (-fps_mode cfr). Default 30 fps (satisfies IG Help 'minimum 30 FPS', IG API 23-60, FB Reels 24-60, TikTok API 23-60); offer 60 fps only when every source clip is >=50 fps; 24/25/50 fps sources are conformed to 30 (or 60). Closed GOP of 2 s (-g 60/-keyint_min 60 at 30 fps, -g 120 at 60 fps, -sc_threshold 0, open_gop=0), -preset slow, -crf 18 with VBV cap -maxrate 20M -bufsize 40M (30 fps) or -maxrate 24M -bufsize 48M (60 fps); peak stays under IG's 25 Mbps max and far above TikTok's 516/2,500 kbps minimums. Colour: SDR only, tag -color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 -colorspace bt709 -color_range tv; tone-map HDR sources (iPhone HLG/Dolby Vision 8.4, PQ) to BT.709 at ingest (zscale/tonemap or libplacebo). No HDR export because TikTok's HDR handling is undocumented.
- Audio: AAC-LC, 48 kHz, 2 channels, 128 kbps (the literal IG value and FB '128kbps+'), loudness-normalised (-14 LUFS integrated target), single audio track.
- Container: MP4, -movflags +faststart+negative_cts_offsets -use_editlist 0 (moov atom at the front, no edit lists, per IG spec), one video + one audio track, .mp4 extension (TikTok web upload does not list MOV).
- Duration: min 5 s; templates target 15-60 s; hard cap 180 s (3 min) so the file is eligible for IG recommendation to new audiences and fits every TikTok creator tier (3-minute floor, max_video_post_duration_sec); warn when > 90 s (IG boost limit). For 90-180 s exports lower -maxrate to 12M so the file stays under 300 MB.
- File size guard: reject/re-encode if > 300 MB (IG API max); this automatically satisfies TikTok ads (500 MB), TikTok API (4 GB) and TikTok Studio (10 GB).
- Post-export validation (ffprobe): 1080x1920, yuv420p, h264 High@4.1/4.2, CFR 30 or 60, GOP <= 2 s closed, AAC 48 kHz stereo, bt709 tags, moov before mdat, no elst, duration 5-180 s, size <= 300 MB. Fail the job with a plain-language message if any check fails.
- Store the safe-zone constants in one shared module (packages/video/safe-zones) with the source citations as comments and a 'reviewed on' date, since both platforms change UI without notice; recheck roughly every 6 months by downloading TikTok's in-feed safe-zone ZIP and Meta's Reels safe-zone checker and re-measuring.
account_requirements: Stage A (manual posting, the owner uploads the exported MP4 from their phone or TikTok Studio): no developer or ad accounts needed. TikTok Studio web upload accepts MP4/WebM, >=720x1280, <=30 min, <10 GB; the owner should turn on 'Upload HD' (1080p, select countries). Instagram app upload: 9:16, >=720 px, >=30 fps per Help Center.

If Studio Assistant later auto-publishes to TikTok (Content Posting API): a TikTok for Developers app with the Content Posting API product and video.publish (direct post) and/or video.upload scopes, user OAuth per staff account, a query to creator_info before every post to honour max_video_post_duration_sec and the creator's privacy options, chunked upload rules (5-64 MB chunks, <=1000 chunks, <=4 GB), rate limits (6 requests/min per user token, <=5 pending shares per 24 h), and file restrictions (MP4 H.264 recommended, 23-60 fps, 360-4096 px, <=10 min). Known from TikTok's docs but NOT re-verified this session: unaudited apps can only post with private (SELF_ONLY) visibility until the app passes TikTok's audit, so public direct posting requires app review.

If Studio Assistant later auto-publishes Reels (Instagram Graph API / Instagram API with Instagram Login): the barber's Instagram must be a professional (Business or Creator) account (standard Meta requirement; not re-verified this session), a Meta app with the content-publishing permission (instagram_business_content_publish or instagram_content_publish) which needs Meta App Review/advanced access to publish for accounts outside the app's test roles, a publicly reachable HTTPS video_url (or a resumable upload session) for the REELS container, compliance with the Reel spec (moov atom first, no edit lists, <=25 Mbps, 3 s-15 min, <=300 MB), and the per-account cap of 100 (docs also say 50) API-published posts per 24-hour moving period.

If the owner ever boosts/promotes the videos: TikTok Ads Manager account and in-feed ad specs (>=540x960, <=500 MB, >=516 kbps auction / >=2,500 kbps reservation, 5-60 s reservation or up to 10 min auction); Instagram Boost requires the Reel to be <=90 s and 9:16 per the Help Center (page may be stale). Ad safe zones are stricter than organic and are already covered by R_strict.

Music: platforms' commercial-music rules are out of scope here, but exported audio must be a single AAC-LC 48 kHz stereo track; keep the licensing model from the other research thread in mind before adding any music bed.
uncertainties: No page could be fetched in full: every official and third-party host (ads.tiktok.com, developers.tiktok.com, support.tiktok.com, developers.facebook.com, www.facebook.com, help.instagram.com, cadenus.io, whymatters.co.uk) failed DNS resolution in the sandbox, so all evidence is from WebSearch summaries that quote the pages. Wording may be paraphrased; verify on the live pages before publishing these numbers in product copy.

TikTok's actual template pixel values were not measured: the 240/660/120/300 figures are third-party readings of TikTok's official 720x1280 in-feed template, and other third parties give 130/484/140/44 or 150/440/60. One site claims TikTok replaced the template in April 2025 (no caption-length variants); unverified. The owner should download the ZIP from the Auction In-Feed Ads help page and re-measure.

No Meta 'Awareness Video ad specs on Instagram Reels' page surfaced; the official 14%/35%/6% figures come from the Reels IMAGE ad spec page (one third party quotes a Reels video page with the same numbers). Whether Meta's diagram also blocks a lower-right corner (~21% x ~40%) is reported only by third parties.

Meta's safe-zone percentages are ad guidance (profile icon + CTA). For organic Reels the bottom overlay is usually smaller (~400-450 px) unless the caption is long; R_strict is deliberately conservative and may push subtitles higher than some creators prefer.
Instagram Help says 'minimum frame rate of 30 FPS' while the Graph API says 23-60 fps; 24/25 fps files are accepted in practice but we standardise on 30 fps to satisfy the stricter wording.

Instagram Reels maximum length: Help Center says record/edit up to 20 minutes (undated), Graph API says 15 minutes (page ~600 days old), Boost page says <=90 s (possibly stale after the 2025 3-minute change). Our 180 s cap sidesteps the conflict.

TikTok HDR: no official statement on HDR upload acceptance or tone-mapping was found (third parties say TikTok plays HDR on capable phones but publishes no upload requirements). Meta supports HDR phone uploads (2023) but the API spec is silent on colour primaries. SDR BT.709 is chosen to avoid washed-out HLG/Dolby Vision uploads.
TikTok publishes no audio spec for the Content Posting API; AAC-LC 48 kHz is inferred from Meta's spec and general practice.
A 60-minute TikTok limit could not be confirmed from any official source; TikTok Support states 30 minutes for web upload; the API ceiling is 10 minutes.

Unaudited TikTok apps being limited to private posts, and Instagram requiring a professional account for API publishing, are from prior knowledge of the docs and were not re-verified in this session's searches.

Whether Meta unified Stories and Reels safe zones in 2026 (one blog claims so) is unverified; Instagram's 2025-2026 profile-grid thumbnail change (and its effect on which part of a 9:16 frame is visible as the cover) could not be confirmed from official sources, so no cover-crop rule is included.

Exact 'last updated' dates were not visible in any summary; the search tool reported approximate ages only (TikTok Media Transfer Guide ~100 days old; IG User Media ~600 days old; TikTok help articles 1-2 years old).

findings.claim: TikTok Creative Center has no official public API; every 'Creative Center API' found is a third-party scraper (Apify actors, TikHub), not a TikTok product.
findings.evidence: Search over business-api.tiktok.com and developers.tiktok.com surfaced no official endpoint for Creative Center hashtags/sounds. A secondary guide states the Creative Center is TikTok's public hub at ads.tiktok.com/business/creativecenter and that 'for API access the Creative Center has no public API, while the Commercial Content API is documented on developers.tiktok.com'. Apify listings describe 'scraping TikTok Creative Center public data by country and time window'.

findings.claim: TikTok's Terms of Service prohibit automated scraping/extraction of any data from the platform without TikTok's written approval, which rules out scraping Creative Center for Studio Assistant.
findings.evidence: US ToS (paraphrased from summary): users may not 'scrape, crawl, export or otherwise extract any data or content in any form, for any purpose, from the Platform using any automated system or software, including automated "bots," except as approved in writing by TikTok USDS Joint Venture'. Global ToS bars using 'automated scripts to collect information from or otherwise interact with the Services'. EEA ToS bars 'extracting data using any automated system or software that is not provided by TikTok or approved in writing by TikTok'. TikTok's privacy blog states 'unauthorized data scraping violates TikTok's Terms of Service'. Developer Terms s.3(k): automated means only as the developer documentation describes; robots/spiders for unauthorized purposes barred.

findings.claim: Creative Center's Trends section changed in 2025-2026: trending Songs and some trend endpoints were reportedly removed/'deprecated', and Trend Discovery appears to need a TikTok for Business login beyond a small logged-out preview (third-party reports only).
findings.evidence: Oct 2026 DEV post: old Creative Center trend endpoints 'now return "deprecated"'; 'the old Songs page now redirects to hashtags'; logged-out Trends 'shows the top 3 hashtags per country'. July 2026 third-party audit: Trend Discovery panels returned 'Data error, please click to reload' when anonymous; verdict 'preview-without-login rather than either fully public or fully gated'. Another source: logged-out Trends menu lists Hashtag, Video and Creator (marked 'coming soon'). None of this is TikTok's own documentation.

findings.claim: TikTok Research API is academic/non-profit only, limited to listed regions (US, EEA, UK, Canada, Switzerland, EU non-profits, Brazil youth-safety); Australia is not listed and a commercial barber app is ineligible.
findings.evidence: Eligibility summary: 'Academic institutions in the U.S., EEA, UK, Canada, or Switzerland qualify, as do not-for-profit or independent research bodies in the EU'; applicants 'must work independently of commercial interests and pursue a public-interest mission on a not-for-profit or non-commercial basis'; requires endorsement letter, ethical review evidence, funding disclosure; decisions ~4 weeks; 'eligibility is decided by TikTok at its discretion'. 'Commercial research should use the separate Commercial Content Library and Commercial Content API, which are not the Research Tools.'

findings.claim: TikTok Commercial Content API is an ads/commercial-content transparency repository (DSA Art. 39), Europe-only data, narrow permitted purposes; it does not expose trending sounds or hashtags.
findings.evidence: Summary: 'supports advertiser-name or keyword searches over the Commercial Content Library'; fields include 'the advertising creative, dates the ad ran, main targeting parameters such as age and gender, and the number of people served the ad'; covers posts with 'a paid partnership label or promotional label'; 'At this time, only data from Europe is available'; requires TikTok for Developers account and application ('hear back within 2 working days'); Developer Terms define 'CCL Purposes' as 'supervising and researching emerging risks brought about by the distribution of advertising and/or commercial content online'; 'offered under Article 39 of the EU Digital Services Act'.

findings.claim: Meta now documents an official Instagram Audio API (apps using Facebook Login) with an endpoint described as searching/retrieving trending audio, plus a media_audio_type field on IG Media; this is new (changelog entry dated 2026).
findings.evidence: Changelog (paraphrased from summary): 'Introducing the Instagram Audio API for apps using Facebook Login. The API lets your app search for and retrieve audio', including 'original sounds from Reels and royalty-free Meta Sound Collection tracks', to 'attach them to Reels at creation time'. Endpoints: 'GET /ig_audio?audio_type={music|original_sound} — Search or retrieve trending audio' and 'GET /{ig_audio_id} — Get metadata for a specific audio asset'. Also 'GET /ig_audio?product=ADS&purpose=AUDIO_COPYRIGHT_REPLACEMENT' for ads. New field 'media_audio_type — The type of audio used in the media: MUSIC ... or ORIGINAL_SOUND'. Releasebot dates the entry June 1, 2026. Several older third-party posts claim Meta's API 'doesn't expose trending audio', which predates or ignores this entry.

findings.claim: Instagram hashtag search (ig_hashtag_search -> top_media/recent_media) is an official, permitted way to see what is being posted under barber hashtags, capped at 30 unique hashtags per 7 days per professional account.
findings.evidence: Meta reference: 'you can query a maximum of 30 unique hashtags within a 7 day period'; cap is per Instagram professional account in user_id; hashtag IDs are static and global; available for the 'Instagram API with Facebook Login'; feature 'Instagram Public Content Access', permission 'instagram_basic' (plus ads_management, business_management or pages_read_engagement if Page role granted via Business Manager); 'generic error for any queries that include hashtags that we have deemed sensitive or offensive'.

findings.claim: YouTube Data API videos.list chart=mostPopular is official and cheap (1 unit) but since July 21, 2025 it no longer reflects general 'Trending Now'; it returns Trending Music, Movies and Gaming chart videos, and has no Shorts filter.
findings.evidence: Revision history entry (July 10, 2025): 'As of July 21, 2025, YouTube will adjust the content that is returned by the video.list method's mostPopular chart. In the past, the mostPopular chart reflected the videos featured on the Trending Now list. Now, the mostPopular chart will feature videos from the Trending Music, Movies, and Gaming charts.' 'This API change is in tandem with the deprecation of YouTube's Trending page.' Reference: mostPopular 'returns the most popular videos for the specified content region and video category'; regionCode 'can only be used together with the chart parameter'; chart is a filter parameter and cannot be combined with id/myRating. No videos.list parameter for Shorts was found; filtering must be client-side (e.g., by duration).

findings.claim: YouTube Data API default quota is 10,000 units/day; videos.list costs 1 unit; exceeding the default requires an API Compliance Audit; YouTube may audit/monitor use and limits extended quota to the approved use case.
findings.evidence: 'default allocation of 10,000 units per day'; 'A call to this method [videos.list] has a quota cost of 1 unit'; 'All developers using YouTube's API Services must complete an API Compliance Audit in order to be granted more than the default quota allocation of 10,000 units'; Developer Policies 8-7: additional quota 'only for the approved use case'; 8-10: 'YouTube reserves the right to survey, monitor, and/or audit your access to or use of YouTube API Services'. June 3, 2026 revision added videos.batchGetStats (1 unit, own 10,000/day bucket). Quotas reset at midnight Pacific Time.

findings.claim: Google Trends has an official API only as an invite-only alpha (announced July 24, 2025); applications are via a form, aimed at researchers, journalists and developers; data is a rolling ~1800-day window, consistently scaled, aggregated by day/week/month/year; still alpha as of late 2026.
findings.evidence: Launch post (Daniel Waisberg and Hadas Jacobi): access 'will open on a rolling basis to a limited number of developers over the coming weeks'. Application page: 'accepting applications for alpha testers through a form'; applicants 'should have a use case in mind and be able to provide direct feedback'; API 'helping researchers, journalists, and developers conduct better analysis on search behavior and trends'; 'limited the data to a rolling window of 1800 days (~5 years)'; zh-tw mirror of the page states 'consistently scaled data' and aggregation 'by day, week, month, and year'. Third parties checked Oct 2026 report it 'is still an alpha' and 'invite-only', 'many applicants reporting no response'.

findings.claim: Google Trends 'Trending Now' has a public RSS feed that third parties use without auth, but Google's terms for automated consumption of it were not retrieved; pytrends' trending_searches reportedly returns 404 in 2026.
findings.evidence: Third-party reports: the RSS path 'needs no auth, isn't disallowed by robots.txt (checked 2026-10-21)'; a scraper listing claims robots.txt 'disallows only the /explore pages'. implementation_decision: Studio Assistant's Trends view must be split into two visually distinct sections and never blend them. SECTION A, 'Live signals' (each card shows source name, fetched_at timestamp in Australia/Melbourne time, a 'stale after' TTL, and a link out; if a fetch fails show an 'unavailable' state rather than silently serving old data as fresh): (1) Instagram hashtag watch via the Instagram API with Facebook Login using the owner's own professional account: a fixed watch-list of at most 30 hashtags per rolling 7 days (e.g., #barber, #skinfade, #taperfade, #barbertransformation, #melbournebarber, #ivanhoe), calling ig_hashtag_search once per tag (cache the static IDs) then top_media; label as 'Top posts under #tag — Instagram, fetched <date>'. (2) Instagram Audio API GET /ig_audio?audio_type=music|original_sound behind a feature flag, labelled 'Instagram audio search results — Instagram, fetched <date>' only after the owner's app is confirmed to have the required Facebook-Login permissions; do not call it 'trending' unless the live reference page confirms the endpoint returns a trending ranking. (3) YouTube Data API v3 videos.list chart=mostPopular regionCode=AU (1 unit/call, cache 6-12 h) labelled honestly as 'YouTube AU popular chart (music/movies/gaming) — YouTube, fetched <date>' because since 21 July 2025 it is not a general trending list; optionally add a low-frequency search.list query for 'barber'/'skin fade' restricted to short videos, after verifying search.list's quota cost on the official page, and filter Shorts client-side by duration. (4) Google Trends: no automated ingestion in v1. Provide a deep link to trends.google.com (geo=AU) and have the owner apply for the Trends API alpha; only add the Trending Now RSS feed if Google's terms are confirmed to permit it. TikTok: no live data at all. The Research API is academic/non-commercial and does not list Australia; the Commercial Content API is Europe-only ads data for DSA purposes; Creative Center has no API and TikTok's ToS bar automated extraction; third-party scrapers (Apify/TikHub) are not acceptable. Instead provide a 'Browse TikTok Creative Center' button that opens ads.tiktok.com in the owner's own TikTok for Business login, plus a manual 'Note a trend' form where staff record a sound/hashtag they saw (stored with who/when, labelled 'Noted by staff'). SECTION B, 'Curated references' (static JSON in the repo, header 'Curated by Studio Assistant — last reviewed 2026-11-12', never worded as 'trending now'): the seven sourced evergreen formats (before/after reveal with commentary; ASMR fade process; satisfying line-up / 360 finish; transformation with client reaction; educational technique explainer; ultra-fast cut montage; timelapse with trending audio cross-posted), each with its source link, a one-line shot list, and a client-consent reminder. Speed-ramp montage, POV and client-story variants may be included only if tagged 'editor suggestion — no external source' until a source is added. Build a scheduled job that re-fetches Section A sources, stores raw responses with fetched_at, and surfaces per-source error states; log which account/token made each call for audit.
account_requirements: Google Cloud project with YouTube Data API v3 enabled and an API key (public data only, no OAuth needed for videos.list/search.list); default quota 10,000 units/day resets at midnight Pacific; stay within it so no API Compliance Audit is needed; comply with YouTube API Services Terms and Developer Policies (verify data-storage/refresh and display rules on the official page, which could not be fetched).

Meta developer app (Business type) using the Instagram API with Facebook Login; the owner's Instagram account must be a professional account (Business or Creator) linked to a Facebook Page; permissions instagram_basic, pages_show_list, pages_read_engagement (+ business_management or ads_management if Page role comes via Business Manager); 'Instagram Public Content Access' feature for ig_hashtag_search; Standard Access suffices while the app only serves accounts the owner manages, so App Review and business verification are only needed if the app is later used for accounts the owner does not own; long-lived Page/User token stored server-side.
For the Instagram Audio API: confirm on the live Meta reference which permissions/features ig_audio requires for Facebook-Login apps before enabling the feature flag (not confirmed in this research).

Google Trends API alpha: owner submits the application form on developers.google.com/search/apis/trends with a stated use case and willingness to give feedback; access is limited and not guaranteed; no fee published.

TikTok: a free TikTok for Business login for manually browsing Creative Center; no TikTok developer app, Research API or Commercial Content API is applicable (ineligible: commercial use, Australia not in Research API regions, Commercial Content API is Europe-only ads data).
Client consent process (verbal or written) before posting transformation/reaction clips, reflected as a checklist item in the curated formats.
uncertainties: No official page was read in full: developers.tiktok.com, ads.tiktok.com, www.tiktok.com, developers.google.com, developers.facebook.com and searchenginejournal.com all failed DNS resolution in the sandbox (must be allowed in network settings), and the shared WebSearch budget ran out before the last six queries. All quotes are from search-engine summaries of those pages.

Instagram Audio API: exact changelog date (Releasebot says June 1, 2026; summary dating ambiguous), required permissions/App Review status, and whether 'trending audio' is a platform-wide ranking or a filtered search are unconfirmed.

YouTube Developer Policies on how long API data may be cached/displayed and attribution requirements were not retrieved; the search summary's claim of a '100 calls per day' cap on search.list conflicts with the historically documented 100-units-per-call cost and must be checked on the official quota calculator.
No official YouTube Data API parameter identifies Shorts; client-side duration filtering is a workaround, not documented behaviour.

TikTok Creative Center changes (deprecated trend endpoints, removed Songs page, login gating of Trend Discovery) come only from third-party blogs dated July-Oct 2026; TikTok's own help pages were not retrieved. Whether Creative Center's TikTok for Business terms add further restrictions beyond the general ToS is unknown.

TikTok Research API regional eligibility list has changed over time (Brazil added); the Commercial Content API 'Europe only' statement came from a page the search engine flagged as ~1,354 days old, so expansion in 2025-2026 cannot be ruled out, though nothing found suggests Australia or trend data were added.

Google Trends: the exact alpha eligibility profile text, the alpha's terms of use, and whether the Trending Now RSS feed may be consumed programmatically under Google's terms were not retrieved; robots.txt claims are third-party.

Barber formats: 'speed ramp montage', 'POV' and 'client story' were not described by any retrieved source; the Vagaro and Socialmon idea lists were surfaced but not quoted. The six/seven sourced formats rest on marketing blogs whose performance claims are unverified.
The Higgsfield MCP server in this session exposes a 'tiktok_music_trending' tool; its data source and licensing were not investigated and it should not be assumed to be an official TikTok trend feed.

topic: Speech transcription provider options for short barber clips (only when speech is present): OpenAI /v1/audio/transcriptions models, timestamps, limits and pricing; Deepgram Nova-3 pre-recorded; AssemblyAI; local whisper.cpp / faster-whisper on a 4-vCPU worker; Anthropic audio input; speech-present gating. Researched 2026-11-14.

findings.claim: OpenAI's /v1/audio/transcriptions accepts these models as of November 2026: gpt-transcribe (the new recommended model), gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-12-15, whisper-1 and gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize.
findings.evidence: The API reference lists "gpt-transcribe, gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-12-15, whisper-1 (which is powered by our open source Whisper V2 model), and gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize". The file transcription guide calls gpt-transcribe the recommended model for transcribing recorded speech in its original language.

findings.claim: Only whisper-1 returns segment or word timestamps (response_format=verbose_json plus timestamp_granularities[]). The gpt-4o models return JSON only. No official page says gpt-transcribe returns timestamps.
findings.evidence: Guide: "The timestamp_granularities[] parameter is only supported for whisper-1." Also: "Existing integrations can use the deprecated whisper-1 model for word or segment timestamps until February 26, 2027." Reference: "response_format must be set verbose_json to use timestamp granularities"; granularities are "word, or segment"; "not available for gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize". For gpt-4o-transcribe and gpt-4o-mini-transcribe "the only supported format is json". Cookbook: the new model returns JSON, so do not assume text, verbose_json, srt or vtt still work; "Timestamps: retain a model and response format that explicitly support word or segment timestamps." The transcription guide's table: "Word timestamps or srt and vtt subtitles | whisper-1 with file transcription."

findings.claim: OpenAI is shutting down whisper-1, gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe and gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize on 2027-02-26 (notice given 2026-08-26). The replacements are gpt-transcribe or gpt-live-transcribe. No replacement for timestamps has been announced.
findings.evidence: Deprecations table: "Feb 26, 2027 | whisper-1 | Deprecated | gpt-live-transcribe or gpt-transcribe | Aug 26, 2026". The changelog adds gpt-4o-mini-transcribe to the same notice. gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-03-20 shuts down on Jan 20, 2027. The OpenAI CLI docs say: "Changing to the recommended transcription model doesn't preserve every output format or metadata field." A forum thread from November 2026 (not official) says word timestamps and SRT/VTT "currently point back to whisper-1" and asks for a roadmap. None was found.

findings.claim: OpenAI's upload limit is 25 MB. Accepted formats are flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav and webm. Larger files must be compressed or split.
findings.evidence: Guide: files can be up to 25 MB, and supported input formats include "flac, mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, ogg, wav, and webm". It suggests compressing or chunking files over the limit. Older cookbook pages leave out flac and ogg.

findings.claim: OpenAI transcription prices: gpt-transcribe $0.0045/min, whisper-1 $0.006/min, gpt-4o-transcribe $0.006/min, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe about $0.003/min. Its model page instead quotes token prices of $1.25 input and $5.00 output per 1M tokens. gpt-live-transcribe is $0.017/min.
findings.evidence: gpt-transcribe model page: "$0.0045" per minute of transcription audio. whisper-1 page: "Transcription — Cost / minute — $0.006". The search summary of the pricing page lists gpt-4o-transcribe $0.006/minute and gpt-4o-mini-transcribe $0.003/minute. A memetik.ai guide dated September 2026 also gives "$0.0045 per minute / $0.00008 per second" for gpt-transcribe.

findings.claim: gpt-transcribe accepts context, keyword and multi-language hints instead of the old language parameter. It is not offered on the free tier.
findings.evidence: Model page: accepts "unstructured context, keyword hints, and multiple language hints". Rate limits: "free tier is not supported"; Build 5,000 RPM, Launch 10,000 RPM, Grow 30,000 RPM. Cookbook: "Replace the legacy language hint with the new-model languages array"; sending both language and languages is listed as a common error.

findings.claim: OpenAI does not keep /v1/audio/transcriptions data for abuse monitoring and does not train on API data by default.
findings.evidence: The data-controls table lists /v1/audio/transcriptions with no training use, "None" abuse-monitoring retention and "None" application-state retention, and marks it Zero Data Retention eligible. Separately, API data "is not used to train or improve OpenAI models unless you explicitly opt in" (effective 2023-03-01).

findings.claim: Deepgram's pre-recorded API is one synchronous call: POST https://api.deepgram.com/v1/listen, with the model and options as query parameters. It returns word timestamps in seconds, and grouped utterances when requested.
findings.evidence: Reference: POST https://api.deepgram.com/v1/listen for pre-recorded audio, with model=nova-3 and smart_format=true in the URL. The response has metadata, then results.channels[].alternatives[] holding the transcript and words[]. Each word has start and end (seconds from the start of the audio), confidence, and punctuated_word when smart formatting is on. utterances=true adds results.utterances[] with start, end, speaker, transcript and words[]. A new utterance starts after 0.8 s of silence by default (utt_split changes this). diarize=true adds speaker IDs. Sources disagree on where utterances sit: blog and SDK examples put them at results.utterances, while the reference example shows only channels.

findings.claim: Deepgram Nova-3 pre-recorded costs $0.0043–0.0048 per minute on pay-as-you-go, billed per second. New accounts get a $200 credit that does not expire. Uploads can be up to 2 GB.
findings.evidence: The cached official pricing page shows Nova-3 Monolingual at "$0.0048 per minute on Pay as you go (was $0.0077)" and Multilingual at $0.0058. It describes a "Free $200 credit then pay-as-you-go" with no minimums, covering roughly 43,000 minutes, and says the credit "does not expire". Several 2026 third-party guides, plus one that checked the page on 2026-09-02, give $0.0043/min for pre-recorded and $0.0077/min for streaming. Diarisation is included free on pre-recorded audio. Getting Started page: "Maximum 2 GB"; requests exceeding 10 minutes (Nova) return a 504.

findings.claim: Deepgram changes in 2026: Nova-3 multilingual now covers 55 languages via language=multi.
findings.evidence: Changelog 2026-10-23: "55 languages, one model, accessed via model=nova-3&language=multi". Self-hosted deployments keep the existing 10-language model.

findings.claim: AssemblyAI is asynchronous: you submit a job (POST /v2/transcript with audio_url, or upload first via /v2/upload) and then poll for the result. Pre-recorded audio costs $0.21/hr on Universal-3.5 Pro and $0.15/hr on Universal-2. Slam-1 is deprecated. Word timestamps are in milliseconds.
findings.evidence: Pricing reference: Universal-3.5 Pro $0.21/hr and Universal-2 $0.15/hr for pre-recorded audio, "prorated to the second". Slam-1 is marked deprecated. Diarisation adds $0.02/hr. API reference: speech_models is an optional array of universal-3-5-pro and universal-2, defaulting to ["universal-3-5-pro","universal-2"] as an ordered fallback list. Limits: 5 GB and 10 hours via URL, 2.2 GB via /v2/upload. Docs: each words[] entry has text, start, end (milliseconds), confidence and speaker. One third-party guide says the 2026 rates were "Not verified as of September 2026".

findings.claim: As of November 2026 the Claude Messages API does not accept audio input. Speech has to be transcribed elsewhere and passed to Claude as text.
findings.evidence: The Messages API reference describes request content as text and/or image (plus document blocks), with no audio. The OpenAI SDK compatibility page says audio and file inputs are not supported: a request with an input_audio or file content part "returns a 400 error". Release notes through API version 2026-10-21 add no audio input. The 2026-09-01 note covers watermarking of audio Claude generates through code execution, which is output, not input. The Transparency Hub lists text (including voice dictation, which is text) and image inputs.

findings.claim: Running Whisper locally on CPU should be fast enough for short clips, but there is no published 4-vCPU benchmark. Expect several times real-time with small or base int8 models.
findings.evidence: faster-whisper README: small model, int8, "8 threads on an Intel Core i7-12700K" transcribed a 13-minute recording in 1m42s using 1477 MB RAM (about 7.6x real time). whisper.cpp small on an Apple M5 with 4 threads: RTF 0.3068 (3.3x real time). On an RK3588 ARM board with 8 threads: about 2x real time and 889 MB. A third-party guide warns that shared vCPU plans won't reach desktop CPU figures. No 4-vCPU x86 benchmark was found.

findings.claim: Both local engines have Silero VAD built in. whisper.cpp also gives word-level timing, but its word timestamps are marked experimental.
findings.evidence: faster-whisper: vad_filter runs Silero VAD to drop non-speech before transcription, configurable through vad_parameters. whisper.cpp: "--vad" with a Silero model passed via -vm (e.g. silero-v6.2.0), built in since May 2025 (issue #3003 / PR #3065). The README says -ml 1 gives word-level timestamps and marks the feature experimental. -ojf writes per-token offsets in milliseconds. A 2024 user report says the word timestamps were "pretty consistently off" without DTW.

findings.claim: Whisper-family models invent text when given silence, music or noise, so audio should be gated before transcription. no_speech_prob is only a secondary check.
findings.evidence: Researchers measured a "99.97%" hallucination rate for Whisper-large-v3 on UrbanSound8K non-speech clips, against 13.52% for Conformer-CTC. Community guidance: the default no_speech_threshold is 0.6 and segments with no_speech_prob > 0.5 are flagged, but borderline values go either way. A whisper.cpp issue: when a language is forced, the decoder can confidently emit a music token and no_speech_prob stays below 0.6. The usual fix is to put VAD in front of transcription.

findings.claim: Silero VAD costs almost nothing on CPU, so it can be a second gate after the existing DSP heuristic.
findings.evidence: README: a 30+ ms chunk "takes less than 1ms to be processed on a single CPU thread". An independent test measured a median of 220–240 µs per 32 ms chunk on a 2.1 GHz Xeon. Supported rates are 8000/16000 Hz for PyTorch JIT and 16000 Hz for ONNX. At 16 kHz the native window is 512 samples (32 ms).

findings.claim: Repo state: the config enum allows only 'none' and 'openai', and OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL defaults to 'whisper-1'. Ingest transcribes only when audio.speechLikely is true, a transcriber is set and the clip is at most 20 minutes. packages/ai/src is empty, so no transcriber exists yet.
findings.evidence: packages/config/src/index.ts:52-54: TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER z.enum(['none','openai']), OPENAI_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL default 'whisper-1'. apps/worker/src/handlers/ingest.ts:152-156 gates on audio.speechLikely and MAX_TRANSCRIPTION_SECONDS = 20*60, and extracts 16 kHz mono AAC at 48 kbps (under 8 MB for 20 min, well within 25 MB). packages/media/src/analysis/audio.ts SPEECH_HEURISTIC: speechLikely = speechConfidence >= 0.35 && speechSeconds >= 1.5. It uses ZCR 0.02–0.3, a 300–3400 Hz band ratio of at least 0.55 and an 8 dB syllabic swing, and its own comment admits "music can pass".

implementation_decision:
DEFAULT ADAPTER: Deepgram Nova-3 pre-recorded (TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER=deepgram). Reasons:
- It is the only hosted option researched that returns word and utterance timestamps synchronously in one request with no shutdown date. Captions must come from the transcript with real timings, and OpenAI's only timestamp model (whisper-1) shuts down on 2027-02-26, about 3.5 months from now.
- Cost is negligible for one studio: about $0.0024 per 30 s clip at $0.0048/min, roughly $0.24 for 100 clips a month. The non-expiring $200 credit covers about 43,000 minutes.

Concrete changes:
1) packages/config: change TRANSCRIPTION_PROVIDER to z.enum(['none','deepgram','openai','whispercpp']).default('none'). Add DEEPGRAM_API_KEY (server-only), DEEPGRAM_MODEL default 'nova-3', DEEPGRAM_LANGUAGE default 'en', and TRANSCRIPTION_COST_USD_PER_MIN (default 0.0048, the conservative end, for AiUsage estimates). If 'none' is selected or the key is missing, show an honest "Transcription needs setup — captions from speech are off" state.
2) packages/ai: add DeepgramTranscriber implementing Transcriber.
   - Call fetch POST https://api.deepgram.com/v1/listen?model=nova-3&language=en&smart_format=true&punctuate=true&utterances=true.
   - Body: the existing 16 kHz mono speech.m4a as raw bytes with Content-Type audio/mp4.
   - Pass the job's AbortSignal through. Retry 429/5xx with backoff, at most 3 attempts.
   - Map results.utterances[] to TranscriptSegment {startSec: start, endSec: end, text: transcript}. If utterances are missing, fall back to grouping channels[0].alternatives[0].words[] on gaps of 0.8 s or more. Keep words[] (start, end, confidence, punctuated_word) for word-timed captions.
   - Record provider 'deepgram', the model, the language and an estimated cost.
   - Idempotency: key the stored result by assetId plus the SHA-256 of the speech audio, so a retried job reuses the result instead of paying twice.
   - Write the parser against a recorded live response fixture, because sources disagree on where utterances sit.
3) OpenAI adapter, kept as an optional second choice: always use whisper-1 with response_format=verbose_json and timestamp_granularities[]=segment and =word, and map segments[] to TranscriptSegment. Config validation must reject gpt-transcribe, gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe and gpt-4o-transcribe-diarize for captions, because they return no documented timestamps. From 2027-02-26 (Australia/Melbourne), treat the OpenAI transcriber as unavailable and show "needs setup". Re-check before then whether OpenAI has published a timestamp path for gpt-transcribe.
4) Local adapter, optional and later: whisper.cpp whisper-cli with a ggml base.en or small.en model, --vad -vm <silero model>, -ojf, -ml 1 -sow, 4 threads, called from the worker with execFile and the AbortSignal. Use it only if the owner wants no third-party audio processor. Measure real-time factor on the actual 4-vCPU box with scripts/make-sample-footage.sh clips before enabling. Not the default because it needs a model download and native build, its word timestamps are experimental, and Whisper hallucinates on non-speech audio. faster-whisper would add a Python runtime to a Node worker, so prefer whisper.cpp.
5) AssemblyAI: not adopted. It is cheaper ($0.15–0.21/hr), but the upload, submit and poll flow adds a long-running poll loop for no meaningful saving at this volume. Leave it as a possible future adapter behind the same interface.
6) Anthropic: never send audio to Claude, because the Messages API has no audio input. Claude (the planner) only ever sees transcript text and segment timings.

SPEECH-PRESENT GATING, cheapest first:
- Stage 0: skip if there is no audio stream, the clip is over 20 min, or the owner marked the clip as music-only or "mute original sound".
- Stage 1 (exists, free): keep the ffmpeg silencedetect step and the DSP SPEECH_HEURISTIC (speechConfidence >= 0.35 and speechSeconds >= 1.5).
- Stage 2 (add, about 1 ms of CPU per second of audio): run Silero VAD ONNX through onnxruntime-node on the 16 kHz PCM already decoded in analyseAudio, in 512-sample windows. Call transcription only if VAD finds at least 1.0 s of speech in total at probability 0.5 or higher. Store vadSpeechSeconds on the analysis. This removes the music false positives the DSP heuristic admits by design.
- Stage 3 (post-filter, no extra cost): drop the transcript if the text is empty. For Deepgram, drop words with confidence below 0.5 and segments whose mean word confidence is below 0.6. For whisper-1, drop segments with no_speech_prob above 0.6 or avg_logprob below -1.0. Never caption from dropped segments, and log what was dropped.
These thresholds are starting points to tune on real studio clips (clippers, music and chatter), not documented values. Only Whisper's 0.6 no_speech_threshold default comes from a source.
account_requirements: Deepgram (the default adapter): create an account in the Deepgram Console and a project API key. Store it only on the worker as DEEPGRAM_API_KEY. The $200 non-expiring free credit applies first, then pay-as-you-go with no minimums, and adding a card is needed once the credit runs out. There is no app review or approval step.

OpenAI (optional, timestamps only until 2027-02-26): an OpenAI Platform account with billing or prepaid credit and an API key (OPENAI_API_KEY). The free tier does not support gpt-transcribe. Rate-limit tiers are Build, Launch and Grow. Zero Data Retention needs OpenAI's prior approval but is not needed here, because the docs list no abuse-monitoring retention for /v1/audio/transcriptions.
AssemblyAI (not adopted): it would need an account and API key on pay-as-you-go. No approval step was found.

Local whisper.cpp (optional): no account. Needs a build of whisper-cli on the worker image, a downloaded ggml Whisper model (base.en or small.en) and a Silero VAD ggml model, plus about 1–1.5 GB of RAM headroom on the 4-vCPU worker.
Anthropic: no requirement. Claude does not accept audio, so no Anthropic plan or feature unlocks transcription.

Recommended, not researched: the owner should tell clients and staff that the audio in filmed clips may be sent to a third-party speech-to-text processor (Deepgram, a US company) and get their consent before posting.
uncertainties: No official page was read in full. WebFetch failed with ENOTFOUND for platform.openai.com and developers.openai.com, so every claim relies on search summaries of official pages, some of them cached. To verify directly, allow developers.openai.com, platform.openai.com, deepgram.com, developers.deepgram.com, assemblyai.com and platform.claude.com in the session's network settings.

OpenAI: no source confirms or rules out that gpt-transcribe returns segment or word timestamps. The docs only say timestamp_granularities is whisper-1-only and that switching models does not preserve every output format. OpenAI may add a timestamp path before 2027-02-26, but no official timeline was found.

OpenAI pricing for gpt-4o-mini-transcribe conflicts: $0.003/min on the pricing page per the search summary, against $1.25/$5.00 per 1M tokens on its model page. This hardly matters, because that model has no timestamps.

The Deepgram Nova-3 pre-recorded price is either $0.0043/min (several 2026 guides and Deepgram blogs) or $0.0048/min (cached official page, possibly a streaming promotion). The live page was not read.

Deepgram: the exact nesting of utterances (results.utterances vs inside channels) differs between sources. The 'requests exceeding 10 minutes return 504' wording comes from a page about 895 days old and may mean processing time rather than audio length. The auth header format (Authorization: Token <key>) is from prior knowledge and was not re-verified in this session.

Deepgram: support for language=en-AU on Nova-3 monolingual was not confirmed, so the plan uses language=en. Accuracy on Australian accents and barbershop noise (clippers, music) has not been measured for any provider.
AssemblyAI: word start and end are in milliseconds per its docs, and its 2026 rates come from its own pricing reference, which one third party flagged as unverified.
Local CPU speed: no 4-vCPU x86 benchmark was found. The 7.6x real-time faster-whisper figure is from a dedicated 8-thread desktop i7-12700K, so it is an upper bound.

Anthropic: no 2026 release note adds audio input and the docs say audio is unsupported, but the search could not show every content-block type. Treat 'no audio input' as high but not certain confidence.

Data handling by Deepgram and AssemblyAI (retention, training opt-out, data region) was not researched. Neither was whether the Australian Privacy Act applies to this small business; recording consent was not researched either.
The gating thresholds (VAD at least 1.0 s at probability 0.5 or higher; confidence cut-offs) are engineering starting points, not values from any provider's documentation.
