findings.claim: Meta's official requirement is that the URL be public when Meta fetches it. The docs say nothing about signed query strings, redirects, Range, Content-Length, how many fetches Meta makes, or how long the URL must stay valid.
findings.evidence: From search snippets of Meta's docs. IG User Media, video_url: 'We cURL the video using the passed-in URL, so it must be on a public server.' Content Publishing guide: media used in publishing attempts 'must be hosted on a publicly accessible server at the time of the attempt.' I found no Meta text on signed URLs, 3xx handling, Range, Content-Length or fetch count. A community research issue reached the same conclusion: the docs 'are silent on redirects, content types, fetch counts, and how long the URL must stay up'.

findings.claim: Video fetching is asynchronous after POST /{ig-user-id}/media. The only documented bounds are the polling guidance and the 24-hour container lifetime.
findings.evidence: IG Container / Content Publishing snippets: 'Video uploads are asynchronous, so receiving a container ID does not guarantee that the upload was successful. To verify that a video has been uploaded, request the status_code field on the IG Container.' 'We recommend querying a container's status once per minute, for no more than 5 minutes.' 'Containers expire after 24 hours'. Status 'EXPIRED — The container was not published within 24 hours and has expired.' Status values: ERROR, EXPIRED, FINISHED, IN_PROGRESS, PUBLISHED. Limit: 400 containers per account per rolling 24 hours.

findings.claim: No official source says whether Meta fetches once or again later, for example a retry or a re-fetch at media_publish. Community evidence points to the fetch happening while the container is IN_PROGRESS. One unverified report says Meta retried several times.
findings.evidence: social-kit issue #6 (search summary): 'the only implicit bound is that video containers stay IN_PROGRESS while Meta downloads, so the URL must live until FINISHED'. Its follow-up, issue #23 ('Prototype: measure how Meta fetches media URLs'), was still open, 'since Meta's docs don't say how many requests it makes, from which IPs, or how long a URL must stay reachable.' bundle.social: 2207052 means 'Meta's fetcher could not download the file from the URL you gave it when you created the container.' A search summary cited one GitHub issue (xorbitsai/xagent #3507) in which Instagram rejected a container 'after all three attempts'. I could not open it. No source showed media_publish failing because the URL had been removed after FINISHED.

findings.claim: Expiring signed query-string URLs are not documented as rejected. Third-party guides treat them as usable while unexpired and name expiry as the failure mode. No source confirms that Supabase or R2 URLs specifically work.
findings.evidence: bundle.social: 'a signed URL that expires in 60 seconds, a URL behind authentication, or an origin that blocks datacenter IPs produces error 9004' (subcode 2207052). Ayrshare (localised page): causes include 'expired signed URLs (such as S3 presigned URLs)' and 'hotlink protection or referer checks on CDNs'. One search summary described a public PR that 'uploads an MP4 to private Supabase Storage and passes a temporary signed URL (1 hour)' to Meta. I could not re-verify it. Searches for R2 presigned URLs with Instagram returned nothing specific to R2.

findings.claim: Meta's documentation says nothing on redirects. Community reports say the URL should resolve directly to the raw file: no redirects, HTML wrappers or auth tokens. Redirecting share links such as Dropbox dl=1 work only some of the time.
findings.evidence: n8n community thread on the error 'Media download has failed. The media URI doesn't meet our requirements.': Meta 'now expects the URL to resolve straight to the media file, with no redirects, auth tokens, or HTML wrappers'. That is a forum claim; I found no Meta changelog behind it. Google Drive 'download' links 'are redirects, not direct image files'. Dropbox dl=1 'works now but may break in the future'. A Make user said a raw=1 Dropbox link 'opened fine in a browser but Instagram kept rejecting it'. Searches for a documented case of the fetcher failing on a 302 found none.

findings.claim: I found no evidence, official or community, on whether Meta's fetcher uses Range requests or needs a Content-Length header.
findings.evidence: Searches for Range, 206 and Content-Length together with video_url turned up nothing on fetcher behaviour. letmepost's preflight docs only recommend a plain 'curl -I' check for HTTP 200 (not a redirect) and the correct Content-Type, and never mention Content-Length or Range. On the storage side, R2 lists Range on GetObject, and its changelog says R2 'unconditionally return[s] HTTP 206 on ranged requests'. For Supabase, a 2021 discussion reported a missing Accept-Ranges header on createSignedUrl responses, later 'working fine again'. Neither shows what Meta requests.

findings.claim: The fetch uses the facebookexternalhit user agent. WAF bot rules can block it. Meta's Facebook Video API rejects hosted files that robots.txt restricts.
findings.evidence: Ayrshare: Meta 'fetch[es] the media from your URL using the facebookexternalhit user agent'. 'Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode, AWS WAF managed bot rule groups, and similar services may block Meta's crawler IP ranges even if robots.txt allows it.' Meta Web Crawlers page: FacebookExternalHit 'might bypass robots.txt when performing security or integrity checks'. Meta Video API (Pages) docs: 'files hosted on sites that restrict access via robots.txt are rejected' and fbcdn-hosted files 'will get rejected'. That last rule is documented for Facebook video, not Instagram.

findings.claim: Meta officially offers a way for Reels to skip public hosting: a resumable upload where the server POSTs the video bytes directly to rupload.facebook.com. It is documented only for Facebook Login for Business apps, which is Studio Assistant's planned primary (Unified Login) mode.
findings.evidence: Resumable uploads page / IG User Media snippets: the guide covers 'large video files, from local and publicly hosted content, to be published on Instagram. This is available only for apps that have implemented Facebook Login for Business.' Step 1 is POST /<IG_ID>/media with media_type=REELS&upload_type=resumable, which returns a container id and a rupload URI. Step 2 is 'POST https://rupload.facebook.com/ig-api-upload/<IG_MEDIA_CONTAINER_ID>' with an 'Authorization: OAuth <token>' header. For a local file you send 'offset' (generally 0) and 'file_size' (bytes) headers with --data-binary; for a hosted file you send a 'file_url' header instead. The host table lists graph.facebook.com with 'rupload.facebook.com (For resumable video uploads)' under Facebook Login, and graph.instagram.com only under Instagram Login. AdaptlyPost reads this as 'an app built on Business Login for Instagram cannot use resumable at all'. Success response: {"success":true,"message":"Upload successful."}. After upload you poll status_code until FINISHED, then call media_publish.

findings.claim: cover_url still requires Meta to fetch an image from a URL. thumb_offset needs no hosting.
findings.evidence: IG User Media snippets: cover_url is the image used as the cover for the Reels tab. 'If you specify both cover_url and thumb_offset, we use cover_url and ignores thumb_offset.' The Reels tab cover is supplied as a public URL to a JPEG. An out-of-range thumb_offset fails with error 2207057. One Postiz PR says cover_url is 'honoured on graph.instagram.com/v20.0 (tested)'. I found no source on whether cover_url can be combined with upload_type=resumable.

findings.claim: Signed-URL formats differ by provider. Any change to a SigV4 query string breaks the signature. R2 presigned URLs only work on the S3 API host.
findings.evidence: Supabase: signed URLs look like '{storageUrl}/object/sign/{bucketId}/{filePath}?token={token}' with an optional 'download' parameter. The download option makes Supabase send 'Content-Disposition: attachment' (search summary). R2, from the earlier full read in docs/research: presigned GET 'Timeout from 1 second to 7 days', S3 API domain only, not custom domains. Strapi issue: appending a parameter to an S3 presigned URL broke validation, because 'AWS uses the full URL to compute and validate the signature'.

implementation_decision:
Drop the untested "signed URL valid at least 2 hours" rule. Do not make the Instagram module depend on Meta fetching from our storage.

1. PRIMARY (Unified Login = Facebook Login for Business on graph.facebook.com, the mode already chosen in docs/research/decisions-summary.md): publish Reels by resumable binary upload, so the MP4 never gets a public URL.
   - Worker job `instagram.publish` runs in this order: content_publishing_limit pre-flight; POST /{ig-id}/media with media_type=REELS, upload_type=resumable, caption, share_to_feed, thumb_offset; store the container id; stream the rendered MP4 from the private R2 bucket (S3Store GetObject) into POST https://rupload.facebook.com/ig-api-upload/{vNN}/{container-id} with headers Authorization: OAuth <token>, offset: 0 and file_size: <bytes>, body = the file bytes.
   - The upload is one request from offset 0. On failure, resend the whole file to the same container (idempotent by container id), and create a new container if the old one is ERROR or EXPIRED.
   - Then poll status_code (15–30 s initial delay, once a minute for 5 min, then back off for up to 24 h) and call media_publish.
   - This satisfies CLAUDE.md: no object is exposed, the token stays server-side, the AbortSignal cancels the stream, and the job can resume from the stored container id.

2. COVER: default to thumb_offset (the frame the owner picked in the UI), which needs no hosting. Treat a custom cover_url as an optional feature behind a capability flag. Enable it only after a Development-mode spike shows it works with upload_type=resumable. When enabled, use the staging pattern in step 3 for the JPEG.

3. FALLBACK (legacy Instagram Login on graph.instagram.com, where resumable upload is not documented, or if rupload proves unreliable): pass video_url as a presigned GET on the R2 S3 API host (<account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com).
   - Do not use a custom domain: presigned URLs only work on the S3 host, and a Cloudflare zone could put Bot Fight Mode or WAF rules in front of a custom domain.
   - Rules:
     (a) Copy the render to a dedicated staging key `ig-staging/<uuid>.mp4` (unguessable; the source object stays untouched).
     (b) Presign for 24 h to match the container lifetime, since Meta documents no fetch window and the 7-day cap leaves room.
     (c) Send the URL exactly as presigned, never re-serialised. Put it in a form-encoded POST body so the &-separated X-Amz-* parameters arrive intact.
     (d) Give Meta the final object URL directly. Never route through a redirecting endpoint of our own, because redirects are undocumented and community reports say they fail.
     (e) Content-Type video/mp4 (image/jpeg for covers), no Content-Disposition: attachment.
     (f) Delete the staging object only after media_publish succeeds or the container reaches ERROR or EXPIRED, not at FINISHED: whether Meta re-fetches at publish is undocumented. Deleting the object is the effective revocation.
   - If the storage driver is ever Supabase, use its S3-protocol presigned GET, or createSignedUrl without the `download` option.
   - Map 2207052 and 2207003 to "re-stage with a fresh URL and a new container"; do not retry the same URL.

4. Before building the fallback, run a one-off integration spike against the owner's account in Development mode:
   - Publish a 10 s synthetic reel via (i) resumable binary upload, (ii) an R2 presigned video_url, and (iii) the same video_url served through a temporary logging proxy route.
   - The proxy route streams from R2, returns 200 with Content-Length and Accept-Ranges, and logs User-Agent, Range headers, request count and timestamps relative to the container POST.
   - Record the result in docs/research. That evidence decides whether the fallback needs the proxy, which would also need robots.txt to allow facebookexternalhit and no bot-blocking WAF.

5. UI and observability: show the upload mode in use (direct upload vs URL fetch), container status and Meta error text verbatim. Never show a reel as published until media_publish returns a media id and the permalink has been read back.
account_requirements: Instagram professional (Business or Creator) account for the shop, connected through the owner's Meta app.

Meta app set up with Facebook Login for Business (Unified Login) and a configuration granting at least instagram_basic and instagram_content_publish (plus business_management if /me/assigned_instagram_accounts comes back empty). Resumable direct upload is documented only for Facebook Login for Business apps. A legacy Instagram Login app would have to rely on the public-URL video_url route.

The app can stay in Development mode with Standard Access while it publishes only to the owner's own account through app role holders. App Review and Business Verification are needed only if the app is offered to other businesses.

Server-side outbound HTTPS from the worker to graph.facebook.com and rupload.facebook.com. In this research sandbox developers.facebook.com was blocked, so the production or worker network must allow these Meta hosts.

Cloudflare R2: one private bucket and an API token scoped to Object Read & Write on that bucket. For the fallback, use presigned URLs on the S3 API host only (not a custom domain) and keep any Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode or WAF bot rules away from whatever host Meta fetches from.
Only if the logging-proxy fallback is ever used: the web app must be publicly reachable over HTTPS, its robots.txt must allow facebookexternalhit, and no WAF rule may block Meta's crawler IP ranges.

Renders must meet the Reels spec (MP4 H.264/AAC, moov atom first via faststart, 3 s–15 min, ≤300 MB) and stay within the per-account publishing quota (read content_publishing_limit) and the 400 containers per rolling 24 h limit.
uncertainties: developers.facebook.com and supabase.com were blocked in this sandbox (DNS ENOTFOUND), so every Meta quote above comes from search-result snippets, not full pages. Snippet metadata suggested the pages are about 600 days old and mix v25.0 and v26.0. Whether anything changed in 2025–2026 could not be confirmed from Meta directly.
No official or verified community source says whether Meta's video_url or cover_url fetcher follows 3xx redirects. The 'no redirects' rule is a forum claim.
No source says whether the fetcher sends Range requests or requires Content-Length or Accept-Ranges. R2 and Supabase both support ranged GETs, but nobody has shown what Meta actually sends.

Fetch timing and count are undocumented: once at container creation, retried (one unverified report of 'three attempts'), or again at media_publish. A safe URL lifetime is therefore unknown. 24 h is a conservative choice based on the container lifetime, not a documented requirement.

No first-hand evidence was found that a Cloudflare R2 presigned URL or a Supabase createSignedUrl URL passes Meta's fetch. The one Supabase example (a 1-hour signed URL in a public PR) could not be re-verified.

Whether Meta's Instagram fetcher honours robots.txt on r2.cloudflarestorage.com or *.supabase.co is unknown. The robots.txt rejection rule is documented for Facebook Video API file_url uploads, not for Instagram.
Whether cover_url can be combined with upload_type=resumable is undocumented in what was found.

The resumable route's per-file limits are unclear: one Meta snippet says '100MB maximum' (possibly a video or Stories limit), while the Reels spec elsewhere says 300 MB. The size limit for resumable uploads needs confirming in the spike.

A Meta developer community thread reported intermittent problems with the resumable flow, including being unable to read the correct status after a failed upload. How reliable it is in late 2026 is unknown.
GitHub MCP access to the community repositories (eukosh/social-kit, gitroomhq/postiz-app) was refused for this session, so those issues and PRs were seen only through search summaries.

findings.claim: Yes, in principle. The Sound Collection licence is tied to where the content is distributed (Meta Company Products), not to which tool adds the audio. Content you 'create, upload, and distribute' on Instagram or Facebook is covered, and nothing in the wording seen limits the licence to Meta's in-app creation tools.
findings.evidence: Sound Collection Terms (search summary, consistent across queries): 'Meta hereby grants you a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use the SC Audio Content for commercial or non-commercial purposes in content you create, upload, and distribute on the Meta Company Products (including through links to the Meta Company Products embedded in third party sites) only.' The word 'upload' covers externally produced files. I found no clause restricting use to in-app editors.

findings.claim: Meta's own help pages describe Sound Collection as a library you download and mix in your own editing software. This is the opposite of an 'in-app only' licence.
findings.evidence: Creator Studio / Business help (summary): you search, filter and 'download' each file; 'Sound collection is only accessible from your computer'; you need 'your own video editing software' / 'your own video creation software to add the music and sounds to your videos, since you cannot add music or sounds to posts with sound collection.' Instagram help: Sound Collection is 'an audio library of sound effects and royalty free music that you can download for your videos.' Meta Sound Collection page: 'Free to use in any videos you create and share on Facebook and Instagram.'

findings.claim: The binding restriction is that the audio cannot be used apart from Meta products. A rendered MP4 containing Sound Collection audio is licensed only while its destination is Instagram/Facebook, or an embed of the Meta post. The same file posted to TikTok or YouTube, offered as a website video, or shared as a general download falls outside the licence.
findings.evidence: Terms: 'You may not perform, distribute, make available or otherwise use the SC Audio Content separately from the Meta Company Products.' 'Meta reserves all rights and remedies for use of any SC Audio Content by you outside of the uses permitted above without Meta's express prior written consent.' The grant's parenthetical allows 'links to the Meta Company Products embedded in third party sites', so an Instagram embed on the shop website is allowed but the raw MP4 is not.

findings.claim: The licence runs to the person or entity that accepts the terms, and Meta can audit compliance and change the terms. The owner's own Meta login must download the tracks and accept the terms. Studio Assistant cannot source Sound Collection files itself.
findings.evidence: Terms (summary): entered into by 'Meta Platforms, Inc. and Meta Platforms Ireland Limited and the person or entity accepting them'; 'deemed accepted on the date you click "accept"'; 'Meta reserves the right to monitor or audit your compliance with these Terms and to update these terms from time to time.' These terms control Sound Collection use where they conflict with Meta's broader Terms.

findings.claim: Meta's Music Guidelines treat Sound Collection as already cleared, unlike other music, for commercial use on Meta.
findings.evidence: Music Guidelines: 'Use of music for commercial or non-personal purposes in particular is prohibited unless you have obtained appropriate licenses.' 'If you want to utilize music not in the public domain or in Sound Collection, you should secure the appropriate licenses directly from the applicable rights holders for the applicable territories.' Earlier research (same repo) found that boosted Reels 'can't use licensed music' and Instagram recommends 'royalty-free music, like what's available in our Sound Collection, or original audio'.

findings.claim: The Graph API itself does not separate audio mixed in-app from audio mixed in a file. Content publishing uploads one finished video, and the Reels container only lets you name the original audio. Copyright detection is a separate fingerprint check that runs on every API-created video. Neither treats Sound Collection audio specially in any wording found.
findings.evidence: IG User Media reference: 'audio_name' is 'For Reels only. Name of the audio of your Reels media', renamable once; 'music tagging is only available for original audio.' Copyright Detection: 'Early copyright detection is supported only for Instagram media created via the content publishing API'; container field copyright_check_status returns status (completed | error | in_progress | not_started) and matches_found (true = 'the video is violating copyright'); published media copyright_check_information lists matches with actions 'BLOCK' or 'MUTE' per geo; 'The media_url field is omitted from responses if the media contains copyrighted material.' Documented under Instagram API with Facebook Login.

findings.claim: I found no official Meta statement on whether Sound Collection tracks are exempt from Rights Manager matching or from copyright_check_status. Secondary sources say Meta's help page promises Sound Collection videos 'will not be demonetised or muted'. They also say matches can still happen, for example when a third party registers the same recording or when rights change. So a match is unlikely but not ruled out, and must be handled.
findings.evidence: Secondary quotes attributed to business/help/880459498798521: 'nearly 16,000 songs and sounds' and videos 'will not be demonetised or muted' for copyright (not confirmed on Meta's page; its indexed text was only a short summary). Third-party guides: 'rights systems can still flag audio through matching'; 'even royalty-free music can create matches when distributors register it'. Meta Music Guidelines: content 'may be reviewed by the rights owner and blocked, muted or removed if use of the music is not properly authorized.' No official page found that describes a Sound Collection allowlist in Rights Manager.

findings.claim: 2026 change: Meta added an Instagram Audio API for Facebook-Login apps that attaches Sound Collection or original audio to a Reel at creation time, so Meta mixes the audio instead of the app. This is an alternative to baking the track into the MP4, but I could not verify its exact container parameter.
findings.evidence: Changelog (summary): 'Introducing the Instagram Audio API for apps using Facebook Login. The API lets your app search for and retrieve audio — original sounds from Reels and royalty-free music from Meta's Sound Collection — and attach it to Reels at creation time.' Endpoints GET /ig_audio?audio_type={music|original_sound}, GET /{ig_audio_id}; new field media_audio_type (MUSIC | ORIGINAL_SOUND). Third-party wrappers pass it as audio_configuration{audio_id, volume, loop} on REELS containers. They say it is not available with Instagram Login. Date: June 1 2026 (Releasebot/GitHub) vs Jun 22 2026 (one summary of the official changelog).

findings.claim: The repo's current contract cannot represent a Meta-only licence. MusicLicenceSchema.kind has no Sound Collection value, and permitted has instagram but no facebook or Meta-only lock. The renderer's track picker cannot yet apply the rule above.
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/music.ts: kind enum ['owner_upload','catalogue','commercial_licence','cc0','cc_by','public_domain','unknown']; permitted { promotionalUse, instagram, tiktok, youtube, website }; PUBLISH_PLATFORMS = ['instagram','tiktok','youtube','website']; checkMusicForPlatforms blocks only by per-platform booleans.

implementation_decision:
The two research docs need one combined answer: Sound Collection tracks MAY be rendered into an MP4 with FFmpeg, but only when the MP4 can go nowhere except Meta (Instagram/Facebook via the Graph API, or the owner uploading it in the Meta apps). That rule should replace the decisions-summary.md line 'never bake it into exported files' with 'never bake it into files bound for, or downloadable to, non-Meta destinations'. The Instagram decision ('Sound Collection downloads may be mixed into API-bound Reels') stands, with the guards below.

1. Contract (packages/core/src/music.ts, Zod):
   - Add kind 'meta_sound_collection'.
   - Add a 'facebook' platform.
   - Add a licence-level field `destinationLock: 'meta_only' | null`.
   - For kind 'meta_sound_collection', a refinement forces permitted = { promotionalUse: true, instagram: true, facebook: true, tiktok: false, youtube: false, website: false } and destinationLock = 'meta_only'.
   - Licence passport fields: Sound Collection track title, artist, asset URL/ID, downloaded_at, the downloading Meta account (must be the owner/business), terms_accepted_at, and a screenshot of the terms page as proof. Attribution is not required.
   - The track is owner-uploaded only. Studio Assistant never scrapes or fetches Sound Collection itself.
2. Renderer and track picker:
   - A render whose soundtrack has destinationLock 'meta_only' carries `renderLock: 'meta_only'`.
   - checkMusicForPlatforms blocks TikTok, YouTube and website targets with the reason 'Meta Sound Collection music is licensed for Instagram and Facebook only'.
   - The picker greys these tracks out for any job that targets a non-Meta platform. For multi-platform jobs it offers a second render with a different licensed track or original audio. A cross-post therefore always gets its own render and never reuses a Meta-locked MP4.
   - Downloads of meta_only renders are labelled 'For Instagram/Facebook upload only'.
   - meta_only renders never feed the website module. On the website, show the Instagram embed instead, which the licence permits.
3. Publishing (Instagram worker job):
   - Upload meta_only renders through the resumable upload path where available. Otherwise use a short-lived signed video_url, never a lasting public link.
   - After the container reaches FINISHED, poll copyright_check_status until status = completed. This needs Facebook Login (Unified login), which is already the primary auth mode.
   - If matches_found = true, do NOT publish, even for a Sound Collection track. Set the job to needs_attention, show the owner the matched segment and rights owner, and offer 'swap track' or 'use original audio'.
   - After publishing, read copyright_check_information once and store it. A later MUTE or BLOCK shows as an honest status, never hidden.
   - If the account is on the Instagram Login fallback, copyright detection is unavailable. Show a warning before publishing Sound Collection reels and offer the owner manual in-app upload instead.
4. Instagram Audio API (attach a Sound Collection ig_audio id at creation): do not build it yet. Meta's own parameter reference has not been read, and wrappers disagree on field names. Re-check developers.facebook.com once the host is allowed, then add it as an optional adapter that avoids baking the track in.
account_requirements: The owner (not a staff member or Studio Assistant) logs in to Meta Sound Collection with the Facebook account tied to the business, on a computer (Sound Collection is 'only accessible from your computer'), accepts the Sound Collection Terms, and downloads each track. The licence runs to 'the person or entity accepting them'.

The owner keeps proof for the licence passport: the track's asset link or ID, the download date, and a screenshot or date of terms acceptance. Meta 'reserves the right to monitor or audit your compliance' and may update the terms.
The owner agrees, recorded in the app, that Sound Collection renders are posted only to Instagram/Facebook, or embedded from there, and never cross-posted to TikTok, YouTube or the website as a file.

The Instagram professional (Business/Creator) account is connected through Facebook Login for Business (Unified login) with a linked Facebook Page. Copyright detection (copyright_check_status / copyright_check_information) and the 2026 Audio API are documented for Facebook Login only.

Permissions in the Facebook Login for Business configuration include instagram_content_publish and pages_read_engagement, which the docs list for reading copyright_check_status on containers, plus the account-discovery permissions already decided.

No extra App Review is needed while the Meta app stays in Development mode with only the owner and app admins connecting (per the existing Instagram decision). Advanced Access/App Review is needed only if the app is ever opened to other businesses.

If Reels with Sound Collection music are later boosted or used as ads, Meta's guidance steers to Sound Collection or original audio, never licensed-library music. The owner must use the Meta-native boost/Ads Manager flow under Meta's Commercial Terms.
uncertainties: I could not read the full Sound Collection Terms page (www.facebook.com blocked in this sandbox; it has to be allowed in the session's network settings to re-check). The grant and 'separately' clauses are search-summary quotes, consistent across several queries. The 'last updated March 2022' date is a third-party claim, and I could not confirm whether the terms changed in 2025-2026.

No wording found explicitly addresses whether audio added outside Meta's tools, then uploaded via the Graph API, is covered. The conclusion that it is covered rests on the grant ('content you create, upload, and distribute on the Meta Company Products'), Meta's help pages telling users to download and use their own editing software, and the absence of any in-app-only restriction. Instagram is a Meta Company Product, but I did not read the Facebook Terms definition of 'Meta Company Products'.

Whether Sound Collection recordings are allowlisted in, or excluded from, Rights Manager / copyright_check_status matching is not documented in any official source I could reach. The 'will not be demonetised or muted' promise is attributed to business/help/880459498798521 only by secondary sites. Third-party reports of false matches on royalty-free music are anecdotal.

developers.facebook.com was blocked, so the Copyright Detection page, the IG Container reference and the Instagram Audio API reference were seen only through search summaries. The Audio API's exact creation-time parameter (wrappers say audio_configuration{audio_id}) and its date (June 1 vs June 22 2026) are unverified, as is whether it needs extra permissions.
Whether Sound Collection availability, or the copyright-detection behaviour, differs for an Australian business account is not documented in the sources found.

Hosting the meta_only MP4 at a short-lived signed URL for Meta to fetch is, in my reading, part of uploading to Meta and not 'making available separately'. No Meta source addresses this intermediate-hosting case directly.

findings.claim: The premise that createPost is marked experimental is not supported by Buffer's API reference. The labels it does use are on other operations.
findings.evidence: A search of the reference says createPost "takes a CreatePostInput! and returns PostActionPayload!, and creates a post for a channel", with no status tag shown. The "⚠️ Experimental" label appears on movePostInQueue, removePostFromContentItem and deleteSnippet, and "🧪 Preview" on createPostTemplate and deletePostTemplate. One third party calls the whole API a 'public beta', and another says it has been public since 27 May 2026.

findings.claim: Buffer's GraphQL API works on the Free plan with a personal API key. Only the organisation owner can create keys, and calls must come from the server.
findings.evidence: Buffer API page: "Buffer's API is publicly available to every Buffer customer" and "API keys are personal and tied to your user account, not your organization. Currently, only the organization owner can create API keys". Requests "should be made from your server" and use a Bearer header. Help Center: "Free: 1 API key and 1 app client. Essentials gets 3 and Team gets 5." Keys are created at publish.buffer.com/settings/api under Personal Access, '+ New Key'.

findings.claim: Free-plan API rate limits are small but enough for one shop. Published figures conflict.
findings.evidence: Developer docs and pricing page: 150 requests per 15 minutes, 600 per 24 hours, and a 30-day limit of 1,000 per channel capped at 3,000. All keys share one set of limits, and exceeding any of them returns 429. An older Help Center article gives a flat 3,000 per 30 days, and a troubleshooting page gives 100 per 15 minutes and 250 per 24 hours.

findings.claim: createPost can target a TikTok channel with a video asset and schedulingType automatic. Automatic is the normal mode for TikTok, and notification is an opt-in reminder.
findings.evidence: Video example: creating a video post "works in the same way as creating a text post, with the addition of a video entry in the assets array". The sample mutation uses schedulingType: automatic, mode: addToQueue and metadata.thumbnailOffset. MCP guide: automatic means "Buffer's publishing workers send the post, with nobody having to act", and notification "is required for Facebook Groups and Instagram personal profiles, and is also available on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube when you ask for a reminder". It also says TikTok needs "an image or a video". Modes are addToQueue, customScheduled with dueAt, shareNow and shareNext.

findings.claim: Buffer's TikTok-specific input fields are minimal. There is no privacy-level, branded-content or music field.
findings.evidence: TikTokPostMetadataInput has optional isAiGenerated ("TikTok video only") and a title for photo posts. The video privacy field is documented for YouTube only. A roadmap feature request notes TikTok disclosure settings are not exposed. TikTok video captions are limited to 2,200 characters, and a custom thumbnail image is not accepted (frame offset only).

findings.claim: A full video-to-TikTok auto-publish through Buffer's API is not proven. Buffer's own roadmap names a TikTok domain-verification blocker for URL-hosted video, and Buffer has no upload endpoint.
findings.evidence: Roadmap (about May 2026): the API "only supports URL-based video transfer (PULL_FROM_URL) for TikTok posts". That "requires the hosting domain to be verified in TikTok's Developer Dashboard, which creates friction for users hosting videos on third-party services". Binary FILE_UPLOAD "would eliminate the domain verification dependency entirely" but is still listed as being explored. Hosting guide: no upload endpoint. The URL must be public, direct, HTTPS and stable until the post publishes, and signed or expiring URLs "often work when createPost is called but expire before the post publishes". TikTok's docs say unverified PULL_FROM_URL returns 403 url_ownership_unverified. A third-party skill page says domain verification is not checked at createPost time, so failures appear only at publish. No official TikTok video example and no verified end-to-end report were found, and two third-party GitHub PRs are untested.

findings.claim: Buffer exposes post status by polling, not webhooks. Statuses map cleanly onto queued, processing, published and failed.
findings.evidence: The PostStatus enum has draft, error, needs_approval, scheduled, sending and sent. Sent posts return sentAt and externalLink. A post in error carries a PostPublishingError with a display message and an optional help link. No webhook documentation was found. A daily-limit query (DailyPostingLimitStatus: isAtLimit, limit, scheduled, sent) exists.

findings.claim: Buffer's TikTok product rules: TikTok works only on Buffer's new (non-legacy) plans, the Free plan includes automatic publishing, and media and posting limits apply.
findings.evidence: Help Center: "scheduling and publishing to TikTok are only available on our new plans". The pricing-and-features page lists Automatic publishing on Free. A Buffer guide says the free plan lets you connect "up to three social media channels — TikTok included — and schedule posts with automatic publishing". Video must be 3 s to 10 min, 1 GB or less, MOV/MP4/WEBM at about 23-60 fps. Music, polls, stickers and filters force notification publishing. TikTok is capped at "25 posts per 24 hours". An older Buffer article says a TikTok business account is needed, but the newer buffer.com/tiktok page says one is not required.

findings.claim: Buffer plan and cost (USD, per channel): the Free plan is enough for the API plus TikTok automatic publishing but caps each channel at 10 scheduled posts. Essentials costs about US$5-6 per channel per month.
findings.evidence: Third-party 2026 snapshots: Free $0 for up to 3 channels with 10 scheduled posts per channel (stated as of October 2026). Essentials $6 per channel per month billed monthly, or $5 billed annually ($60 a year). Team $12 or $10. Other sources describe a flat 20% annual discount instead. "There is no separate Buffer API pricing" on any plan. Buffer's own comparison articles say "Essentials starts at $6 per channel per month, Team at $12". The official pricing page appeared in results, but its figures were not quoted.

findings.claim: Buffer's legacy REST API shuts down on 1 February 2027, so any Buffer integration must use the GraphQL API.
findings.evidence: Buffer API page and a third-party PR: "That REST API also shuts down on 1 Feb 2027". New-style keys are rejected by the old REST endpoint with 401.

findings.claim: Zernio documents the full TikTok video direct-post flow, including provider-hosted media upload and explicit consent flags.
findings.evidence: Zernio docs: send POST /v1/posts with platform "tiktok", a mediaItems entry of type 'video', and tiktokSettings with content_preview_confirmed: true and express_consent_given: true, which are "required". The example uses privacy_level 'PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE' and publishNow: true, and draft: true sends the video to the creator's TikTok inbox. Media flow: presign, PUT the file to the upload URL (expires after an hour), then reference the returned public URL. Uploads stay in temporary storage for 7 days, and creating a post copies them to permanent storage. Video limits: MP4/MOV/WebM, 4 GB, 3 s to 10 min, 2,200-character caption.

findings.claim: Zernio's TikTok lane changed in September 2026. New connections use TikTok's Business API, publish videos as public only, and have a per-account cap.
findings.evidence: 11 September 2026 update: new TikTok connections now go through TikTok's Business API. Accounts connected before 10 September that hit quota errors can be reconnected. Docs: Business app accounts "publish videos as public only, and Creator Inbox drafts are the only route to a non-public video", and a non-public direct post "gets rejected". The cap is "15 videos and 15 photo posts per account per rolling 24 hours", and posts over the cap are held rather than failed. The user must approve every requested permission, since a partial grant is refused. Licensed music and location tags (17 September 2026 update) also require the Business API lane.

findings.claim: Zernio pushes publish status by webhook, and per-platform events map onto Studio Assistant's provider states.
findings.evidence: Webhook events: post.platform.published, post.platform.failed, post.published, post.partial, post.failed and post.tiktok.url_resolved. TikTok exposes the video id "some minutes after publishing", so platformPostUrl can be empty at first. Failed or partial posts can be retried with POST /v1/posts/{postId}/retry. Endpoints must return 2xx within 5 seconds, and delivery logs are queryable.

findings.claim: Zernio's 'first two connected accounts free' pricing still appears on its official pricing page and docs. Some meters bill from the first unit.
findings.evidence: zernio.com/pricing: "First 2 accounts free, no credit card required". After that, accounts 3-10 cost $6 a month each, 11-100 cost $3 and 101+ cost $1. docs.zernio.com/pricing: "Accounts are counted across your whole team (owner plus invited members), and the first 2 are free". The free allowance works as a $12 monthly credit. X API pass-through, provisioned phone numbers, outbound messages past 10,000, managed ads past 500 and WhatsApp fees "bill from the first unit, even with 2 or fewer accounts". The rate limit is 60 requests per minute for 0-2 accounts. No last-updated date was visible.

implementation_decision:
The answer is no for Buffer as things stand. None of the evidence shows Buffer's createPost carrying a video to a TikTok Business account end to end. createPost itself is not labelled experimental, it works on the Free plan with the owner's personal key, and schedulingType automatic is the default for TikTok. The problem is that Buffer has no upload endpoint and, per its own roadmap, TikTok video goes only by PULL_FROM_URL. TikTok then requires the hosting domain to be verified, and the owner cannot verify Studio Assistant's storage domain in Buffer's TikTok app. Buffer would also need a stable, public, non-expiring media URL, which conflicts with the private-media rule. Zernio does document the full flow: presigned upload to Zernio storage, POST /v1/posts with the tiktokSettings consent flags, publishNow or a scheduled time, and published/failed webhooks. Its first two connected accounts are still free.

Concrete decision:
(1) Keep draft/export as the only shipped TikTok path for Stages A and B.
(2) Build Stage C as one provider adapter behind a feature flag, with Zernio as the primary and only enabled provider. The worker job uploads the rendered MP4 through Zernio's presign flow, so the bytes go server to server and no public URL of ours is exposed. It then calls POST /v1/posts with platform tiktok, privacy_level PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE (the only value the Business lane accepts) and the two consent flags. The flags are set only after the owner has seen the in-app preview and ticked an explicit consent box. The job is idempotent: it stores the Zernio postId and never re-posts.
(3) Keep the provider states queued, processing, published and failed. Zernio's webhooks and post statuses back each one: a scheduled or held post is queued, the window between publishing and post.tiktok.url_resolved is processing, post.platform.published is published, and post.platform.failed or partial is failed with Zernio's error message and a retry action. They are set only from real webhook or poll data. Until the owner connects Zernio and a live smoke test (one short 9:16 MP4) reaches published, the module shows 'needs setup' or 'unverified'.
(4) Buffer stays a documented fallback only. Implement it only if a live test shows a Studio Assistant-hosted video publishing to TikTok, or once Buffer ships TikTok FILE_UPLOAD. Its mapping would be scheduled to queued, sending to processing, sent to published and error to failed, by polling because there are no webhooks. Use mode shareNow so the media URL lives only briefly.
(5) Never attach Commercial Sounds through either provider. Music stays an in-app step for the owner, which Buffer forces into notification mode anyway.
account_requirements: Zernio (primary): the business creates its own Zernio account. The first 2 connected accounts are free with no credit card, counted across the whole team including invited staff, so connect only TikTok (and at most one other network) to stay at US$0. A third account costs US$6 a month. Do not connect X unless a card is on file, because X pass-through bills from the first call.
Zernio API key: stored server-side only and encrypted at rest. Free-tier rate limit is 60 requests per minute.

Connect the TikTok account through Zernio's TikTok Business API flow (any connection made after 10 September 2026) and approve every requested permission, since a partial grant is refused. Videos direct-post as public only. Limits are 15 videos and 15 photo posts per account per rolling 24 hours, 3 s to 10 min, 4 GB or less, MP4/MOV/WebM, and a 2,200-character caption.

Studio Assistant must show the owner the final video preview and TikTok creator info, then capture explicit consent before setting content_preview_confirmed and express_consent_given. It should also set the AI-generated disclosure where applicable.
TikTok: use a TikTok Business Account owned by the shop. Commercial Sounds and music must be added in the TikTok app, not through the API.

Buffer (fallback only): a Buffer account on a current, non-legacy plan where the business owner is the organisation owner, because only the owner can create the personal API key at publish.buffer.com/settings/api.

Buffer Free plan: US$0, up to 3 channels, 10 scheduled posts per channel, 1 API key, about 150 requests per 15 min, 600 per 24 h and 1,000 per channel per 30 days. Essentials (about US$6 per channel per month, or US$5 billed annually) removes the 10-post queue cap. Prices are in USD from third-party snapshots; check AUD billing and GST on buffer.com/pricing.

Buffer TikTok limits: 25 posts per 24 h, video 3 s to 10 min, 1 GB or less, MOV/MP4/WEBM at 23-60 fps, 2,200-character caption. Music and polls force notification mode. Video must be at a stable public HTTPS URL that TikTok accepts, which may need domain verification Buffer handles, not the owner. Buffer's legacy REST API ends on 1 February 2027.

Network access: allow developers.buffer.com, api.buffer.com, zernio.com, docs.zernio.com and the Zernio API host in the session or deployment network settings, both to re-verify these docs directly and for the worker to call the providers.
uncertainties: Every source came from web-search summaries, not full pages. WebFetch to developers.buffer.com and zernio.com failed with DNS ENOTFOUND, so both hosts have to be allowed in the session's network settings before the pages can be read directly. All quoted wording should be re-checked on the live pages.

No official or verified report was found of a Buffer createPost video publishing automatically to TikTok. It is unknown whether Buffer re-hosts media on its own TikTok-verified domain, which would remove the url_ownership_unverified risk, or passes our URL straight to TikTok's PULL_FROM_URL. The roadmap entry naming the problem is about 188 days old and may be stale.
Whether createPost has ever carried an 'experimental' label is unconfirmed. The current indexed reference shows no label on it, but this comes from search snippets.

Buffer pricing differs between sources: monthly versus annual US$5 or US$6 for Essentials, US$10 or US$12 for Team, or a 20% annual discount. The official pricing page's figures were not quoted. AUD pricing and GST treatment are unknown.
Buffer's API rate-limit figures conflict between the developer docs, the pricing page and Help Center articles.

A third-party guide says a channel with 'require approval' turns API posts into drafts, and another says TikTok auto-publish needs Essentials. Both conflict with or go beyond Buffer's own statements and are unverified.
Whether a TikTok Business Account is required for Buffer automatic publishing is unclear: an older Buffer article says yes, the newer buffer.com/tiktok page says no.

Zernio's docs do not explicitly say its TikTok app is audited, or that presigned public URLs are on a TikTok-verified domain. That they work is inferred from the docs describing public-only Business-lane direct posts and the presign-to-mediaItems flow. A live smoke test is needed.

Zernio's pricing pages showed no last-updated date, so the free tier could not be confirmed as of 9-14 November 2026 beyond appearing on the current official pages in search. One Zernio blog gives an older 25 videos per day cap that conflicts with the docs' 15 per rolling 24 h.
Whether Zernio's Business-lane connection supports TikTok personal or creator accounts, and the exact Zernio API base host, were not confirmed.

topic: spotify_dev_mode_status_2026: Is Development Mode Client ID creation open to a new Spotify for Developers account as of November 2026 (no pause)? Have the Developer Terms (v10, 15 May 2025) or Developer Policy been revised since, e.g. alongside the 6 Feb 2026 post that Spotify's index re-dates to 18 Jun 2026? Does any current revision address internal business tools, or commercial use of Embeds and the Play Button?

sources.date_note: Says 'Posted February 6, 2026', with an added 'March 9' update section. developer.spotify.com/community lists it as 'Blog post June 18, 2026'. Direct fetch blocked (ENOTFOUND).
Index page that shows the 6 Feb post under 18 Jun 2026. It also lists the 18 Jun 2026 refresh-token post and a 13 Aug 2026 'Introducing Spotify Soloist' post.

Third-party note. Probes ran 2026-09-04/05 and it cites Terms 'Version 10, effective as of 15 May, 2025'. Only the first 100k of 154k characters were read.
Opened 19 Jul 2026, comments 31 Jul and 15/16 Oct 2026, closed 15 Oct 2026. Third-party.
Opened 7 Nov 2026 ('Date checked: 2026-11-07'), still open. Third-party. Repeats the Feb rules but not the July raise to 25.
8 to 19 Sep 2026. Mentions 'Developer Terms V.11' and 'V.12'. Ambiguous: these are probably clause numbers, not versions.

About Apr 2026. A 'reached your limit' message explained by the one-Client-ID rule then in force.
Jan 2026. Says the portal had been disabled for new apps 'since late-December'.
Recent (2026) developer question about commercial approval for a venue. No official Spotify answer surfaced.
About Spotify's consumer Terms of Use (dispute resolution and arbitration), effective 15 Oct 2026. It does not concern the Developer Terms.

findings.claim: Creating a new app was paused from about late December 2025 until 11 February 2026. Spotify ended the pause by reopening Development Mode under stricter permanent rules.
findings.evidence: Spotify Community and Home Assistant threads quote the Dashboard tooltip on the greyed-out Create App button: 'New integrations are currently on hold while we make updates to improve reliability and performance'. A moderator said the same, and support reportedly said 'no ETA'. Home Assistant (Jan 2026): the portal had been 'disabled for creation of new Apps since late-December'. Spotify's 6 Feb 2026 post, per search summary: all newly created Development Mode Client IDs are created under the updated rules starting 11 February.

findings.claim: As of November 2026 a new account can create a Development Mode Client ID, subject to the 2026 rules. No later pause was found, but no official page or Dashboard was viewed directly.
findings.evidence: Official July 2026 changelog and 23 Jul 2026 blog, per search summary: 'Client ID limit increased from 1 to 25 per developer account'. Quota is now 'counted per developer account', and a 429 response carries 'reason': 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED'. Quota-modes doc, as quoted by a third-party note read 2026-10-25: 'Newly-created apps begin in development mode.' Third-party flutster issue #1, Oct 2026 comment: 'Rechecked 2026-10-16: app creation is open (25 apps per account, owner needs Premium, 5 users per app)'. The issue was closed as completed. Flutster issue #2 (7 Nov 2026) says the freeze 'appears to have been lifted, replaced by a new permanent policy'. That issue still cites the old one-Client-ID limit, so it predates or misses the July raise. No Aug to Nov 2026 Spotify post or changelog about a new hold appeared. The only 2026 'limit reached' reports (about Apr 2026) are explained by the then one-Client-ID rule.

findings.claim: Conditions on a new Client ID as of November 2026: the owner needs Spotify Premium, each Client ID allows up to 5 authorised users, each account can hold up to 25 Client IDs sharing one pooled quota, and the endpoint set is reduced.
findings.evidence: 6 Feb 2026 post: 'Development Mode use will require a Spotify Premium account'. Each Client ID is 'limited to up to five authorized users'. 'API access will be limited to a smaller set of supported endpoints.' The March 9 update section: 'Postponed endpoint access changes for existing integrations', while the Premium requirement, user cap and Client ID limit 'take effect as planned'. The July 2026 changelog raised the Client ID limit to 25. Quota-modes doc as quoted 2026-10-25: 'The app owner must have a Spotify Premium account for apps in development mode to function.'

findings.claim: No revision of the Developer Terms or Developer Policy after 15 May 2025 was found. Third parties who read the pages in Sep and Oct 2026 still saw v10 and the 15 May 2025 dates. This is partly better than the 543-day-old index copies.
findings.evidence: Search snippets of developer.spotify.com/terms: 'Version 10, effective as of 15 May, 2025'. Policy: 'Effective as of 15 May, 2025'. Searches for a 'Version 11' found nothing official. Third-party spot-mixer note ('I read all Spotify pages on 2026-10-25') quotes the Terms as 'Version 10, effective as of 15 May, 2025', and says the Policy shows 'Effective as of 15 May, 2025' with no version number. Third-party vaTheo note (probes 2026-09-04/05) cites 'Version 10, effective as of 15 May, 2025'. Neither the 6 Feb 2026 post nor its March 9 update says a new Terms version came with the changes. The Terms say Spotify 'may revise these Developer Terms from time to time and the most current version will always be posted on our website.'

findings.claim: The one apparent 'V.11 / V.12' reference is not evidence of a new Terms version.
findings.evidence: Analytify issue #97 (Sep 2026): 'do not implement Spotify Developer Terms V.11 user-license requirements' and 'correct the current V.12 warranty reference'. It quotes no Terms text and never mentions 'Version 10' or 'effective'. It reads like Section V clause numbers (end-user licence and warranty-disclaimer clauses). Two independent notes from Sep and Oct 2026 still report Version 10. Spotify's 15 Oct 2026 terms update concerns the consumer Terms of Use (dispute resolution and arbitration), not the Developer Terms.

findings.claim: Why the 6 Feb 2026 post shows up as 18 Jun 2026 is still unresolved. The only content change found is the March 9 addendum, and no June edit was found.
findings.evidence: developer.spotify.com/community lists 'Blog post June 18, 2026 | Spotify Update on Developer Access and Platform Security', while the post itself says 'Posted February 6, 2026'. A search for June 2026 changes to it found none, and the most recent change found is the 'March 9: Postponed endpoint access changes for existing integrations' section. One community user said the post 'had been edited to include the actual reason'. That is unverified. 18 Jun 2026 is also the date of the official refresh-token-expiration post, which could explain a co-listing or edit. The previously unexplained '13 Aug 2026' index entry matches a separate official post, 'Introducing Spotify Soloist' (2026-08-13), not a re-dated quota post.

findings.claim: No current Spotify document addresses internal business tools. The official 2026 framing of Development Mode excludes business use rather than allowing it.
findings.evidence: 6 Feb 2026 post: Development Mode 'will be reduced in scope while continuing to support learning, experimentation, and personal projects for non-commercial use by individual developers'. It is 'intentionally limited' and 'should not be relied on as a foundation for building or scaling a business on Spotify.' Policy (as quoted 2026-10-25): 'Except for the limited commercial uses for Non-Streaming SDAs (set out below) commercial uses are not permitted for SDAs.' The permitted exceptions are selling advertising, sponsorships or promotions within the app, and selling the app or access to it. Both the third-party note and a search summary say Terms III.1(a) licenses the platform to develop SDAs '(i) for private personal use'. That wording is not verified against the live page. No published process exists for commercial approval of a Development Mode app. A 2026 community thread asking for commercial approval for a venue drew no official answer in the results, and the Web Playback SDK still requires 'prior written approval' for commercial projects. Extended Quota is 'organizations (not individuals)' only, and per the quota-modes page requires about 250k MAU.

findings.claim: The Widget/Embed terms have not been revised since 2014 as far as can be seen. The 'Play Button may not be used for commercial purposes' clause is undefined and still the latest wording found. Separately, Spotify says using Embeds means accepting the Developer Terms.
findings.evidence: developer.spotify.com/documentation/embeds/terms is indexed as 'Version 2.0. Effective as of 27 May 2014'. Its clause, as quoted in community posts: 'Please note that the Spotify Play Button may not be used for commercial purposes. This restriction does not prohibit you from embedding the Spotify Play Button on Websites that contain advertising.' The licence covers display 'on any website or webpage controlled by you'. 'You must have an end user agreement and privacy policy.' Spotify 'may request ... proof that your website ... is properly licensed'. A search summary (not exact text) also says Widgets may not be used to promote a product, service or website. A community user asking 'What is the definition of "commercial purposes"?' got no official definition. Embeds documentation: 'By using Spotify Embeds, you accept the Spotify Developer Terms of Service.' Developer Terms v10: 'if you use any of the Spotify Widget ... you will be bound by the separate Spotify Widget Terms.' Policy: 'If you use Spotify Widgets, you must also comply with the restrictions set out in the Spotify Widgets Terms.' No 2025-2026 change to the Embed or Widget terms was found.

findings.claim: No Web API rule change after July 2026 was found.
findings.evidence: Searches found Web API changelogs for Feb, Mar, May and Jul 2026 only. The Sep and Oct 2026 release notes that surfaced belong to the separate Ads API. Developer blog posts after July: 13 Aug 2026 'Introducing Spotify Soloist' (Spotify Connect CLI) with an Oct 2026 platform update. Nothing changes Development Mode access.

implementation_decision:
Tier 1 (Web API search) fails the test 'worth building only if a Client ID can be created AND business use is not excluded'. Client ID creation is open: Premium owner, up to 25 Client IDs per account, 5 users each, pooled quota, no pause since 11 Feb 2026. But the only current official wording on purpose limits Development Mode to 'personal projects for non-commercial use by individual developers'. It says Development Mode 'should not be relied on as a foundation for building or scaling a business', and the Policy says commercial uses 'are not permitted' beyond the narrow Non-Streaming exceptions. No 2025-2026 revision carves out internal business tools, and no approval route exists. So Studio Assistant should NOT build Tier 1 in Stage A, B or C. Remove it from the roadmap, or record it as 'blocked by Spotify policy: needs written permission from Spotify'. Do not write a Client ID, OAuth or Spotify search adapter. If the owner ever gets written permission from Spotify, revisit then and re-verify the live Terms and Policy first. Tier 0 still ships, made more conservative:
(1) Store only the Spotify URL/URI the owner pastes plus the owner's own notes, inside the authenticated app. Render the official embed iframe unmodified on Studio Assistant's own pages, which count as a 'website or webpage controlled by you'. No autoplay, no caching or persisting oEmbed data, no LLM or planner input, no export or third-party transfer, and Spotify attribution with a link back.
(2) Never use the embed in anything public or promotional: no client-facing pages, no website module, no social posts or emails. The Play Button 'commercial purposes' ban and the promotion restriction are undefined, and the Widget text is still the 2014 version.
(3) Show honest UI text: 'Spotify links are kept for your own music reference only. They are not licensed for playing in the shop or in your videos.'
(4) Keep a one-switch fallback to link-only mode (URL + notes, no iframe) and default to it if Spotify publishes stricter Widget/Embed terms.
(5) Studio Assistant's privacy policy and end-user terms page must exist before any embed renders, because the Widget Terms require 'an end user agreement and privacy policy'.
(6) Before go-live, allow developer.spotify.com in the session network settings and re-read /terms, /policy and /documentation/embeds/terms live, recording version and date in docs/research.
account_requirements: Tier 0 (embed or link-only): no Spotify for Developers account, Client ID or Premium needed. Spotify's Embeds docs say using Embeds means accepting the Spotify Developer Terms (v10, 15 May 2025) and, for Widgets, the Widget Terms (v2.0, 27 May 2014). The owner should read both.

Tier 0: Studio Assistant must publish an end-user agreement and privacy policy (a Widget Terms condition). Embeds may only be shown on pages the owner controls, unmodified and not obscured, with Spotify attribution and link-back. Nothing on public, promotional or client-facing surfaces.

Tier 0: no use of Spotify for in-shop playback. The consumer licence is personal and non-commercial, so a commercial background-music service is needed for the salon. The 15 Oct 2026 consumer Terms update concerns dispute resolution and does not change this.

Tier 1 (not recommended): would need an owner Spotify account with active Premium, a Spotify for Developers account, acceptance of Developer Terms v10 and the Policy, a Development Mode Client ID (up to 25 per account, quota pooled), and every user added to the allowlist (maximum 5 per Client ID). Development Mode has no app review, and Extended Quota is closed to individuals and small businesses (organisations only, about 250k MAU).

Tier 1 precondition: written confirmation from Spotify that an internal business tool is allowed, because the official 2026 framing limits Development Mode to non-commercial personal projects. No published request channel exists. The owner would have to contact Spotify via the developer community or support with no guaranteed answer.

Verification: developer.spotify.com is blocked in this sandbox (ENOTFOUND). It must be allowed in the session's network settings to read the live Terms, Policy, Widget Terms and Dashboard before go-live.
uncertainties: No official Spotify page could be fetched (developer.spotify.com ENOTFOUND, web.archive.org and archive.org blocked). All official wording comes from search-engine summaries. The freshest readings of the Terms and Policy headers (Sep and Oct 2026) come from two third-party GitHub research notes, which cannot be independently verified.

That app creation is open in November 2026 is inferred from the official July 2026 Client ID raise, the absence of any later hold notice, and a third-party 16 Oct 2026 recheck. Nobody here viewed the Dashboard. A short-lived pause or regional quirk after October 2026 cannot be ruled out. Flutster issue #2 (7 Nov 2026) still cites the one-Client-ID limit, which conflicts with the July raise to 25.

Why developer.spotify.com/community re-dates the 6 Feb 2026 post to 18 Jun 2026 is unresolved. It could be an unseen edit (one community user claimed an edit 'to include the actual reason'), a co-listing with the 18 Jun refresh-token post, or an index error. The edit history of the post was not available.

A Terms or Policy revision after 15 May 2025 cannot be fully excluded: the official pages were not read live, and the Terms allow silent revision ('the most current version will always be posted on our website'). The Analytify 'V.11/V.12' references are ambiguous, probably clause numbers.

The exact current wording of Terms III.1(a), including whether it says '(i) for private personal use', is quoted only by a third-party note and a search summary of the older developer-terms-of-use URL. It was not verified against the live v10 text.

The current live Widget Terms were not read. Search still shows the 2014 v2.0 text, and a beta-site copy with different numbering may be newer. 'Commercial purposes' is undefined, and it is unclear whether a private internal reference library in a business's own app counts. The 'may not be used to promote a product, service or website' wording comes from a search summary, not verified exact text.

The search budget for this turn ran out before the remaining checks: exact Terms licence clause, live Widget Terms version, and any October or November 2026 Dashboard notices. A follow-up message can continue them.

sources.title: Square's official OpenAPI specification (api.json)
sources.date_note: Downloaded in full this session (3,273,134 bytes, HTTP 200) and grepped locally. x-fern-global-headers sets Square-Version to literal "2026-09-16". This is current API contract text. It has no pricing and no per-country notes for Bookings.

findings.claim: I could not confirm current (November 2026) AU prices for Free, Plus or Premium from an official source this session. The only figures available are Free A$0 (single location), Plus A$40/month per location and Premium A$90/month per location. They come from an earlier search summary of a page the search engine flagged as possibly stale.
findings.evidence: Earlier-session summary of squareup.com/au/en/appointments/pricing: "$0/mo. for a single location" (Free), "$40/mo. per location" (Plus), "$90/mo. per location" (Premium), with a "free 30-day trial" and no contract. The AU FAQ summary says plans are "on a per-location basis". This session, fetching squareup.com failed ("getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND squareup.com") and WebSearch returned "Web search was not performed: this turn's web search budget is used up". US pages show US$49/US$149, which are not AU prices.

findings.claim: The paid-plan gate on seller-level write access is confirmed in Square's current official API contract (API version 2026-09-16), and the plan names are Appointments Plus or Premium. The contract adds no country exception.
findings.evidence: From the official spec downloaded in full this session, the descriptions of CreateBooking, UpdateBooking and CancelBooking each say: "For calls to this endpoint with seller-level permissions to succeed, the seller must have subscribed to *Appointments Plus* or *Appointments Premium*." The same sentence appears on the booking custom-attribute write endpoints: CreateBookingCustomAttributeDefinition, UpdateBookingCustomAttributeDefinition, DeleteBookingCustomAttributeDefinition, UpsertBookingCustomAttribute, DeleteBookingCustomAttribute, BulkUpsertBookingCustomAttributes and BulkDeleteBookingCustomAttributes. Read endpoints such as ListBookings and RetrieveBooking carry no plan sentence.

findings.claim: The AU pricing page (unverified, stale-flagged summary) lists "Bookings API (write access)" and cancellation/no-show fees under Plus. I could not confirm this for November 2026.
findings.evidence: Earlier-session summary of the AU pricing page: Plus adds "customer confirmation texts and emails, cancellation policy and fees, class scheduling, waitlist, and appointments reports" and "Bookings API (write access)", described as "The app can create, update or cancel every booking of a seller. A seller is granted this permission through a paid subscription plan." Premium adds "resource management, custom staff commissions". The API side agrees: the spec exposes BusinessAppointmentSettings.cancellation_fee_money ("The flat-fee amount charged for a no-show booking.") and the cancellation_policy enum value CANCELLATION_TREATED_AS_NO_SHOW ("Cancellations are treated as no shows and may incur a fee as specified by `cancellation_fee_money`."). The spec does not say which plan enables these.

findings.claim: No Free-plan staff limit for AU could be confirmed this session. The 'no employee limit' wording comes only from the same stale-flagged summary.
findings.evidence: Earlier-session summary: Free lists unlimited staff accounts ("There is no employee limit"). There was no official page fetch and no new search this session. I found no other source with an AU Free staff cap.

findings.claim: Square says the Bookings API is limited in international locales but does not list which features are missing in Australia in any source available to this research. Australia was in the 2022 launch set, and an Australian barbershop was using the API in 2026.
findings.evidence: Concepts page (earlier summary): "The Bookings API is limited in international locales. For supported international locales, see Square Appointments FAQs." GA blog (12 May 2022): "developers in the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, Spain, and Japan can access the API". The international availability help article (summary) did not list AU-specific gaps. The official spec has no country- or locale-specific statement on any booking schema or endpoint. The only locale restriction found in the whole spec is unrelated (catalog sort_name: "It is currently supported for sellers of the Japanese locale only."). The AU forum thread (about Sept/Oct 2026) describes API use in Australia, with only the no-show-fee restriction getting in the way.

findings.claim: Some features the owner might expect the app to drive are missing from the Bookings API in every country, not only in Australia: deposits or payments on a booking, sending or suppressing confirmations, setting status (including NO_SHOW), and booking services that carry a no-show fee. A gated UI must not offer these as app actions at all.
findings.evidence: Spec Booking properties are exactly: id, version, status, created_at, updated_at, start_at, location_id, customer_id, customer_note, seller_note, appointment_segments, transition_time_minutes, all_day, location_type, creator_details, source, address. None covers deposits, payments or confirmation or notification control. Booking.status is readOnly in the spec. BusinessBookingProfile fields are booking_enabled, customer_timezone_choice, booking_policy, allow_user_cancel, business_appointment_settings and support_seller_level_writes. An earlier-session docs summary says: "You cannot use the Bookings API to book a service that has a non-zero cancellation fee set on its no_show_fee attribute. The non-zero cancellation fee is set in the Square Dashboard. It cannot be set using the Bookings API." Changelog 2024-04-17: "Disallows updates of a booking's appointment segments after a deposit is made for the booking." The Aug 2026 forum lists open gaps: "customer confirmations, personal events, schedule changes, recurring appointments".

findings.claim: Whether the connected seller's plan allows writes can be checked at runtime regardless of country, so the app does not need to rely on price or plan claims.
findings.evidence: Spec BusinessBookingProfile.support_seller_level_writes: "Indicates whether the seller's subscription to Square Appointments supports creating, updating or canceling an appointment through the API (`true`) or not (`false`) using seller permission." Concepts page (earlier summary): without Plus or Premium, "API calls targeted at the seller with seller-level writeable permissions fail with a 403 response."

findings.claim: No Bookings API change in 2025-2026 was found. The plan gate is unchanged in the 2026-09-16 spec. Whether AU prices changed in 2025-2026 is unknown.
findings.evidence: Aug 2026 forum: "the last Bookings API update in the Square API changelog was September 2024", and Square staff are "continuing development on the Bookings API". The spec downloaded this session (Square-Version 2026-09-16) still has the Plus/Premium sentence on the write endpoints. No AU pricing history could be retrieved.

implementation_decision: Do not hard-code or claim any Square price, staff limit or plan feature list in Studio Assistant's UI or copy until someone has checked them on the live AU page. (1) Keep plan facts in one config record ({planName, audPerLocationMonthly, includesApiWrites, noShowFees, verifiedAt, verifiedBy}) with prices null by default. Until the owner or a developer has checked https://squareup.com/au/en/appointments/pricing (or Square Dashboard > Account & Settings > Subscriptions) and filled it in, the Square settings screen says only: "Creating, rescheduling and cancelling bookings from Studio Assistant needs a paid Square Appointments plan (Plus or Premium). Check current Australian pricing in your Square Dashboard." Never show the A$40/A$90 figures or "unlimited staff on Free" as fact. (2) Decide write capability only at runtime. After connecting, call RetrieveBusinessBookingProfile and enable Create, Reschedule and Cancel only when support_seller_level_writes === true. Treat any 403 from a write as authoritative: switch to read-only and show the plan message, whatever the country or plan the owner thinks they have. Gate booking custom-attribute writes the same way, since they carry the same Plus/Premium sentence. (3) Because Square does not list what is missing in Australia, check each write feature on first use. Before the module is marked "Connected", run a one-off self-test on the owner's real AU account during their Plus trial: create a booking for a fee-free test service, then update it, then cancel it. Record pass or fail for each action, and show failed actions as "Not available on your Square account" rather than hiding the failure. (4) Never offer these as app actions in any tier, because the API cannot do them anywhere: taking or attaching deposits, sending or suppressing customer confirmations or reminders, marking a booking NO_SHOW or changing its status, and booking services that carry a no-show or cancellation fee. For each, show a deep link labelled "Do this in Square Appointments". Show the seller's cancellation_fee_money and cancellation_policy read-only, with the source labelled. (5) Tier 0 (reads plus webhooks) stays usable on any plan, and its copy makes no claims about prices or staff limits. (6) Mark this research item as needing re-verification: before telling the owner what to buy, re-run it with squareup.com and developer.squareup.com allowed in the session's network settings and a fresh web-search budget.
account_requirements: A Square seller account registered in Australia, with Square Appointments activated for the Ivanhoe location (pricing is per location).

To create, update or cancel bookings and write booking custom attributes from Studio Assistant: an active or trial Square Appointments Plus or Premium subscription. This is the official API contract (spec version 2026-09-16). The current AUD price must be confirmed by the owner on the live AU pricing page or in Square Dashboard before buying. The A$40/A$90 figures are unverified.

Before paying, the owner starts the free trial (the 30-day figure is unverified) and confirms that RetrieveBusinessBookingProfile returns support_seller_level_writes = true and that the Studio Assistant self-test (create, update and cancel a fee-free test booking) passes on the AU account.

The owner checks the current Free-plan staff allowance and which plan includes no-show or cancellation fees, deposits and confirmation texts, all on the live AU page. None of these could be verified this session.

Services the app will book must have no no-show or cancellation fee set in Square Dashboard, or the owner keeps fee-free variations for bookings made through the app. Fee-bearing services must be booked in Square's own channels.
Deposits, confirmations and reminders, and marking no-shows stay in Square Appointments itself. The owner must be told the app cannot do these.

Square Developer account and an application with OAuth scopes APPOINTMENTS_READ and APPOINTMENTS_ALL_READ, plus APPOINTMENTS_WRITE and APPOINTMENTS_ALL_WRITE for writes, and APPOINTMENTS_BUSINESS_SETTINGS_READ for the business booking profile. Using a single-seller private app with no Marketplace review follows standard practice but was not re-verified.

For future re-verification sessions: squareup.com and developer.squareup.com must be allowed in the session's network settings, and the web-search budget (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_WEB_SEARCHES_PER_SESSION) must not be used up.
uncertainties: I could not get the current (Nov 2026) AU prices for Free, Plus and Premium. squareup.com and developer.squareup.com failed with ENOTFOUND (not allowed in this sandbox), and the shared WebSearch budget for this turn was used up, so no new search was possible. The A$0/A$40/A$90 figures come only from an earlier session's search summary of a page flagged as possibly stale. The user can send a follow-up message to continue the search, or allow those hosts.

I could not confirm whether AU Plus currently includes 'Bookings API (write access)' and no-show or cancellation fees. That wording is from the same stale summary. The API-side plan gate (Plus or Premium) is confirmed in the 2026-09-16 spec, but the spec does not map features to plans or prices.
The AU Free-plan staff limit is unknown. 'There is no employee limit' is unverified, and I did not assume a number.

The Australia-specific gaps behind 'limited in international locales' are unknown. No source enumerates them, the official spec has no per-country Bookings notes, and the referenced Square Appointments FAQ could not be read. Deposits, confirmation control, status changes and booking no-show-fee services are missing from the API globally, not as an AU-specific gap.
Whether AU prices or plan names changed in 2025-2026 could not be checked. No Bookings API changes after September 2024 were found, and the plan gate text is unchanged in the 2026-09-16 spec.
Whether a sandbox test account can be created as an Australian seller to test AU behaviour before the owner pays was not verified.
